facts.value: Singapore: local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT SGD 20–35 per transfer, SHA/OUR.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Hong Kong: local transfers to 120+ countries free; SWIFT HKD 120–200 per transfer, SHA/OUR.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No single numeric withdrawal/settlement minimum established; regional bank payout matrices could not be verified.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: PayNow dynamic QR: minimum SGD 0.50; maximum SGD 200,000 subject to the shopper's internet-banking limit.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: SEPA Direct Debit: minimum EUR 1; maximum EUR 100,000 subject to risk approval.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: A universal card-transaction ceiling or unverified-account collection allowance is not published.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Visa/Mastercard merchant locations: AU, CH, EEA, HK, MY, SG, NZ, UK, US; CA, IL, JP, MX marked Beta.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: US: LLC/corporation, partnership/other entities and registered or unregistered sole proprietorships.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: UK: limited company, LLP, limited/general partnership and sole trader.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: EEA: private limited company, limited/general partnership and sole trader.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Hong Kong: limited company, sole proprietorship or partnership.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: AU/NZ guides cover companies, partnerships, trusts and other entities; Singapore company/partnership documents are published. Exact sole-trader coverage in these guides is incomplete.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: US business presence and owner rules differ from a US bank address.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Settlement needs an Airwallex business wallet; universal external-bank/local-owner-residency prerequisites are not published.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Business/owner verification plus a Payments-specific website and business review.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Public online signup, business verification, then request Payments and individual method activation.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: No universal minimum sales volume, revenue or business age found for ordinary Payments.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Software/SaaS, e-commerce goods and professional services are marketed; approval remains conditional.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: US/UK/AU: AI/generative AI, dropshipping, marketplaces, crowdfunding/financial services and several delayed-delivery models require approval; adult content, counterfeit goods, unlicensed finance and other listed activities are prohibited.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Cards reach global shoppers except sanctioned countries; local methods impose their own shopper-country rules.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Reserves and settlement deferral are account-specific; Australian terms permit holding a reserve for 180 days or longer if reasonably required.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: Business-account processing estimate 1–3 business days after all required information; manual Payments review typically 1–2 business days.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Gateway, processor and acquirer; for standard Payments you remain the legal seller. Optional Merchant of Record is excluded from base pricing.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: 130+ charge currencies, with method and merchant-location exceptions; examples AUD, CAD, CHF, CNY, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NZD, SGD, USD.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: US Visa/Mastercard use the card page's explicit currency list; US Amex, JCB, UnionPay, Discover and Diners Club process USD only.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Major cards plus Apple Pay and Google Pay; brand availability differs by seller market.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: ACH USD, SEPA EUR, PayNow SGD and multi-currency bank transfers; wallets and BNPL also depend on location.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Yes: single payments, one-time invoices and one-time/reusable links.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Automatic card/off-session charging through stored PaymentConsent credentials and Billing subscriptions.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: ACH supports one-off and recurring debits; SEPA is designed for recurring debit collection.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Billing supports flat, seat/per-unit, tiered, package and usage pricing; trials, coupons, mixed frequencies, prorated plan changes and automatic payment recovery.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Hosted Payment Page, embedded/drop-in components, Native API/mobile integrations, plus no-code payment links and QR codes.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: API/SDKs, signed webhooks, sandbox/test cards; official Shopify, SHOPLINE, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop and Salesforce Commerce Cloud plugins.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Standard Payments seller determines tax obligations, registers, files and remits; optional Tax automates calculation, not those legal duties.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Billing supports one-time/recurring commercial invoices, digital invoice payment, coupons, custom/automatic tax and credit notes.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Funds settle into the Airwallex wallet, then may be sent by supported local or SWIFT bank transfer.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: AU/SG/HK Visa/Mastercard like-for-like currencies: AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, HKD, JPY, NZD, SGD, THB, USD.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: UK/EEA Visa/Mastercard like-for-like: AED, AUD, CAD, CHF, CZK, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, HUF, JPY, NOK, NZD, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, TRY, USD, ZAR.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: US Visa/Mastercard like-for-like: USD, EUR, GBP, SGD, AUD, CAD, HKD, NOK, SEK, CHF, NZD, JPY, DKK, MXN.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: US cards: normally one business day after capture, subject to final onboarding/reserve terms.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Australia cards: normally two business days after capture, subject to final onboarding/reserve terms.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: UK/EEA/SG/HK cards: normally three business days after capture, subject to onboarding/reserves.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: After an outbound transfer is initiated, most bank routes arrive in 0–3 business days.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: No native file hosting, automatic software-licence issuance or universal membership entitlement engine established.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Conditional: Payments for Platforms supports connected accounts, split proceeds and platform fees.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Documented crypto-related route is an Early access outbound payout: USDC on Ethereum, funded/reported in USD.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Beneficiary Ethereum address is supplied; custody/private-key control during conversion is not described.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: USD-denominated transfer to a configured USDC/Ethereum beneficiary; exact fees and eligible seller countries require enablement.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Outbound USDC completion: four Ethereum block confirmations, described as minutes; wrong-address/network transfers can be irreversible.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Hosted Airwallex API service; the merchant builds/runs the client integration.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Payment activity, settlement, fee, reconciliation and balance-activity exports; tax CSV exports; inbound stored-card migration.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: No general public outbound stored-card/subscription migration procedure or completeness guarantee found.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Plan cancellation and full account closure are separate; AU/UK Payments contracts specify two months' merchant notice for ordinary termination.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Personal data can remain after closure or a deletion request for legal, AML, fraud, accounting, dispute and contractual reasons.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Airwallex Payments, the Airwallex group's payment-acceptance product; official URL /global/payments.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Help Centre, email support and authenticated WebApp Kai/chat escalation; higher-tier account management is listed.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Universal human-support hours, full language coverage and guaranteed response times were not found.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Active public Payments offer with live pricing/docs; several methods/countries remain Beta or Early access.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: UK contract: Airwallex (UK) Limited, FCA-authorised electronic money institution, firm reference 900876; merchant PCI duties depend on integration.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Airwallex acquired South Korean payment company Paynuri on 21 January 2026 and financial automation company Leapfin on 4 June 2026.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: AUSTRAC ordered an external audit of Airwallex’s AML/CTF program on 22 January 2026 after identifying suspected compliance failures.

apps.name: Amazon Pay
apps.line: Let shoppers pay with payment details saved in their Amazon account.

free.text: No setup or monthly fee listed for US accounts

cells.countries: US, UK, Europe, Japan and India
cells.payout: US next schedule; EU daily; Japan every 14 days

fee.math: The rate for a US card charge made on the web or in a mobile app.
The UK rate for sellers taking under GBP 50,000 a month in payments.
The Germany rate for sellers who take under EUR 50,000 a month in payments on average.
In India, prices are agreed directly with Amazon. No standard rate is published.

facts.label: Other required accounts
facts.value: Standard checkout requires an Amazon Payments merchant account and the merchant’s own website or supported commerce platform; no separate card acquirer is listed as a standard dependency.

facts.label: US setup/monthly costs
facts.value: No setup or monthly fee is listed on the standard US public fee schedule.

facts.label: UK/EU setup/monthly costs
facts.value: The EU/UK public schedule lists transaction fees and no general setup or monthly account charge.

facts.label: Japan setup/monthly costs
facts.value: Japan: setup fee ¥0, monthly fee ¥0, transaction fee ¥0 as a separate fixed transaction charge, and bank-transfer fee ¥0.

facts.label: India pricing availability
facts.value: Direct India merchant commercials are discussed with Amazon Pay; no standard public fee card was found in the official onboarding docs.

facts.label: US international card processing
facts.value: US account payment from a method issued outside the US is charged 3.9% plus USD 0.30 authorization fee.

facts.label: UK/EU cross-border fee
facts.value: EU fee schedule describes cross-border fees from 0% to 3.3% by issuer country group, and separately shows another table from 0.4% to 1.5%.

facts.label: EU/UK currency conversion
facts.value: If a transaction requires conversion to ledger currency, Amazon applies a 0.5% spread above its bank service provider’s wholesale exchange rate, embedded in the conversion rate.

facts.label: Japan and India currency conversion
facts.value: No separate public standard FX spread was found for Japanese or India merchant accounts in the local fee/onboarding pages checked.

facts.label: EU Monthly Invoice method
facts.value: Optional Monthly Invoice transactions use a 2.45% processing fee plus EUR 0.35 authorization fee instead of the standard processing fee.

facts.label: Japan local-method fee differences
facts.value: Japan publishes a single physical/service and digital-content processing rate; no separate fee schedule by card, gift card, Paidy, points, or Merpay was found.

facts.label: Recurring-payment surcharge
facts.value: No separate recurring or subscription surcharge is listed on the public US, EU/UK, or Japan fee schedules.

facts.label: Tax calculation and collection add-on
facts.value: Amazon Pay charges the amount submitted by the merchant; the merchant must include any sales tax or VAT in that amount. No bundled tax calculation/remittance service was found for this gateway offer.

facts.label: Refund transaction fees
facts.value: For US/EU accounts, the processing fee and any cross-border fee are refunded when the transaction is refunded; authorization and chargeback dispute fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: Refund method and limits
facts.value: Merchants can make full or partial refunds through Seller Central or Refund API after capture. EU docs cap the refund at 15% above the charge or GBP 75, whichever is lower, and allow up to 10 refunds per charge.

facts.label: Japan refund handling
facts.value: Japan merchants can issue full or partial refunds to a previously captured payment through Refund API; Amazon sends the buyer a refund confirmation.

facts.label: US chargeback handling and fee
facts.value: Amazon handles communication with the card network when the merchant asks it to contest a chargeback; the US fee is USD 20 plus tax where applicable unless the transaction qualifies for Payment Protection.

facts.label: US Payment Protection
facts.value: A qualifying unauthorized chargeback on physical goods may be protected if the seller meets account/policy conditions and submits requested evidence, including proof of delivery to the Amazon-provided address, on time.

facts.label: EU/UK dispute fee
facts.value: EU/UK fee page lists EUR 20 for EU or GBP 14 for UK, excluding VAT, for a chargeback dispute not covered by Payment Protection; non-VAT-registered EU sellers are charged VAT on this fee.

facts.label: Japan chargeback liability
facts.value: Japan help says qualifying unauthorized-payment cases may be protected under its payment guarantee policy; service chargebacks can still be the merchant’s responsibility.

facts.label: A-to-z guarantee scope
facts.value: Amazon Pay A-to-z is for eligible physical goods bought on third-party websites; it covers non-delivery/late delivery, materially different or defective goods, return/refund failures, and overcharges. It excludes services, digital goods, stored value, and other listed cases.

facts.label: A-to-z merchant response and debit
facts.value: EU merchants have 7 calendar days to respond. If they do not respond or are found responsible, Amazon can refund the buyer and debit the merchant; repeated claims can trigger warnings, suspension, termination, and higher reserves.

facts.label: A-to-z buyer cap: UK/EU
facts.value: UK buyer policy caps A-to-z reimbursement at GBP 2,000; the localized European policy’s cap is shown in account currency and varies by regional page.

facts.label: US payout fee
facts.value: No standard US bank disbursement fee is listed on the public fee schedule or Getting Paid help page.

facts.label: Japan payout fee
facts.value: Japan lists bank transfer fee as free, regardless of payment cycle.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: A general minimum payout amount was not found in the standard payout and settlement pages checked.

facts.label: Transaction amount limits
facts.value: A complete current public transaction minimum/maximum by country and method was not found in merchant FAQs, pricing, and integration overview pages.

facts.label: Standard seller countries: US
facts.value: Businesses established in the United States can register for the standard Amazon Pay merchant account.

facts.label: Standard seller countries: UK and Europe
facts.value: The standard regional account is available to sellers established in the UK, Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, or Switzerland.

facts.label: Standard seller country: Japan
facts.value: Japan-based merchants can apply for the Japanese Amazon Pay merchant product.

facts.label: India local seller route
facts.value: Amazon provides India-specific online merchant documentation, onboarding through Amazon Pay or listed payment aggregators, and Amazon Pay Balance/Later integration options.

facts.label: Other standard seller countries
facts.value: Outside the standard US, UK/Europe, and Japan lists, the standard Amazon Payments merchant FAQ does not offer a general signup route.

facts.label: US individual and sole-proprietor form
facts.value: US sole proprietors and single-member LLCs may provide an SSN for the US tax interview; other businesses generally provide an EIN.

facts.label: EU/UK individual registration
facts.value: The EU/UK agreement permits the applicant to contract as an individual or through the business employing the applicant.

facts.label: Japan legal form
facts.value: Japan’s merchant eligibility page requires a corporation based in Japan; individuals and sole traders are not eligible for this direct merchant offer.

facts.label: India legal forms
facts.value: The India onboarding docs require a GST certificate and business bank proof but do not state a complete eligible legal-form list.

facts.label: US local presence and bank
facts.value: US merchants need a US business presence, US phone number, US bank-issued credit card, US checking account/routing details, and US tax ID or SSN.

facts.label: UK and EU bank requirements
facts.value: UK account payouts are in GBP to a UK GBP-denominated bank account. EUR-account merchants may receive EUR to a bank in the listed EEA/European jurisdictions, Switzerland, or the UK.

facts.label: Japan local bank
facts.value: Japanese merchants need a Japanese bank account; Amazon’s Japanese FAQ says payments go to an account based in Japan.

facts.label: India local requirements
facts.value: India merchant docs ask for a GST certificate and a cancelled cheque or bank letter showing account details and IFSC.

facts.label: Standard verification
facts.value: Amazon collects personal and business information, requires proof of identity, and can request documents for both personal and business identity plus bank/card data.

facts.label: Business/site review
facts.value: Amazon reviews the seller’s business, website URLs, product and policies against its acceptable-use rules; further documents may be requested during or after registration.

facts.label: US tax verification
facts.value: US merchants complete an online tax interview; the result is a W-9 using EIN or SSN as applicable. Non-US applicants generate W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E and are directed to register in their home region instead of the US.

facts.label: India verification
facts.value: The India direct route requires KYC with Amazon’s point of contact after sharing GST and bank documents; the docs do not publish the full KYC checklist.

facts.label: Standard signup route
facts.value: Merchants can register online, enter business/site details, complete verification, and then activate the production account; the registration flow first grants test-environment access.

facts.label: India signup route
facts.value: India direct merchants contact Amazon Pay to discuss commercial terms, complete KYC, then select API/SDK integration; aggregators are also listed as routes.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No general minimum revenue, monthly sales, or transaction count for standard merchant signup is stated in the registration, fee, or merchant FAQ pages checked.

facts.label: Physical goods
facts.value: Physical product sales are supported, subject to the seller agreement, website review, and prohibited-product rules.

facts.label: Digital goods and services
facts.value: Digital goods, services, preorders, and micropayments can be processed under the standard merchant FAQ; the standard fee card applies to micropayments.

facts.label: Subscriptions
facts.value: Amazon Pay supports recurring transactions and automatic payments, including fixed or variable amounts and repeated billing.

facts.label: Prohibited and restricted categories
facts.value: Prohibitions include adult content, crowdfunding, money services and third-party payment processing, gambling, weapons, illegal goods, cryptocurrency, tobacco, and several regulated/high-risk products and services.

facts.label: Compliance enforcement
facts.value: Amazon may block transactions, hold related funds, restrict use, suspend or terminate accounts if it suspects a policy breach.

facts.label: Buyer country coverage
facts.value: Amazon Pay describes buyers using their existing Amazon accounts internationally, but does not publish a single complete allowlist of buyer countries across all seller accounts and methods.

facts.label: EEA/UK SEPA buyer access
facts.value: The EU/UK merchant FAQ lists SEPA buyers for EUR payments in the EEA and associated jurisdictions; card availability can be narrowed to Visa and Mastercard in some cases.

facts.label: Restricted buyer activity
facts.value: Buyer transactions linked to prohibited activity, sanctioned goods, or restricted categories can be blocked under the Acceptable Use Policy.

facts.label: US reserve policy
facts.value: New US accounts enter Tier I: the greater of unresolved dispute value or trailing 7 days of sales is held. After six months and more than 100 completed orders, a Tier II reserve may use the greater of unresolved disputes or order-defect-rate times trailing 30-day sales.

facts.label: EU/UK reserve policy
facts.value: Standard reserve tiers begin with 100% of the prior 7 days’ sales or unresolved disputes, then may move to 3% of average daily processed payments over 28 days or unresolved disputes after 3 months and 100 orders. Tier II-Plus may reduce holds to unresolved claims if ODR remains below 1%.

facts.label: Reserve triggers
facts.value: Amazon can set account, performance, or dispute reserves based on sales history, refunds/claims, business type, presales, delivery windows, and creditworthiness.

facts.label: Approval-time estimate
facts.value: EU verification can take up to 7 business days when information is accurate; Japan’s public merchant contact page says review typically takes just under a week.

facts.label: Provider type and seller role
facts.value: Payment gateway / digital wallet checkout. The merchant sells its own goods or services and Amazon Pay processes the payment.

facts.label: Merchant-of-record status
facts.value: Amazon Pay does not take over the merchant’s sale, fulfillment, returns, or tax obligations under the standard checkout agreement.

facts.label: Shopify Payments edition
facts.value: On Shopify’s US-only Amazon Pay with Shopify Payments offer, Shopify Payments processes and pays out the transaction under the seller’s Shopify agreement; Amazon Pay’s standard fee schedule does not apply.

facts.label: US charge currency
facts.value: US standard merchant account charges buyers in USD.

facts.label: UK and EU charge currencies
facts.value: UK accounts charge GBP and EU regional accounts charge EUR by default.

facts.label: EU multi-currency
facts.value: European accounts can enable customer presentment in AUD, GBP, DKK, EUR, HKD, JPY, NZD, NOK, ZAR, SEK, CHF, or USD; Amazon converts funds to the merchant ledger currency.

facts.label: Japan charge currency
facts.value: Japan merchant checkout charges in JPY.

facts.label: India charge currency
facts.value: India merchant documentation describes the local Amazon Pay Balance/Later integrations; a complete public charge-currency list was not found in those integration pages.

facts.label: US card methods
facts.value: US buyers can pay with Visa, Mastercard, Discover, American Express, Diners Club, and JCB credit cards, plus Visa/Mastercard debit cards.

facts.label: UK/EU card methods
facts.value: UK/EU buyers can use Visa, Mastercard, and American Express credit cards and Visa Electron, Delta, and Maestro debit cards; some cases permit only Visa or Mastercard credit.

facts.label: UK/EU SEPA direct debit
facts.value: SEPA direct debit is supported for eligible EUR buyers with a valid SEPA bank account, subject to account and checkout conditions.

facts.label: Japan payment methods
facts.value: Japanese buyers can use Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Diners Club, eligible debit/prepaid cards, Amazon Gift Card balance, Paidy, JCB partner points, and Merpay; availability can vary by merchant.

facts.label: India payment methods
facts.value: India integration docs list Amazon Pay Balance and Amazon Pay Later, through direct or aggregator integrations.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Single authorization and capture payments are supported.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Merchants can set up automatic recurring charges against a buyer-authorized merchant agreement.

facts.label: Recurring payment method limitation
facts.value: US merchant agreement help says only credit cards can be used for a recurring payment authorization; debit cards are not accepted for this flow.

facts.label: Subscription billing features
facts.value: Amazon Pay can authorize fixed or variable recurring amounts, but does not publish a complete subscription billing suite covering plan catalogs, trials, proration, usage metering, or dunning.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Website and mobile checkout are supported through Amazon Pay buttons and integrations; hosted checkout v2 brings address, payment, and consent confirmation into a consolidated flow.

facts.label: Payment links
facts.value: A general merchant payment-link product for sending arbitrary checkout URLs was not found in Amazon Pay checkout pages or integration docs.

facts.label: API and SDK
facts.value: Amazon publishes API integration guides, SDKs, code samples, and checkout v2 developer resources.

facts.label: Events and notifications
facts.value: Amazon supports Instant Payment Notifications (IPNs) for transaction, refund, recurring permission, and dispute status changes.

facts.label: Test mode
facts.value: Amazon offers Sandbox testing before live account activation; Seller Central can configure notification endpoints for Sandbox and Production.

facts.label: Ecommerce integrations
facts.value: Amazon’s merchant registration and integration pages link to ecommerce plugins and partner integrations; the exact plugin set varies by region and version.

facts.label: Sales tax responsibility
facts.value: The merchant sets the price and submits the total including any VAT, GST, or sales tax. Amazon Pay charges exactly the submitted amount; tax calculation, registration, filing, and remittance remain the merchant’s responsibility unless handled separately.

facts.label: Provider-fee VAT registration
facts.value: EU merchants can submit a VAT number so Amazon determines VAT treatment on Amazon Pay fees; invalid VAT registration can result in unbilled VAT being charged later.

facts.label: Receipts and invoices
facts.value: Amazon sends transaction/refund emails to buyers and exposes transaction records in Seller Central; a complete tax-invoice generation feature for the merchant’s underlying sale was not found.

facts.label: Payout method: US
facts.value: US standard accounts receive bank disbursement to a linked US checking account by ACH.

facts.label: Payout method: UK/EU
facts.value: UK and EU standard accounts receive payout to an eligible bank account in the supported ledger currency; the merchant FAQ lists GBP and EUR bank corridors.

facts.label: Payout method: Japan
facts.value: Japanese merchants receive settlement by bank transfer to a Japan-based ordinary or checking account.

facts.label: India payout method
facts.value: India docs require merchant bank information and a cancelled cheque/bank letter; public docs do not provide a complete payout-method matrix across direct and aggregator routes.

facts.label: US payout currency
facts.value: US standard merchant account settles in USD.

facts.label: UK/EU payout currencies
facts.value: UK account pays GBP; EU regional accounts pay EUR. Multi-currency charge receipts are converted into the ledger currency before disbursement.

facts.label: Japan payout currency
facts.value: Japan merchant account pays in JPY.

facts.label: US settlement schedule
facts.value: US settlement occurs after the account’s 24-hour settlement window closes; Amazon initiates bank transfer on the next scheduled settlement date.

facts.label: US bank arrival time
facts.value: US Getting Paid page says ACH usually takes 3–5 business days after settlement starts; another Amazon welcome FAQ says 1–2 business days.

facts.label: EU/UK payout timing
facts.value: Regional merchant FAQ says disbursements are processed daily and usually appear in 1–2 business days, subject to reserves.

facts.label: Japan payout timing
facts.value: Japan normally makes the first settlement 14 days after account registration; later settlements run every 14 days, with bank arrival usually 3–5 business days after settlement.

facts.label: Bank-account-change hold
facts.value: Adding or changing payout-bank details triggers a 3-day disbursement hold.

facts.label: Digital fulfillment
facts.value: Amazon Pay can process digital-good transactions, but merchant delivery/access control remains the merchant’s responsibility; no hosted digital-file delivery is included in the gateway docs checked.

facts.label: Marketplace/split payments
facts.value: Marketplace processing third-party payments requires prior Amazon approval; a general self-serve split-payment or multi-seller marketplace feature was not found.

facts.label: Transaction exports
facts.value: Seller Central provides downloadable settlement and transaction reports for reconciliation and tax reporting.

facts.label: Payment-data portability
facts.value: A public customer/payment-token migration path to another processor was not found in merchant reporting or integration documents checked.

facts.label: Closing a merchant account
facts.value: Amazon says the merchant should disable the button, settle refunds and open disputes, download reports, have no transactions in the prior 90 days, and reach a zero balance before closure.

facts.label: Ongoing account fee and remaining funds
facts.value: Amazon says there is no ongoing fee just to keep a standard account open; payout/closure requires resolving debts, claims, refunds, and reserves.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: Amazon Pay is Amazon’s merchant checkout service for accepting payments on third-party websites and apps using payment and address details saved in an Amazon account.

facts.label: Owner and contracting entities
facts.value: Amazon Pay is an Amazon business. The standard US merchant account contracts with Amazon Payments, Inc.; EU accounts with Amazon Payments Europe S.C.A.; and UK accounts with Amazon Payments UK Limited. The Japanese and India merchant pages checked do not clearly identify their contracting legal entity.

facts.label: Former product names
facts.value: Amazon Pay was previously branded Checkout by Amazon in the US and launched under the Amazon Pay name in Japan in 2015.

facts.label: Current operating status
facts.value: The product and merchant registration/help pages are live, and the official FAQ still lists current checkout methods, pricing, payout, and account closure instructions.

facts.label: Full-market shutdown notice
facts.value: No Amazon notice closing the full third-party merchant checkout service in a country was found in the official Amazon Pay business blog, regional product/help pages, or Amazon newsroom search. Japan did retire Amazon Pay for national tax bill payments on 2026-01-03.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Amazon Pay offers online merchant support and Seller Central support; Japanese merchant inquiries include pre-sales contact and phone support for enrolled merchants.

facts.label: Support hours and languages
facts.value: No complete public support-hours and language matrix covering US, EU/UK, Japan, and India was found.

facts.label: Checkout v1 sunset
facts.value: Amazon’s EU Checkout v2 page says Checkout v1 would be discontinued on 2026-03-31; a separate official help page says v1 remains supported throughout 2026.

facts.label: Shopify product change
facts.value: Shopify says its Amazon Pay third-party integration stopped being supported on 2025-01-06. Amazon Pay with Shopify Payments is the replacement for eligible US/USD sellers.

facts.label: Japan national tax payment sunset
facts.value: Amazon Pay stopped being available for national tax payments in Japan on 2026-01-03.

facts.label: Country shutdown or acquisition
facts.value: Official Amazon Pay blog/newsroom and current merchant pages disclosed no full country shutdown or acquisition notice for this merchant checkout service.

facts.label: Legal entity and jurisdiction
facts.value: Standard contracts identify Amazon Payments, Inc. (US), Amazon Payments Europe S.C.A. (EU), and Amazon Payments UK Limited (UK).

facts.label: Licence/security scope
facts.value: Amazon Pay publishes US money-transmitter licenses for Amazon Payments, Inc. and states it follows PCI DSS when handling card data; the public pages checked do not establish one licence or certification scope for every regional entity and product.

facts.value: Peru minimum payout balance or minimum bank transfer was not published.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: Colombia payment links accept COP 1,000 to COP 10,000,000 per transaction for cards, PSE, Bancolombia, Nequi and QR Bre-B.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: Bold's general contact page states sales from COP 1,000 to COP 30,000,000; the online link guide gives a COP 10,000,000 cap for the named online methods.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: Peru payment links allow up to PEN 20,000; a seller can ask Bold to assess a higher case-specific limit.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: Bold may set separate transaction and period-volume limits by merchant; no complete API/account limit table was published for either country.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Colombia: merchant must be domiciled in Colombia.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Peru: the local offer is for a merchant registered as a natural person with a business or as a legal entity, with valid RUC or DNI; the contract is governed as a Peru offer.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: The current public pages establish Colombia and Peru seller offers; signup from another country was not published.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Colombia: terms cover a natural person's own commercial activity and merchants registered personally or through a legal representative; persons and companies are eligible in principle.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Peru: the agreement explicitly defines merchant as a natural person with a business or a legal entity.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: A complete public list of accepted legal forms by region, including foreign-owned company structures, was not published.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Colombia sellers must be domiciled in Colombia and connect a deposit account for settlement; the Cuenta Bold wallet/account is a separate Bold CF product.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Peru merchants register a local bank account for settlement. A Cuenta Bold or POS is not required to make a payment link.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Rules for settling to a foreign bank account were not published for either offer.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Colombia onboarding is subject to identity and risk review; Bold can request merchant and beneficial-owner information and supporting documents.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Peru onboarding requires identity, beneficial-owner and business information; Bold may request additional documents for AML/risk checks, with a five-business-day response period when requested.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: A universal website checklist or review time for online-only sellers was not published.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Colombia merchants can register online; the online API is an application available to a registered Bold merchant with the payments product active.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Peru link payments are self-serve through the Bold app; the seller does not need a website, technical skill or POS device to create a link.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: The Peru tariff page invites sellers processing over S/ 20,000 monthly to request a rate review; Bold says merchants processing above S/ 50,000 can contact sales for a custom offer.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: A minimum sales volume, setup fee or annual commitment for standard online access was not published.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Colombia's terms permit lawful goods and services subject to the restricted-activity schedule; software and platform subscriptions are prohibited when sold without the rights holder's authorization.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Peru permits lawful commercial products/services and offers online links; a public product-by-product approval matrix for SaaS, digital downloads, memberships or courses was not published.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Colombia's current prohibited list bars sex shops, unauthorized software/platform subscriptions, gaming/streaming account resale, illegal drugs, virtual-asset trading, gambling, unlicensed lending, prostitution and other listed high-risk activities.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Peru merchants must sell the goods/services declared during affiliation and comply with local law, sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls; Bold may restrict risky or unreported activity.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Colombia's API agreement requires PCI DSS compliance from merchants who capture, process, transmit or store card data; some implementations require Bold's integration certification.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Colombia: foreign-issued cards are accepted on enabled channels, but Bold can restrict use outside Colombia or by merchant activity; payment links can be shared to buyers abroad.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Peru: payment links can be sent worldwide and foreign-issued cards are supported, subject to product, acquirer and risk rules.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: A complete buyer-country and sanctioned-country matrix by method was not published for either country.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Colombia terms permit full balance holds for an initial 180 days after a dispute or suspected fraud; the payment network can extend the period.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Peru terms permit full balance holds for up to 180 days for dispute/fraud review, with possible extension by the payment network.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: A general identity, website or API certification approval deadline was not published.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Colombia: payment acceptance gateway/aggregator and payment-link, button, QR and API tools. The merchant sells to the buyer; Bold processes, collects as agent and transfers the money.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Peru: acquiring/payment acceptance, links, QR and POS. Bold collects as the merchant's agent and is not the seller of the merchant's goods or services.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Colombia payment links can be set up in COP or USD; USD display does not mean USD payout, as sales settle in COP at Bold's applicable exchange rate.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Peru supports PEN settlement and says foreign-issued cards may settle in PEN or a currency enabled for the issuer.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Other charge currencies, apart from COP/USD links in Colombia and the stated Peru settlement rules, were not listed in a full public currency matrix.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Colombia online checkout supports Visa/Mastercard and other enabled card networks, PSE, Bancolombia payment button, Nequi/digital wallets and QR Online/Bre-B, depending on channel and buyer setup.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Peru online links accept cards, Yape, Plin, QR and other enabled digital wallets; Amex and Diners are available for link payments, not every POS method.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Cash, crypto and bank-debit methods beyond the named local methods were not found in the current online method lists.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time sales are supported through links, buttons and API payments in Colombia and Peru.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Colombia's online API can be called by an external billing system to make recurring charges, but the public product does not provide a standalone subscription engine; the merchant's system must handle schedules and tokenization.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Peru's public link product does not document automatic subscription renewals or recurring payment methods.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Bold does not document native plan catalog, usage billing, proration, trials, dunning or subscription recovery. Colombia merchants must manage subscription logic through their own system and API calls.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Peru's link guide supports a fixed-price reusable link or personalized one-use link with expiry and a configured number of payments; it does not document recurring billing.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Colombia: hosted payment link and hosted checkout/button; merchants can use the API for a custom web/app payment experience.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Peru: payment links are created in the Bold app; sellers may add product image, description, expiry and payment-count controls.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: A custom domain for hosted checkout was not published.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Colombia offers a REST API, payment button, payment-link API and plugins for WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Jumpseller, Sumer and Tiendanube. A separate official integration page also names Shopify.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Colombia has test keys and a simulated payment environment; test webhook delivery is triggered manually from the test checkout.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Webhooks report payment events; up to five endpoints can be registered, with some link/button events taking up to 10 minutes.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Colombia's API integration requires Bold review/certification and may require PCI evidence; API call limits and charges for exceeding them are account-specific and not numerically published.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Colombia merchant remains responsible for its own products and tax duties; the acquirer makes legally required withholding reports and Bold shows the deductions.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Peru seller must issue SUNAT-compliant boleta/factura and comply with local tax rules; Bold deducts IGV and applicable withholding from settlement.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Colombia: merchant must give buyer a receipt, electronic invoice or equivalent and keep delivery/transaction support for at least five years.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Peru: Bold sends a transaction confirmation to merchant email within 24 hours and gives link/QR payments a transaction ID; merchant must issue a SUNAT receipt or invoice.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Tax-exempt checkout handling and buyer tax-ID invoice automation were not published.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Colombia: seller balance can be sent to a registered bank account; Cuenta Digital Bold is an optional separate deposit account product.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Peru: settlement is paid to the seller's registered bank account.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: PayPal, Payoneer, crypto-wallet or other non-bank merchant payout methods were not published.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Colombia sales settle in COP; USD-priced links convert to COP at Bold's stated conversion basis.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Peru pricing and standard settlement are in PEN; foreign card transactions may settle in PEN or another currency enabled for the issuer.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: A complete seller payout currency matrix by account and bank was not published.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Colombia: next-day option reaches Cuenta Digital before 10 a.m.; immediate settlement is also offered; external-bank option arrives one business day after 2 p.m.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Peru: standard bank settlement is 24 hours for BCP, BBVA, Scotiabank and Interbank, and 48 hours for other banks, counted from 23:59 on the sale date on business days; contract states a maximum of three business days after confirmation.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Additional Peru transfers outside the standard settlement cadence may cost extra; no amount or processing-time schedule is public.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: Bold processes payment and sends status events; digital fulfillment, license-key delivery and membership provisioning are not described as built-in services.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Peru POS supports splitting a restaurant/table bill so multiple buyers pay their share; this is checkout bill-splitting, not marketplace seller settlement.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: A marketplace product for splitting a single online sale across sellers and its fees was not published.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: Bold does not publish a crypto checkout offer; Colombia's prohibited-activity policy bars virtual-asset businesses.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Not applicable: the checked Bold payment offers do not accept crypto assets.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto checkout or settlement path is published.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: payment and refund docs cover fiat transactions.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: Bold is a hosted payment service, not self-hosted crypto software.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Colombia online transactions can be downloaded in daily or monthly Excel reports; status can also be queried by API or webhook.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Customer export, portable card tokens, subscription migration and automated transfer to another gateway were not published.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Peru contracts are indefinite and either party may terminate with at least 30 calendar days' notice; termination does not remove unsettled chargeback obligations.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Colombia terms allow suspension/termination for breach, risk or inactivity and describe treatment of open disputes; a seller closure notice period and data-retention schedule were not clearly published in checked payment terms.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Bold is the payments brand operated in Colombia by Bold.Co S.A.S. (NIT 901.281.572-4); Bold Pagos acts as payment aggregator and works with acquiring partners.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Bold Perú contracts merchants through the brand's Peruvian platform. Its terms identify Compañía Peruana de Soluciones y Servicios Integrados S.A.C. (RUC 20601443651) as the contracting “Bold” and call the offer part of Grupo Bold.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Bold Perú's tariff page footer identifies Soluciones y Servicios Integrados S.A.C. with RUC 20602370497, different from the RUC in its current terms.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: In Peru, Bold says merchants migrated from VendeMás can keep their account-executive-agreed rates; the site does not call this a corporate acquisition.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Colombia merchants can contact Bold Payments by WhatsApp, email or help center; online API merchants also have a support bot 24/7 and may book paid expert sessions.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Peru publishes phone, WhatsApp and email support, available Monday-Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m., Saturday 9 a.m.–7 p.m., Sunday/holidays 9 a.m.–6 p.m.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Bold online payments are active in Colombia and Peru. Current product pages, legal terms and developer docs are live.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Bold's press room shows articles through February 2026 and its Academia lists 2026 posts; the checked sources contain no shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Colombia payment services are provided by Bold.Co S.A.S. and Bold CF Compañía de Financiamiento S.A.; Bold CF is supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Peru terms name Compañía Peruana de Soluciones y Servicios Integrados S.A.C. as contracting entity; the tariff footer shows a different RUC, leaving the entity identifier unresolved.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: The online API agreement requires merchant PCI DSS controls when the merchant captures/stores payment-card data; Bold says its system/device certificates are maintained but does not publish a current certificate scope in these pages.

apps.name: BTCPay Server
apps.line: Self-hosted crypto checkout and invoicing software.

free.text: Free software; you pay for hosting and network costs

cells.payout: Merchant sends payouts; network timing varies

fee.math: BTCPay takes no fee on each payment. Network and hosting costs are separate.
BTCPay takes no fee on each payment. Network and hosting costs are separate.
BTCPay takes no fee on each payment. Network and hosting costs are separate.
BTCPay takes no fee on each payment. Network and hosting costs are separate.

apps.news: The Foundation about, goals and privacy pages describe project funding and support; no separate current Foundation newsroom or shutdown/rebrand notice was found.

facts.label: Separate processor account
facts.value: No separate gateway, acquiring account or BTCPay merchant account is required for the core software.

facts.label: External account dependencies
facts.value: Shopify integration requires a Shopify store and relevant Shopify plan; other ecommerce integrations depend on their own platform.

facts.label: Software setup and recurring price
facts.value: BTCPay Server software has no setup charge, subscription, or transaction fee.

facts.label: Hosting cost
facts.value: Server rental, electricity, domain, backup storage and maintenance are paid or supplied by the operator; there is no single BTCPay price for them.

facts.label: Example VPS estimate
facts.value: Current specifications say a low-cost VPS around or below $20 USD per month can usually satisfy the small Bitcoin-only starting profile.

facts.label: International card processing
facts.value: Core BTCPay Server does not process cards and publishes no cross-border card surcharge.

facts.label: Fiat price conversion
facts.value: Configured exchange-rate sources quote the crypto amount for an invoice denominated in a fiat currency; BTCPay itself does not convert collected crypto into fiat.

facts.label: Third-party conversion cost
facts.value: No standard conversion spread or fee is published for optional exchange or conversion plugins.

facts.label: Local payment method cost
facts.value: No fee schedule for local fiat methods applies because the core checkout does not collect bank, card, cash or mobile-money payments.

facts.label: Billing surcharge
facts.value: BTCPay adds no subscription billing surcharge or per-renewal service fee.

facts.label: Tax and checkout add-ons
facts.value: There is no BTCPay tax calculation, filing, fraud-review or paid checkout add-on fee schedule.

facts.label: Refund workflow and service fee
facts.value: Refunds are manually initiated through pull payments; BTCPay charges no refund-processing fee.

facts.label: Refund network cost
facts.value: The merchant pays the crypto network or Lightning routing/channel cost for a refund payout; the amount depends on network conditions and route.

facts.label: Disputes and chargebacks
facts.value: There is no card-acquirer chargeback desk or card dispute fee in the core crypto software; the merchant handles buyer complaints directly.

facts.label: Transaction reversal risk
facts.value: On-chain crypto payments are generally not reversible by BTCPay after broadcast; refunds are new merchant-authorized transactions.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: BTCPay does not charge a payout fee; outgoing on-chain network fees or Lightning routing/liquidity costs may apply.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No universal BTCPay payout minimum is published; asset dust thresholds, wallet rules and channel liquidity may constrain a transaction.

facts.label: Payment limits
facts.value: No universal minimum or maximum invoice amount is published across all enabled assets.

facts.label: Store and server limits
facts.value: Self-hosted operator controls store count and server settings; docs say a server can attach unlimited stores, subject to infrastructure capacity.

facts.label: Seller countries
facts.value: BTCPay publishes no seller-country allowlist for self-hosted software; its use-case page says anyone can use BTCPay, including individuals, merchants and nonprofits.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: BTCPay software has no merchant onboarding step that limits sole traders, individuals, or companies. Local business, tax and crypto rules still apply.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: No BTCPay business registration, local address, or bank account is required to install the software.

facts.label: Hosting region
facts.value: The merchant selects and operates the server or chooses an independent host; the project publishes no mandatory hosting country.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: BTCPay itself does not require merchant identity checks or KYC to use self-hosted software.

facts.label: Website review
facts.value: No BTCPay project website or product review is required before the merchant can deploy the software.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Download or deploy the open-source software; there is no central merchant signup or sales approval.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No minimum revenue, transaction count, or business size is published for self-hosted use.

facts.label: Digital goods and software
facts.value: Invoices and integrations can be used to sell digital goods, software and online services; delivery/access is controlled by the merchant's store or app.

facts.label: Subscriptions and memberships
facts.value: Subscription offerings can describe SaaS access, newsletters, memberships and recurring donations.

facts.label: Physical goods and services
facts.value: E-commerce integrations and custom integrations can take payment for merchant-supplied physical products or services.

facts.label: Donations and crowdfunding
facts.value: BTCPay supports donation and crowdfunding use cases through store applications and optional integrations.

facts.label: Product restrictions
facts.value: No centralized prohibited-product list for self-hosted BTCPay software was found; the software does not perform merchant underwriting.

facts.label: Host or plugin restrictions
facts.value: Independent hosts and third-party plugins may set separate acceptable-use or compatibility rules.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: BTCPay has no processor-managed buyer-country list; a customer's ability to pay depends on supported crypto networks and local law.

facts.label: Reserve and held balance
facts.value: BTCPay does not hold a processor reserve or merchant balance; received payments go to the merchant's configured wallet.

facts.label: Approval time
facts.value: There is no BTCPay merchant approval or underwriting stage; time to install and sync depends on the operator's hardware, network and chosen chain.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Free, open-source, self-hosted, non-custodial crypto checkout and invoicing software.

facts.label: Legal seller
facts.value: The merchant sells to the buyer and controls the store, wallet, product, order fulfilment, taxes and customer policy.

facts.label: Checkout denomination
facts.value: Merchants can create invoices in supported fiat reference currencies or crypto denominations; a displayed fiat quote is converted to the selected crypto amount using the configured rate source.

facts.label: Settlement currencies
facts.value: Core settlement is to supported crypto wallets, not a bank balance in fiat.

facts.label: Bitcoin methods
facts.value: Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning are supported.

facts.label: Optional crypto methods
facts.value: Optional chain definitions include Litecoin, Groestlcoin, Feathercoin, Dash, Dogecoin, Monacoin, Monero, Beldex, Liquid, Zcash and Decred.

facts.label: Fiat methods
facts.value: The core payment product does not provide card acquiring, bank transfer collection, cash payments or mobile-money processing.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time invoices, payment links, point-of-sale pages and ecommerce checkout are supported.

facts.label: Manual recurring billing
facts.value: Subscriptions can send reminders and let the customer pay each billing period manually.

facts.label: Prepaid-credit renewals
facts.value: Automatic subscription renewals can deduct from customer credit balances that were prepaid.

facts.label: Automatic wallet debit
facts.value: A recurring debit from a customer's arbitrary Bitcoin wallet is not the subscription model documented by BTCPay.

facts.label: Subscription plans and portal
facts.value: Merchants can set offerings, plans, prices, billing intervals and access rules; the customer portal supports top-ups, plan changes and billing history.

facts.label: Subscription dunning
facts.value: Reminder emails are available when email is configured; a card-style automatic retry or recovery service is not described.

facts.label: Trials and grace periods
facts.value: Plans can include a trial measured in days and a grace period during which access may continue after renewal funds are insufficient.

facts.label: Plan changes and renewal rules
facts.value: Merchants can permit or limit subscriber upgrades and downgrades, and can mark plans renewable or non-renewable.

facts.label: Usage and recovery features not specified
facts.value: Seat metering, usage-based pricing, coupon handling, proration and automatic failed-payment retries are not specified in the subscription guide.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: BTCPay creates a hosted invoice checkout page with selected crypto payment methods and live payment state.

facts.label: Payment links and invoices
facts.value: The merchant can create an invoice/payment request and share its link without first integrating an online store.

facts.label: Point of sale and forms
facts.value: Built-in apps include Point of Sale, Crowdfund and Payment Request; form features are configured by the store operator.

facts.label: Custom checkout and theme
facts.value: Checkout branding and integrations can be customized on the merchant's server; no centrally hosted checkout domain is provided by the project.

facts.label: Developer API
facts.value: The Greenfield API and legacy BitPay-compatible API support invoice and store workflows.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: Webhooks notify the merchant's software about invoice/payment events and can be used to automate fulfilment.

facts.label: Store integrations
facts.value: Official guides cover WooCommerce, Drupal, Magento, PrestaShop, Shopify and other store integrations, plus custom integration.

facts.label: Plugin directory
facts.value: Server admins can browse the plugin directory for payment options, integrations and other tools; each plugin page links to source, documentation, supported server versions and user reviews.

facts.label: Plugin installation and trust
facts.value: Only server admins install plugins; installation takes effect after a server restart. Plugins run inside BTCPay and can access server services and data, and listing does not mean security-audited.

facts.label: Test environment
facts.value: Developers can use regtest/test-network configuration and test the store checkout before accepting real payments.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities
facts.value: The merchant remains responsible for tax registration, tax calculation, collection, reporting and payment to authorities.

facts.label: Tax coverage
facts.value: No country tax engine, filing coverage list, or remittance service is published for core BTCPay.

facts.label: Buyer payment record
facts.value: Invoice pages record payment request, amount, exchange-rate period, payment methods and payment/settlement status.

facts.label: Tax and business invoice data
facts.value: Invoice metadata can include item description, item code, buyer details and tax amount; these fields do not certify a locally compliant tax invoice.

facts.label: Receipts and invoice export
facts.value: Invoice reports can export CSV containing invoice, payment, method, rate, fee and metadata details.

facts.label: Payout destinations
facts.value: Funds are paid to merchant-controlled crypto wallets; no bank, PayPal or fiat payout method is built into core BTCPay.

facts.label: Payout approval and sending
facts.value: Recipient claims create a payout; the store reviews or auto-approves the claim, then separately sends the funds from a compatible wallet.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: BTCPay does not maintain a fiat balance. Wallets hold the enabled crypto assets; fiat amounts may be used to denominate invoices.

facts.label: Invoice settlement timing
facts.value: Lightning payments normally settle without waiting for on-chain confirmations; on-chain invoices settle under the merchant's configured confirmation policy.

facts.label: Merchant payout timing
facts.value: The merchant initiates outgoing payouts; time to confirmation depends on network or Lightning routing conditions. There is no processor settlement batch.

facts.label: Product delivery
facts.value: BTCPay tracks payment and invoice status; the merchant's store, ecommerce platform or custom app delivers files, software access and memberships.

facts.label: Integration scope examples
facts.value: Official integration guides cover ecommerce storefronts and platforms including WooCommerce, Drupal, Shopify, Magento and PrestaShop.

facts.label: Marketplace and split settlement
facts.value: Core docs do not describe a standard managed marketplace onboarding or automatic fiat/crypto split-settlement product.

facts.label: Bitcoin and Lightning
facts.value: Bitcoin supports on-chain payments and Lightning through CLN, LND or Phoenixd.

facts.label: Litecoin and Groestlcoin
facts.value: Litecoin is listed with no Lightning backend; Groestlcoin is listed with CLN or LND Lightning.

facts.label: Other optional chains
facts.value: Available definitions also include Feathercoin, Dash, Dogecoin, Monacoin, Monero, Beldex, Liquid, Zcash and Decred.

facts.label: Third-party coin support and maintenance
facts.value: Bitcoin and Litecoin are project-maintained; other chain integrations rely on their communities and are used at the operator's risk.

facts.label: Tokens and networks
facts.value: Liquid definition supports Liquid assets, including USDt; other tokens/chains may be added by plugins. Token support is network-specific, not a universal ticker list.

facts.label: Custody model
facts.value: Non-custodial: payment goes directly to the merchant's wallet; the BTCPay project and an ordinary host do not hold merchant funds.

facts.label: Receiving without exposing private keys
facts.value: BTCPay can derive receiving addresses from a public wallet key; private spending keys are not required to receive invoices.

facts.label: Wallet options
facts.value: The operator may use the internal wallet, a watch-only/hardware wallet workflow, or supported wallet connection; spending keys kept off-server reduce hot-wallet exposure.

facts.label: Hot-wallet incident implication
facts.value: The November theft report specifically involved server hot wallets; project states hardware wallets and wallets with spending keys kept off-server were unaffected in those reported thefts.

facts.label: Settlement path
facts.value: Supported cryptocurrency payments settle to the merchant's configured wallet; BTCPay does not hold or sweep them to a provider balance.

facts.label: Fiat off-ramp
facts.value: Core BTCPay does not cash out to bank fiat; optional third-party conversion plugins or independent exchanges are separate services.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: No provider payout queue or payout schedule exists; merchant transfers are initiated from the wallet and confirmation depends on the chosen network.

facts.label: Invoice expiry and confirmation
facts.value: Invoice rate lock and expiry are configurable; on-chain settlement follows the store's confirmation policy, while Lightning normally settles without on-chain confirmation waits.

facts.label: Partial, underpaid and late payments
facts.value: Store settings can define expiry, confirmation windows and underpayment tolerance; expired or partially paid invoices require merchant review.

facts.label: Refund procedure
facts.value: Merchant issues a refund claim link; after the customer supplies a destination, the merchant reviews and pays a new crypto transaction.

facts.label: Wrong amount, asset or address
facts.value: Wrong-chain or wrong-address transfers are not automatically reversed by BTCPay; refund/recovery depends on merchant control of the destination wallet and the network.

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: Core BTCPay is self-hosted software run on the merchant's own server or VPS; updates, backups, uptime and security are operator responsibilities.

facts.label: Current practical server profile
facts.value: For a small Bitcoin-only setup without heavy add-ons, current specs recommend 4 GB RAM, 2 virtual CPU cores, at least 50 GB usable SSD and bandwidth for the initial chain sync.

facts.label: Older published minimum
facts.value: Deployment FAQ still lists 2 GB RAM, 80 GB pruned storage and Docker for Bitcoin plus Lightning.

facts.label: Extra chain and Lightning requirements
facts.value: Each full node adds storage and upkeep; Monero's chain was about 105 GB as of July 2026 and specs advise at least 250 GB SSD. Lightning needs an always-on service, peer connectivity, liquidity and careful backups.

facts.label: MIT licence and operator cost
facts.value: MIT-licensed software is free to download; merchant pays only its server/infrastructure costs and crypto network or Lightning costs, not a BTCPay processing fee.

facts.value: Docker deployment provides backup and restore scripts for databases, volumes and generated secrets; Lightning recovery needs extra channel-backup care.

facts.label: Moving or importing history
facts.value: A built-in migration to another payment provider is not documented; an operator can retain exported reports and use server backup/migration procedures.

facts.label: Closing an account/server
facts.value: There is no central BTCPay merchant account to cancel; the operator can stop or remove their own instance and retains control of server data and wallet funds.

facts.label: Outstanding funds on closure
facts.value: BTCPay does not hold funds on exit; the operator must move funds from their own wallet and manage any open invoice or refund obligations.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: BTCPay Server; self-hosted crypto payment and invoicing software.

facts.label: Owner and maintainers
facts.value: Community-developed software; the BTCPay Server Foundation supports the project and accepts donations for project work and operating costs. No commercial processor owner was identified.

facts.label: Old names and current status
facts.value: No former product name, acquisition, rebrand, or shutdown notice was found. Project remains active; GitHub and blog list current 2026 releases and advisories.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Public documentation, FAQs, GitHub issues and community Mattermost/Telegram are the published support routes.

facts.label: Paid support and guarantees

facts.label: Current operating status and release

facts.label: November 2026 hot-wallet incident
facts.value: The project says thefts reported on 2026-11-01 affected hot wallets on versions 2.4.1 and earlier; older operators should move to a fresh server and new wallet after sweeping remaining funds.

facts.label: August LND security incident
facts.value: An unauthenticated remote attacker could obtain LND admin macaroon files on versions before 2.4.2; the project confirmed attacks and stolen funds.

facts.label: Plugin Builder compromise
facts.value: Builder intrusion detected 2026-09-02 affected plugin developers using the builder; the project found no attempt to tamper with published plugins. It reopened in 2.4.5 with isolated builds.

facts.label: Software licence
facts.value: The BTCPay Server repository is licensed under the MIT License. It permits use, copying, modification, distribution, sublicensing and sale subject to the notice and licence conditions.

facts.label: Processor authorization
facts.value: No BTCPay Server merchant processor or contracting entity was found in the product docs; they describe self-hosted software rather than custody or fiat acquiring. A payment-services licence for the software is not published.

facts.label: Security maintenance scope
facts.value: Project publishes releases and security advisories through its blog and GitHub; its 2.4.7 notes report 85 scanner findings fixed.

facts.value: Payment Links and Invoices do not list cards, bank debit, mobile money, or cash methods.

facts.label: Repeat payment requests
facts.value: Reusable links can collect repeat payments and recurring invoices can be created.
