facts.value: A crypto-only company can submit crypto-wallet statements and tax returns when it has no conventional bank account; alternatives are subject to review.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: A particular local office, local director, or bank account in the merchant’s country is not stated as a universal merchant-eligibility condition.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Merchant signup requires a business application and identity, AML/CFT, fraud, and background review; CoinGate may request more information during the relationship.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Standard company documents include business registration, articles of association, live ID check for the applicant, passport or national ID for the director and each 25%+ beneficial owner, and operational-address evidence; a remote business may use a director’s personal address proof with an explanation. CoinGate may also request more documents or a business-specific questionnaire.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Operational-address proof may be a utility bill, lease, or insurance policy. Remote businesses may provide a director’s personal proof of address with an explanation.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: CoinGate may request source-of-funds/wealth records, tax declarations or audited statements, bank statements, licenses, ownership information, and a business-specific questionnaire.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: A personal login can be created before applying for a business account; live merchant processing requires business verification and approval.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: No published minimum revenue, transaction volume, company age, or monthly sales threshold for Standard merchant signup was found.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: The processing service covers payments for a merchant’s goods or services. CoinGate does not publish a complete product-by-product approval matrix for SaaS, software, ebooks, courses, memberships, or physical goods.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Prohibited or rejectable activity includes unlicensed financial services, unregistered money transfer, unregulated or anonymous exchanges/P2P, pyramid schemes, artificial trading, and unlicensed gambling; adult content without age checks or lawful controls; weapons, controlled substances, unauthorized medicines, spyware, unlawful hacking tools, and services designed to evade AML or sanctions.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: ICOs, token sales, and NFT transactions require prior written consent or appropriate legal classification/registration.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Sanctioned customers, beneficial owners, jurisdictions, wallets, or transactions are prohibited; suspicious or prohibited use can lead to holds, suspension, or termination.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: CoinGate’s current restricted-payments help page lists Afghanistan, Belarus, Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Myanmar, Palestine, Russia, Syria, Yemen, and Crimea, Sevastopol, Donetsk, and Luhansk as unsupported payment locations.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Payments cannot originate from sanctioned jurisdictions, and merchants must enforce this in their order flow; buyer access is not identical to seller signup coverage.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: No universal percentage reserve or fixed reserve period for merchants is published.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: CoinGate may delay, suspend, or freeze a transaction/account for AML, sanctions, fraud, legal, authority, or security review.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Dormancy can trigger restrictions, conversion of balances, and a fee accruing at 2% per week (minimum €10) after 12 months without customer transactions plus 6 months without a response to due-diligence requests.

facts.label: Approval-time estimate
facts.value: Merchant verification usually takes 1–2 business days after all required documents are submitted.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Crypto payment processor with hosted payment pages, merchant billing links, API checkout, plugins, payment buttons, and payment channels.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: The merchant sells the goods or services to the shopper; CoinGate is not the seller or merchant of record.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: The price currency can be entered as a fiat currency or supported crypto asset; the shopper chooses a supported crypto and network at checkout.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: CoinGate explicitly lists EUR, USD, and GBP as fiat settlement currencies; all fiat bank withdrawal paths and currencies depend on the enabled account options.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Checkout is crypto-only: supported coins and networks are selected by the buyer on CoinGate’s hosted payment page.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Supported merchant checkout assets currently include BTC/Bitcoin and Lightning; LTC/Litecoin; ETH/Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism; BCH/Bitcoin Cash; XRP/XRP; TRX/Tron; DOGE/Dogecoin; BNB/Ethereum and BSC; POL/Ethereum and Polygon; USDC/Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism; SOL/Solana; EURC/Ethereum.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: BTC is accepted on Bitcoin and Lightning; ETH on Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism; BNB on Ethereum and BSC; POL on Ethereum and Polygon; USDC on Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Yes. Merchants can create one-time checkout orders, payment buttons, and billing invoices.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Billing can send scheduled invoices weekly or monthly, but the customer manually pays each invoice in crypto; automatic recurring wallet debits and saved card mandates are not described.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: A payment channel assigns one permanent deposit address to a named client/contact for repeated deposits; it is enabled on request.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Billing supports named person/business contacts, saved products, quantities, invoice line items, expiry settings, invoice history, resend/cancel, and reusable invoice templates, and up to 10% configurable underpayment cover.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Automated card retry/dunning, plan changes, seat billing, usage metering, trials, and prorations are not published as merchant billing features.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Hosted checkout page: supported and required for payment completion; checkout cannot be fully white-labeled or replaced with the merchant’s own payment UI; merchant display-name and order-title customization is available.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Payment links: available through Billing invoices and dashboard-generated payment requests; can be emailed or shared directly.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Payment buttons support fixed-price, slider, and preset-amount options.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Merchant API and API reference support order creation, status, settlement currency, and callbacks/webhooks. Merchants generate separate API credentials for each integration and use separate credentials for sandbox.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Official ready-to-use ecommerce plugins include WooCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, and OpenCart; CoinGate’s product site also lists WHMCS and other extensions. Callbacks and notifications can be configured by integration, including JSON or form encoding.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Sandbox supports simulated orders, payments, refunds, settlement flows, and callback testing; sandbox credentials and data are separate from production.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Payment completion notifications, API callbacks, and callback formats are configurable per integration.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: The merchant is responsible for its own tax assessment, collection, payment/remittance, and filings; CoinGate says it does not do these or issue merchant tax reports.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: CoinGate may request tax declarations or financial statements for KYB and may report information to authorities where legally required.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: CoinGate creates customer invoice/payment pages and can email or share them; merchant supplies contact, amount, line items, and invoice title.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: CoinGate service-fee invoices are generated monthly on the 15th for the previous month; order, refund, and transaction reports can be exported as CSV.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Merchants can withdraw crypto to their own external wallet or fiat to a bank account; supported bank rails shown include SEPA and SWIFT.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Crypto payouts can be sent to third-party blockchain addresses or beneficiaries; payout links are also listed in the current company updates.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Fiat receive/settlement currencies: EUR, USD, and GBP. CoinGate maps EUR to SEPA/SWIFT, USD to SWIFT, and GBP to SWIFT.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Merchants may keep supported crypto paid by shoppers or convert it to another supported crypto, including USDC; BTC and USDC are examples listed for payment channels. Current merchant assets include BTC, LTC, ETH, BCH, XRP, TRX, DOGE, BNB, POL, USDC, SOL, and EURC.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: USDT is no longer a current merchant settlement option; most merchant support ended under MiCA changes in 2025.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Standard automatic settlements are weekly. Enterprise advertises weekly or on-request settlements; the Enterprise overview also says on-demand automatic settlements.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Manual crypto and fiat withdrawals are usually processed within a few hours; additional checks or larger transfers may take up to 24 hours.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Fiat transfer arrival time at the merchant’s bank, by currency and country, is not guaranteed as a fixed universal number.

facts.label: Product delivery and access extras
facts.value: CoinGate processes crypto payments and credits crypto or converted funds; the merchant remains responsible for providing its product/service, refunds policy, and delivery terms. CoinGate does not publish content hosting, course delivery, license-key distribution, or member-area access as checkout features.

facts.label: Product delivery and access extras
facts.value: No digital content hosting, course delivery, license-key distribution, or member-area access product is published as part of CoinGate checkout.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Payment channels can assign a separate recurring deposit address to each named client/contact and identify incoming payments for the merchant.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: A checkout transaction split among multiple sellers/beneficiaries or a marketplace submerchant onboarding product is not published in the checkout pages checked.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Merchant checkout supports BTC on Bitcoin and Lightning.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Merchant checkout supports LTC/Litecoin, BCH/Bitcoin Cash, XRP/XRP, TRX/Tron, DOGE/Dogecoin, and SOL/Solana.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: ETH is accepted on Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism; BNB on Ethereum and BSC; POL on Ethereum and Polygon.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: USDC is supported on Ethereum, BSC, Solana, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, and Optimism; EURC is supported on Ethereum.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: During payment processing, CoinGate receives crypto on the merchant’s behalf and credits the merchant’s CoinGate account; customer assets are held in custody under its regulated service.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Merchants can configure settlement to keep crypto or convert it; crypto left in the account remains subject to price volatility and account/custody risks.

facts.label: Crypto settlement paths and fees
facts.value: Settlement options include keeping the original crypto, converting to another crypto such as USDC, or converting to EUR/USD/GBP for bank withdrawal.

facts.label: Crypto settlement paths and fees
facts.value: EUR bank settlement uses SEPA or SWIFT; USD and GBP are listed with SWIFT rails.

facts.label: Crypto settlement paths and fees
facts.value: Standard checkout has a 1% merchant fee and payment quotes include an additional risk margin; crypto payouts to third parties are €0.50 + 0.5%, or €0.50 + 1.5% with conversion; manual platform conversion is 1%.

facts.label: Crypto settlement paths and fees
facts.value: CoinGate’s default settlement fallback is USDC unless the merchant changes its currency settings.

facts.label: Crypto settlement paths and fees
facts.value: For crypto checkout, funds appear in merchant CoinGate balance after required blockchain confirmation and any compliance checks; fiat then requires a separate withdrawal.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Hosted checkout shows the exact coin, network, amount, and a 20-minute payment window; the shopper must pay the exact amount to the active address.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: On-chain confirmations vary by network; Bitcoin Lightning is described as seconds, while other chain confirmation times depend on network conditions.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Expired, late, underpaid, and overpaid payments have separate handling; invoice settings can allow underpayment cover up to 10%, and expired orders can be processed for a configured period.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Wrong coin/network, unsupported chain, missing Solana memo, or missing/invalid XRP destination tag can cause delay, manual mapping, non-credit, or a refund-only outcome.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Refunds are new crypto transfers, may use a different supported currency/network than the original, and can differ in value because of exchange rates.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Hosted service: CoinGate hosts payment pages and handles order monitoring, confirmation, account reporting, and settlement. Merchant needs no self-hosted payment server, but API users maintain their own store and callback endpoint.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Dashboard exports include order, refund, and ledger transaction CSVs; transaction exports show credits, debits, fees, conversions, and running balance.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Customer-subscription migration, one-click transfer to another processor, and crypto payment-data portability routes are not published.

facts.label: Closing and fund release
facts.value: Merchant may close an account with at least 30 calendar days’ written notice. CoinGate may also close without cause with 30 days’ notice, or suspend/terminate immediately for specified legal, compliance, insolvency, or breach events.

facts.label: Closing and fund release
facts.value: For non-dormant closure, unrestricted balances must be withdrawn within 6 months after the request; after that, or without proof of ownership, the right to the balance is forfeited.

facts.label: Closing and fund release
facts.value: Dormant-account balance claim is discretionary and requires requested documents within 6 months after closure; balances under €10 may be deducted immediately under the dormancy terms.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: CoinGate is the merchant crypto payment product operated by UAB Decentralized, a Lithuanian private limited liability company. The entity was registered as UAB Virtualios Valiutos in 2014 and renamed UAB Decentralized in 2020.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: A corporate parent or ultimate owner above UAB Decentralized is not named on the About, terms, or legal-documents pages checked.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Public help center and email support are listed; verified business users can submit a ticket from the dashboard or a specific order/refund.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Transaction-linked tickets are prioritized and usually answered within up to 2 business hours, according to the help page.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Standard plan lists standard email support; Enterprise lists dedicated technical support, direct developer access, and a dedicated account manager.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Active: current pricing, merchant checkout, support, and developer documentation are available; status page currently reports services online.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: MiCA-related change: CoinGate stopped DAI and phased out USDT for merchant payments/settlement during 2025; current merchant stablecoin is USDC.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: BCH payments, settlement, and payouts were re-enabled on October 12, 2026 after being disabled from July 1, 2026.

facts.label: Legal, licence, and security scope
facts.value: Services are provided by UAB Decentralized, incorporated in Lithuania; the Bank of Lithuania register lists crypto-asset service-provider licence LB002323 and payment-institution licence LB002324, both valid from December 16, 2025.

facts.label: Legal, licence, and security scope
facts.value: Current General Terms were published December 1, 2025 and took effect January 1, 2026; current crypto-payment special terms took effect September 1, 2026.

facts.label: Legal, licence, and security scope
facts.value: The older Merchant Terms page says the service was not subject to authorization; it was superseded by General Terms from January 1, 2026 and should not be used as the current licensing answer.

facts.label: Legal, licence, and security scope
facts.value: Current AML policy describes identity/beneficial-owner checks, ongoing screening, blockchain analytics, and transaction monitoring; current terms also require two-factor authentication for account access and transfers.

facts.label: Legal, licence, and security scope
facts.value: General security certifications such as a published PCI DSS level or SOC 2 report for merchant processing were not found in the legal, security, and product pages checked.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Court affirmed a EUR 16,530 AML/CTF fine against CoinGate operator UAB Decentralized on 19 November 2025.

cells.countries: Access depends on review; full seller list unpublished

facts.label: Required accounts and dependencies
facts.value: Merchant needs a CoinPayments account and completed compliance review; API use additionally needs a CoinPayments integration. No separate card processor is needed for crypto checkout.

facts.label: Fiat-bank payout dependency
facts.value: Fiat bank payout is subject to approval and an account-manager configured route; bank and local-rail eligibility may involve partners.

facts.label: New platform fixed charges
facts.value: A standard setup, monthly or annual subscription amount is not published on the New fee page.

facts.label: New processing fee schedule
facts.value: New platform: 0.5% for coins and 1% for tokens; personal-wallet deposits are free for first USD 15,000/month then 0.5%, excluding conversions.

facts.label: Legacy processing fee schedule
facts.value: Legacy platform: 3% for coins and tokens; personal-wallet deposits are free for first USD 15,000/month then 3%.

facts.label: Inactivity fee by agreement
facts.value: The global PaidInSatoshi agreement says accounts become dormant after 12 months without a transaction and incur a 5.5% fee on the account balance per further 12 months.

facts.label: US dormant-account fee
facts.value: The US agreement allows a dormancy or administrative fee only as permitted or required by applicable state law; it does not publish a standard rate.

facts.label: International card cost
facts.value: Not applicable: the core crypto gateway has no international card-processing rate.

facts.label: Currency conversion fee
facts.value: New fee page says conversions carry the conversion partner’s fee plus a blockchain network fee; no universal conversion percentage is published.

facts.label: Conversion rate basis and timing
facts.value: Conversion rates are set when the merchant initiates the conversion; the checkout fiat/crypto amount is locked for 60 minutes.

facts.label: Network fee by settlement mode
facts.value: New pricing shows no network charge for To Balance; ASAP uses a network fee per payment; Nightly uses one network fee for the batch. Legacy has its own fee table.

facts.label: Local payment-method fee
facts.value: Not applicable: local bank transfers, cards and mobile-money methods are not standard buyer checkout methods on the core crypto gateway.

facts.label: Recurring/billing surcharge
facts.value: No separate subscription or invoice surcharge is published; the standard crypto payment processing fee applies to a successful merchant payment.

facts.label: Tax, fraud and checkout add-ons
facts.value: No public tax calculation/filing or fraud-tool add-on fee is listed; CoinPayments says merchants retain their own tax and legal responsibilities.

facts.label: Merchant refunds
facts.value: Confirmed crypto transfers are irreversible; a customer refund is initiated by the merchant as a new transfer, not through a card dispute reversal.

facts.label: Automatic refunds and refund cost
facts.value: New checkout automatically routes eligible late, expired, underpaid or excess funds into refund flow; refunds deduct network fees, and excess below the network fee is not returned.

facts.label: Chargebacks and disputes
facts.value: Confirmed on-chain payments do not have card-network chargebacks; merchant handles product/service disputes and customer refunds.

facts.label: Compliance holds and risk review
facts.value: CoinPayments/VASPs may delay, refuse, cancel or hold transactions for legal, fraud, technical or compliance review.

facts.label: Crypto payout fee
facts.value: New public schedule lists no CoinPayments withdrawal service fee; external wallet sends incur the applicable network fee, while internal CoinPayments transfers have no network fee.

facts.label: Fiat payout fee
facts.value: No universal public fiat-bank payout fee schedule was found.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No universal minimum balance for merchant withdrawal or bank payout is published on current public pages.

facts.label: Asset-specific minimums
facts.value: API docs note conversion pairs and spend requests have platform limits; exact minimums are route/currency-specific and should be checked through live currency-limit/fee APIs.

facts.label: Payment limits
facts.value: FAQ says single transactions of USD 350,000 or more require additional approval; no general daily/monthly checkout maximum is published.

facts.label: Minimum payment
facts.value: No universal minimum invoice amount is published. Network minimums, dust thresholds and conversion-pair limits vary by asset/route.

facts.label: Account-tier/verification limits
facts.value: Unverified account processing limits or a public tier/limit table are not published.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Services are unavailable to persons in Afghanistan, Belarus, Cuba, Haiti, Iran, North Korea, Libya, Myanmar, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Venezuela and Yemen; sanctions restrictions also apply.

facts.label: Complete seller-country allow-list
facts.value: No complete public list of every country whose business can open a new merchant account was found.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Terms permit personal or merchant accounts, but new-business onboarding asks each business to complete KYB and document its legal existence.

facts.label: Sole traders and legal-form country rules
facts.value: Whether sole traders, unincorporated sellers or individual merchants are accepted in each country is not published.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Signup routing and the applicable contracting entity depend on business-registration country; fiat bank payout requires approval and an eligible bank destination.

facts.label: Seller bank ownership/location conditions
facts.value: Exact business-bank account ownership and country requirements are not published as a universal rule.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: KYB is part of onboarding. Businesses provide proof of legal existence/registration, and identification for directors, control persons, beneficial owners and authorized representatives; associated people complete KYC as required.

facts.label: Website and business review
facts.value: Onboarding reviews business activity, business regions, purpose, source of funds, website and applicable business licences.

facts.label: Ongoing screening
facts.value: Terms and FAQ describe ongoing AML/KYC/KYB, sanctions and transaction monitoring; accounts may be asked to re-establish eligibility.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: The New platform advertises open account creation followed by email verification and KYB review; supported account activation is subject to approval.

facts.label: Minimum business size or sales volume
facts.value: No minimum revenue, transaction count or company size for standard merchant onboarding is published.

facts.label: Product types
facts.value: The gateway supports merchant sales of goods and services; a complete supported-product catalogue by category is not published.

facts.label: Digital products and subscriptions
facts.value: The official materials show invoicing and crypto payment acceptance but do not give a complete allowed list for SaaS, downloads, courses, memberships and physical goods.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Illegal, fraudulent, sanctioned or otherwise prohibited activity is disallowed; VASPs may refuse high legal, credit or reputational risk.

facts.label: High-risk pricing/approval
facts.value: High-risk industries may face an adjusted processing fee and additional review.

facts.label: Buyer-country reach
facts.value: CoinPayments markets global crypto payment reach and says its infrastructure serves 180 countries, subject to legal and VASP restrictions.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Buyers subject to sanctions or in the listed restricted jurisdictions cannot use affected VASP services; EU/EEA account access was paused from 1 July 2026.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Terms allow transaction delays, refusal, suspension and fund holds for law, suspected fraud, compliance or technical issues.

facts.label: Standard reserve percentage/duration
facts.value: No public standard rolling-reserve amount or fixed hold duration was found.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: FAQ says an account can be opened within a day and most businesses can go live in under a week, subject to verification and integration.

facts.label: Special/high-volume integration timing
facts.value: FAQ estimates a brokerage integration at about two weeks, while noting ready clients may complete it in days.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Crypto payment gateway, hosted invoice/checkout and API; the merchant sells its own goods or services. CoinPayments is not presented as merchant of record.

facts.label: Fiat route versus core crypto checkout
facts.value: Crypto settlement is core; fiat conversion and bank settlement are optional off-ramp services routed through the relevant entity or partners.

facts.label: Invoice denomination
facts.value: Invoice amounts can be set in a supported fiat or digital currency; the buyer pays in an enabled crypto asset.

facts.label: Charge/settlement currency availability
facts.value: Supported fiat and crypto currency catalogue is dynamic; exact merchant-enabled currencies are available through the public currency API and account settings.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Buyer checkout accepts enabled crypto coins and tokens through hosted invoices, payment buttons/plugins or API-created invoices.

facts.label: Fiat checkout methods
facts.value: Fiat bank/card checkout is not listed as a standard shopper method on the core crypto gateway.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Yes. Merchants can create single invoices, checkout payments, API invoices and payment buttons.

facts.label: Recurring payment collection
facts.value: Crypto invoices can be used to bill recurring services, but each invoice is paid by the buyer; automatic scheduled wallet debits are not described as a general core feature.

facts.label: Recurring-method limits
facts.value: CoinPayments does not publish card mandates or crypto auto-debit subscription support in the core checkout documentation.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Invoice creation supports line items, quantities, tax/shipping/discount fields, buyer details, notes, terms and email delivery.

facts.label: Subscription management and dunning
facts.value: Seats, usage billing, trials, prorations, automated retry schedules, card dunning and subscription plan management are not published core features.

facts.label: Hosted checkout and invoice links
facts.value: Hosted invoice checkout is supported and can be created in the dashboard or API; invoice links can be shared or embedded.

facts.label: Buy-now buttons and customization
facts.value: Official API supports permanent and single-invoice Buy Now buttons; hosted invoice docs mention custom branding.

facts.label: API and SDK
facts.value: New platform provides REST/JSON APIs and official client SDKs; production uses regional API instances with instance-specific credentials.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: Signed HMAC webhooks report invoice, deposit, wallet and withdrawal lifecycle events; endpoints and event subscriptions are configurable.

facts.label: Plugins and integrations
facts.value: The New platform lists two current official plugins: WooCommerce and WHMCS. Other platform plugins are listed as in development; API integration is also available.

facts.label: Testing and sandbox
facts.value: API documentation identifies a sandbox environment; live and sandbox keys/instances are separate.

facts.label: Transaction exports and event history
facts.value: Dashboard exports transaction history as CSV with filters; API exposes invoices, transactions and webhooks.

facts.label: Merchant tax responsibility
facts.value: Merchant remains responsible for determining and meeting its tax, licensing, reporting and sales obligations; CoinPayments is not the merchant of record.

facts.label: Tax collection and remittance coverage
facts.value: No CoinPayments merchant tax registration, filing or remittance coverage table is published.

facts.label: Buyer receipts and invoices
facts.value: Hosted invoices collect payment details and can include line items, buyer details, terms and email delivery; transaction data is accessible in the account.

facts.label: Tax invoices and business tax IDs
facts.value: The API has invoice tax fields, but tax-ID validation, exemptions and jurisdiction-compliant tax-invoice generation are not described.

facts.label: Crypto payout destinations
facts.value: Seller can hold funds in CoinPayments balance, send to another platform wallet, or forward to an external crypto address.

facts.label: Fiat payout destinations
facts.value: Approved accounts may withdraw to a bank account or use third-party transfer rails including ACH, SWIFT, SEPA or Faster Payments, depending on route.

facts.label: Crypto balance currencies
facts.value: CoinPayments supports multiple coin and token wallets; the public currency API is the current source of supported asset, chain and status metadata.

facts.label: Stablecoin settlement
facts.value: Merchants can convert incoming assets into a supported stablecoin or retain the original asset.

facts.label: Fiat settlement currencies
facts.value: Fiat payout is described as available in major currencies, but a complete current currency and seller-country list is not public.

facts.label: Crypto settlement timing
facts.value: After required blockchain confirmations, funds can stay in balance or be sent immediately, hourly, nightly or weekly; external settlement adds chain confirmation time.

facts.label: Fiat bank arrival
facts.value: Fiat bank payouts may need extra standard banking review and clearing time; no universal number of days is published.

facts.label: Scheduled payout frequency
facts.value: Public settings show balance/manual, immediate, hourly, nightly (about midnight EST) and weekly (Sunday about midnight EST) modes; FAQ also mentions threshold-based payouts.

facts.label: Digital product delivery
facts.value: CoinPayments provides payment confirmation events and API/plugin integrations but does not advertise delivery of the merchant's files, software licences or membership access.

facts.label: Fulfilment integration
facts.value: Webhooks can report payment/invoice lifecycle changes to the merchant’s app for fulfilment automation.

facts.label: Multi-seller / marketplace
facts.value: No general marketplace seller onboarding or split-payment product is described in core merchant docs.

facts.label: Internal business users
facts.value: Organization account offers role-based users (owner, viewer, sales) with separated permissions; this is team access, not marketplace split settlement.

facts.label: Supported coins
facts.value: Supported major native coins include BTC, ETH, LTC, BCH, BNB, XRP, TRX, SOL, DOGE and others; the list changes and is returned by the public currency API.

facts.label: Supported tokens and networks
facts.value: Tokens include USDT and USDC on multiple chains, with examples on ERC-20, TRC-20, BSC/BEP-20, Polygon, Solana, Base and Arbitrum; network-specific asset IDs are distinct.

facts.label: Live network and confirmation data
facts.value: API catalog records asset chain, status, decimals and required confirmation depth; assets may be active, under maintenance or removed.

facts.label: Custody model
facts.value: CoinPayments and its relevant VASP/partner hold merchant funds in custodial wallets; terms say assets are held for the user and processed under user instructions.

facts.label: Wallet settlement options
facts.value: Merchant may hold a CoinPayments balance, send to an external wallet, or configure automatic forwarding; the separate DepiPay product is described as non-custodial.

facts.label: Crypto-to-crypto / stablecoin route
facts.value: Conversion is merchant-initiated or configured in settlement settings; incoming assets may be converted to another supported coin or stablecoin.

facts.label: Fiat off-ramp
facts.value: Approved merchants can convert to major fiat currencies and settle to eligible bank accounts using SWIFT, ACH, SEPA, Faster Payments or partner/local rails.

facts.label: Fiat payout and conversion cost
facts.value: No universal fiat conversion spread, fixed payout fee or full supported-currency table is published.

facts.label: Confirmation and expiry
facts.value: Invoice uses a 60-minute rate lock; payment completes after the asset-specific confirmation depth. Funds arriving after timeout are eligible for automatic refund.

facts.label: Underpayment and overpayment
facts.value: Merchant can accept an underpayment manually or set a tolerance; otherwise buyer can top up or receive a refund. Overpayment credits the invoiced amount and returns excess automatically.

facts.label: Refund and wrong-network handling
facts.value: Buyer claims a refund to a wallet on the original chain; merchant-issued refunds are outbound transactions. Wrong-address/network recovery depends on asset and circumstances; support may assist but recovery is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: CoinPayments is a hosted service with hosted checkout, dashboard and API; merchants maintain their own store or application and do not self-host the gateway.

facts.label: Export data
facts.value: Dashboard supports CSV export of transaction history with date/type/status/currency filters; API provides transaction and invoice records.

facts.label: Moving to another provider
facts.value: Terms allow account closure and withdrawal of remaining assets, less outstanding amounts and network/third-party fees; no customer/payment-data migration service to another provider is described.

facts.label: Account closure
facts.value: Global agreement allows closure by withdrawing balances; pending transactions can be cancelled, and outstanding obligations/network or third-party fees may be deducted.

facts.label: Closure exceptions
facts.value: CoinPayments may refuse closure or hold assets if an inquiry/investigation is pending and may require identity checks before withdrawal; dormant accounts may be terminated after two years under terms.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: CoinPayments is the merchant crypto gateway at coinpayments.net. New accounts use the New platform; Classic/Legacy is retained for accounts opened before 2025.

facts.label: Corporate and service entities
facts.value: The site identifies CoinPayments Inc. (Cayman Islands) and custodial/service providers including PaidInSatoshi Inc. (Panama), Centauri Pay LLC (US), and Neutron Ventures Sp. z o.o. (Poland) or their partners.

facts.label: Acquisition, rebrand or ownership change
facts.value: No CoinPayments acquisition or rebrand notice was found in the official News & Insights archive and official blog pages checked.

facts.label: Partner acquisition mentioned in company news
facts.value: A March 2026 CoinPayments post announced an OSL Group partnership and noted OSL acquired Banxa in January 2026; the post does not say CoinPayments acquired or rebranded.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Support tickets, operational support, developer support, onboarding and commercial sales channels are published.

facts.label: Support hours and languages
facts.value: A guaranteed support schedule, service-level response time and full language list were not published on the support pages checked.

facts.label: Operating status
facts.value: Active New merchant platform and API; Classic platform remains for accounts opened before 2025. New platform requires new signup and verification, with separate account data and balances.

facts.label: EU/EEA suspension
facts.value: CoinPayments says it stopped serving EU/EEA clients on 1 July 2026 because of MiCA; account access is paused, and remaining balances are held pending a support claim and identity verification.

facts.label: 2017 XRP incident
facts.value: Company statement: on 5 June 2017 a system error allowed some long-term users to withdraw excess XRP from hot wallets; the company says it was not an external hack and says all losses were reimbursed by December 2017.

facts.label: Corporate/news notices checked
facts.value: Current News & Insights and older blog show ongoing 2025–26 product and partnership announcements; no CoinPayments acquisition or shutdown announcement was found.

facts.label: Contracting entity and jurisdiction
facts.value: Global agreement names CoinPayments Inc. (Cayman Islands) and PaidInSatoshi Inc. (Panama); US agreement names Centauri Pay LLC.

facts.label: US regulatory statements
facts.value: US agreement says Centauri Pay LLC is registered as a FinCEN MSB and states that money-transmission licences are being pursued where applicable; some regulated services use Ram Payment LLC.

facts.label: Earlier Lithuanian VASP registration
facts.value: A 2025 EEA agreement named UAB Star Ventures as notified to the Lithuanian FCIS and listed as a virtual-currency exchange and deposit-wallet operator; it did not state MiCA authorization.

facts.label: Security assurance
facts.value: CoinPayments publishes ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 assurance statements/certificates and a vulnerability-disclosure/bug-bounty policy.

apps.name: Coinremitter

free.text: Free: 8 coins, 100 API requests/min, 500 wallet addresses

cells.payout: Automatic wallet withdrawals every 30 minutes

apps.news: Product pages, merchant signup link, current API docs and company blog are live. The blog had posts through 2026-10-28; its home and announcement category, plus product/legal pages, showed no acquisition, rebrand or service-wide shutdown notice.

facts.label: External account dependency
facts.value: No separate payment processor is required; the merchant needs a Coinremitter account and a destination crypto wallet for withdrawals.

facts.label: Required website
facts.value: Website is needed for many API/plugin uses, but invoice and Payment Page URLs can be shared without a website.

facts.label: Free plan
facts.value: Free plan costs $0 per month and includes BTC, LTC, BCH, DOGE, TCN, DASH, BNB and ZANO; 100 API requests/minute, 500 addresses per wallet and limited-hours support.

facts.label: Premium plan
facts.value: Premium is $99.99 USD per month and adds ETH, USDTERC20, TRX, USDTTRC20 and USDCERC20; 500 API requests/minute, unlimited wallet addresses and 24x7 support.

facts.label: Setup and other fixed charges
facts.value: No separate setup or inactivity fee is published on the plans, fees or terms pages checked. Terms allow account suspension after one year inactive, but state no fee for it.

facts.label: International card cost
facts.value: Not applicable: Coinremitter does not accept card payments.

facts.label: Fiat-to-crypto invoice quote
facts.value: Invoice API can calculate the crypto equivalent of a fiat-denominated amount; it exposes fiat-to-crypto rate information.

facts.label: Conversion spread or quote charge
facts.value: No explicit exchange spread, quote expiry, or separate rate fee is published in the API, fee page or terms checked.

facts.label: Local payment method fees
facts.value: Not applicable: no local bank, wallet, card or cash payment methods are offered.

facts.label: Subscription billing surcharge
facts.value: Not applicable to a documented recurring billing offer; no automatic subscription billing feature is published.

facts.label: Tax/fraud checkout add-ons
facts.value: No tax calculation, collection, filing, or separately priced fraud add-on is described on the terms, fees, or product pages checked.

facts.label: Gas Station
facts.value: Gas Station is a Premium-only option for ETH, USDT, BNB and USDC. The merchant pre-funds its Gas Station balance in the relevant network asset; the amount consumed depends on market gas fees.

facts.label: Merchant refunds
facts.value: Coinremitter terms say it does not offer refunds or chargebacks and fees paid to Coinremitter are non-refundable. A merchant may return funds by a separate outgoing crypto transaction; the official blog says volatility can make the refund amount differ from the original payment.

facts.label: Disputes and chargebacks
facts.value: No card chargeback process exists in this crypto-only gateway. Coinremitter terms say it does not offer chargebacks; its blog tells merchants to handle buyer disagreements directly, review chain/wallet history and publish their own refund policy.

facts.label: BTC withdrawal charges
facts.value: BTC: fixed transaction fee 0.0001 BTC plus 0.23% processing fee. Fees page says these are charged on manual or automatic withdrawal.

facts.label: LTC withdrawal charges
facts.value: LTC: fixed transaction fee 0.01 LTC plus 0.23% processing fee.

facts.label: BCH withdrawal charges
facts.value: BCH: fixed transaction fee 0.01 BCH plus 0.23% processing fee.

facts.label: DOGE withdrawal charges
facts.value: DOGE: fixed transaction fee 7 DOGE plus 0.23% processing fee.

facts.label: TCN withdrawal charges
facts.value: TCN: fixed transaction fee 0.0001 TCN plus 0.23% processing fee in the fee table.

facts.label: DASH withdrawal charges
facts.value: DASH: fixed transaction fee 0.02 DASH plus 0.23% processing fee.

facts.label: ZANO withdrawal charges
facts.value: ZANO: fixed transaction fee 0.2 ZANO plus 0.23% processing fee.

facts.label: BNB withdrawal charges
facts.value: BNB: fixed transaction fee 0.0005 BNB with Gas Station or 0.0008 BNB without it, plus 0.23% processing.

facts.label: ETH withdrawal charges
facts.value: ETH (Premium): fixed transaction fee 0.00006 ETH with Gas Station or 0.0001 ETH without it, plus 0.23% processing.

facts.label: TRX withdrawal charges
facts.value: TRX (Premium): fixed transaction fee 12 TRX plus 0.23% processing.

facts.label: USDT ERC20 withdrawal charges
facts.value: USDTERC20 (Premium): fixed charge is 2 USDT with Gas Station or 5 USDT without it, plus 0.23% processing; the network charge is paid in equivalent ETH.

facts.label: USDT TRC20 withdrawal charges
facts.value: USDTTRC20 (Premium): fixed charge is 2 USDT with Gas Station or 5 USDT without it, plus 0.23% processing; network cost is paid in equivalent TRX.

facts.label: USDC ERC20 withdrawal charges
facts.value: USDCERC20 (Premium): fixed charge is 2 USDC with Gas Station or 3 USDC without it, plus 0.23% processing.

facts.label: Processing fee deduction point
facts.value: The fees page and FAQ say the 0.23% processing fee is charged when funds are withdrawn; the terms say it is deducted from each transaction before settlement.

facts.label: Minimum withdrawal
facts.value: A separate minimum withdrawal amount is not published in the fee chart, terms or current API guide searched.

facts.label: BTC minimum payment
facts.value: Fee chart: 0.00001 BTC. The Bitcoin gateway page separately says minimum payment is 0.0001 BTC.

facts.label: DOGE minimum payment
facts.value: 15 DOGE.

facts.label: ZANO minimum payment
facts.value: 0.5 ZANO.

facts.label: TRX minimum payment
facts.value: 10 TRX.

facts.label: USDT ERC20 minimum payment
facts.value: 4 USDTERC20.

facts.label: USDT TRC20 minimum payment
facts.value: Fee table says 4 USDTTRC20; current coin-specific page says 8 USDT.

facts.label: USDC ERC20 minimum payment
facts.value: 4 USDCERC20.

facts.label: Seller country coverage
facts.value: Coinremitter says it is supported in over 130 countries, but does not publish a complete country-by-country merchant signup allowlist in the terms, FAQ or availability pages checked.

facts.label: Singapore sellers
facts.value: Singapore residents, people located in Singapore, Singapore-incorporated/registered businesses and businesses carrying on business there are excluded by the terms.

facts.label: Other restricted seller countries
facts.value: The terms reserve the right to restrict access where local law or regulatory requirements require it, but the pages checked do not give a complete list beyond Singapore.

facts.label: Eligible business types
facts.value: Terms say services are for businesses selling products or services and registered charitable organizations accepting donations.

facts.label: Sole traders and unregistered individuals
facts.value: Public pages do not settle whether a sole trader or an individual trading without business registration qualifies as a merchant.

facts.label: Age and legal capacity
facts.value: Users must be at least 22 years old and have legal capacity to enter the agreement.

facts.label: Local entity and owner residency
facts.value: No general requirement for local incorporation, owner residency or local business presence outside the Singapore restriction is published.

facts.label: Payout wallet
facts.value: A merchant must connect an external/personal crypto wallet address to withdraw collected funds; a bank account is not listed as a prerequisite.

facts.label: Signup identity check
facts.value: FAQ says account registration needs a verified email and optional phone number, with no ID/KYC submission at signup.

facts.label: Business and beneficial-owner information
facts.value: Current terms ask for the authorized representative's full legal name, business legal name and registration details, contact details and beneficial-owner information; the company reserves the right to verify these details and request more documents.

facts.label: KYC policy consistency
facts.value: Public FAQ says there is no KYC at registration, while the terms and privacy policy authorize identity, business and AML/KYC checks when required.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: A public account registration page is linked from the merchant site.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No minimum revenue, processing volume or payment count is published for standard signup.

facts.label: Supported sale types
facts.value: Terms cover goods, services and registered-charity donations; Payment Page materials also describe product sales, services and fundraising.

facts.label: Exhaustive allowed-product list
facts.value: No full approved-product matrix for software, SaaS, ebooks, courses, memberships or physical goods is published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Prohibited businesses
facts.value: Terms prohibit unlawful/fraudulent activity, scams, MLM/pyramid schemes, unrealistic-return investment schemes, unlicensed gambling, controlled/illegal drugs, weapons trafficking, terrorism and any unlicensed business.

facts.label: Compliance review
facts.value: Coinremitter may request documents and may suspend or terminate an account for restricted activity, unsatisfactory information, unacceptable risk or a legal/regulatory request.

facts.label: Buyer-country list
facts.value: No complete list of buyer countries or buyer-specific blocks is published in the terms, FAQ, supported-currency list or API docs checked.

facts.label: Sanctions and local law
facts.value: Terms prohibit sanctions evasion and unlawful transactions; risk warning says Coinremitter may restrict service in jurisdictions where it is prohibited or subject to extra regulation.

facts.label: Wallet holds, limits and reserves
facts.value: Payments credit an internal Coinremitter wallet, then are withdrawn automatically or manually. Merchants can set a maximum 24-hour withdrawal limit; terms also allow risk-based daily/annual processing limits. No standard reserve percentage or hold duration is published.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: No account, business or compliance approval estimate is published. The 3–5 minute statement on How it Works refers to registration, not review or approval.

facts.label: Provider type and seller role
facts.value: Hosted cryptocurrency payment gateway. Merchant sells its goods, services or charitable donations; Coinremitter acts as limited agent to receive, hold and disburse crypto.

facts.label: Merchant of record
facts.value: Coinremitter does not state that it becomes seller or merchant of record. Its terms identify the account holder as the merchant and call Coinremitter a limited receiving/holding/disbursing agent.

facts.label: Fiat exchange service
facts.value: Coinremitter says it is not an exchange, broker or trading platform and does not buy, sell or exchange crypto for fiat.

facts.label: Invoice denomination
facts.value: API invoices can be denominated in a supported fiat currency, then calculated as the equivalent amount of the selected cryptocurrency.

facts.label: Settlement/charge currency
facts.value: Customers pay in a selected supported cryptocurrency; terms say merchant settlement is exclusively in crypto, not fiat.

facts.label: Supported payment methods
facts.value: Crypto transfer only, using the listed coin or token on its supported network.

facts.label: Card, bank and mobile methods
facts.value: Credit cards, bank payments and other fiat payment methods are not supported by Coinremitter.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time invoices and payment pages/buttons can collect single payments.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Automatic scheduled subscription collection is not documented in the invoice, pricing-widget, API or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Seats, usage billing, trials, discounts, proration, automated plan changes and dunning are not published as Coinremitter billing features.

facts.label: Hosted payment pages and invoices
facts.value: Hosted crypto invoice links and shareable payment pages are available; the seller can also send a link directly without a website.

facts.label: Embedded button/widget
facts.value: Payment Button, Pricing, and Presale widgets provide generated code to place on a seller website.

facts.label: Custom domain and checkout branding
facts.value: Pages describe logo, title, color and template customization, but do not publish a custom-domain checkout option.

facts.label: Developer API
facts.value: Current API documentation covers wallets, addresses, invoices, balances, transactions, withdrawal estimates and withdrawals.

facts.label: Webhooks and callbacks
facts.value: Wallet webhooks and invoice/widget notifications can notify the merchant's URL about payment and withdrawal events.

facts.label: Official integrations
facts.value: Official plugins are offered for WordPress/WooCommerce, Magento 2, OpenCart, Laravel, PHP, Node.js and PrestaShop.

facts.label: Test mode
facts.value: Coinremitter provides Test Coin (TCN) on testnet to run a test integration and payment.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities
facts.value: Coinremitter acts as a payment agent, not the seller or tax authority; public terms do not assign it responsibility to calculate, collect, register, file or remit the merchant's sales taxes.

facts.label: Tax coverage tool
facts.value: Tax calculation, collection, registration and filing features are not published in the product pages checked.

facts.label: Payment receipt
facts.value: Payment Page can email a receipt for successful or overpaid transactions; invoice/API flows also support payment notifications.

facts.label: Tax invoice and business tax IDs
facts.value: No tax invoice, tax-ID collection or tax-exempt purchase feature is documented in the invoice/API pages checked.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: Merchant withdrawals are crypto transfers to an external wallet address; bank, PayPal or fiat payout routes are not offered.

facts.label: Payout account requirements
facts.value: Seller configures a valid external wallet address for the selected asset/network.

facts.label: Balance and payout currencies
facts.value: Coinremitter internal wallets are denominated in supported crypto assets; fiat currencies can be used for invoice pricing but are not held or paid out as fiat. Terms say settlement is exclusively in cryptocurrency.

facts.label: Payout timing and options
facts.value: Automatic withdrawals transfer available funds to the external wallet every 30 minutes until the daily limit is reached. Premium supports manual withdrawal.

facts.label: Product delivery
facts.value: Coinremitter collects payment and sends payment events; digital access, file delivery, memberships and license fulfillment are not part of the documented gateway service.

facts.label: Split payments and marketplace sellers
facts.value: A multi-seller marketplace or split-payout feature is not documented in the terms, API or product pages checked.

facts.label: BTC network
facts.value: Bitcoin (BTC) is supported on Bitcoin Mainnet; offered in the Free plan.

facts.label: LTC network
facts.value: Litecoin (LTC) is supported on Litecoin Mainnet; offered in the Free plan.

facts.label: BCH network
facts.value: Bitcoin Cash (BCH) is supported on Bitcoin Cash Mainnet; offered in the Free plan.

facts.label: DOGE network
facts.value: Dogecoin (DOGE) is supported on Dogecoin Mainnet; offered in the Free plan.

facts.label: TCN network
facts.value: Test Coin (TCN) is supported on Testnet for integration testing; included in Free.

facts.label: DASH network
facts.value: Dash (DASH) is supported on Dash Mainnet; offered in the Free plan.

facts.label: BNB network
facts.value: Binance Coin (BNB) is supported on the Binance Smart Chain/mainnet route; offered in Free.

facts.label: ZANO network
facts.value: Zano (ZANO) is supported on Zano Mainnet; offered in Free.

facts.label: ETH network
facts.value: Ethereum (ETH) is supported on Ethereum Mainnet; Premium only.

facts.label: USDT ERC20 network
facts.value: Tether USD on Ethereum ERC20 (USDTERC20) is supported; Premium only.

facts.label: TRX network
facts.value: Tron (TRX) is supported on Tron Mainnet; Premium only.

facts.label: USDT TRC20 network
facts.value: Tether USD on Tron TRC20 (USDTTRC20) is supported; Premium only.

facts.label: USDC ERC20 network
facts.value: USD Coin on Ethereum ERC20 (USDCERC20) is supported; Premium only.

facts.label: Custody model
facts.value: Coinremitter's terms authorize it to receive, hold and disburse merchant crypto; product setup credits an internal Coinremitter wallet.

facts.label: Withdrawal to merchant wallet
facts.value: Funds can be sent to the merchant's external wallet automatically or by a Premium manual withdrawal setting.

facts.label: Crypto settlement assets
facts.value: Seller settles in the crypto asset received or configured for the wallet; supported assets are listed in C01.

facts.label: Crypto, fiat and stablecoin payout path
facts.value: No fiat bank payout or auto-conversion into another asset is offered. USDT and USDC can be received and sent to external wallets on the listed chains.

facts.label: Payment confirmation
facts.value: API/webhook records show the number of network confirmations and required confirmations; the wallet owner configures webhook confirmations (default 3 per How it Works).

facts.label: Invoice completion states
facts.value: API invoice states include Pending, Paid, Under Paid, Over Paid, Expired and Cancelled; default expiry is 1,440 minutes unless changed. Payments under the published minimum threshold may not appear in the wallet; mismatched networks can cause unrecoverable loss.

facts.label: Crypto refunds
facts.value: Original on-chain payments are irreversible; merchant can return crypto through a separate outgoing transaction, with amount affected by volatility and withdrawal fees.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Coinremitter is a hosted gateway, dashboard, invoice service and API. The merchant does not deploy or maintain Coinremitter server software.

facts.label: Transaction records and retention
facts.value: API can retrieve invoices, wallet transactions and payment histories; Coinremitter says merchants should keep their own records because service data is retained for a limited time. Privacy policy lists transaction records for 2 years, account data for 1 year after closure and logs for 2 years.

facts.label: Exports and provider migration
facts.value: A customer, address or payment-data export format and migration route to another provider are not published in the docs and help pages checked.

facts.label: Merchant closure and inactive balances
facts.value: Merchant may close its account by contacting support; fees are non-refundable. Coinremitter may suspend an account after one year inactive, but gives no deadline for releasing any remaining balance. Privacy policy says account data is retained for 1 year after closure.

facts.label: Current product and name
facts.value: Coinremitter is a hosted crypto payment gateway for merchants, with a merchant dashboard, wallet, APIs, invoices, widgets and plugins.

facts.label: Legal operator
facts.value: The privacy and cookie policies name Coinremitter Pte Ltd. as the company.

facts.label: Operator location
facts.value: Coinremitter Pte Ltd. gives its address as The Central, #18-81, 8 Eu Tong Sen Street, Singapore 059818.

facts.label: Parent, acquisition or former name
facts.value: No parent, acquisition or former product name is identified in the official terms, privacy/cookie policies, current product pages or announcement blog checked.

facts.label: Current service and API status
facts.value: Merchant pages and current API documentation are live. The old API docs state that they were to be discontinued after 2025-06-30, with merchants directed to api.coinremitter.com.

facts.label: Regulator notice
facts.value: MAS added CoinRemitter to its Investor Alert List on 2026-10-09; the record shows coinremitter.com and the Singapore address.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Coinremitter provides a web contact form, email support and tickets; free plan has limited-hours support, while Premium advertises 24x7 support.

facts.label: Acquisition, rebrand or shutdown notices
facts.value: No acquisition, company rebrand or full service-shutdown notice appeared in the current terms, product pages, blog home or announcement category searched.

facts.label: Legal entity and jurisdiction
facts.value: Coinremitter Pte Ltd., Singapore, is named in the site's privacy/cookie policies and its listed address matches the MAS alert record.

facts.label: Licence and regulator entry
facts.value: No licence number or regulatory authorization is stated in the product terms, risk warning or privacy policy. MAS's Investor Alert List contains CoinRemitter; no Coinremitter licence record was identified in the MAS Financial Institutions Directory search.

facts.label: Enforcement action
facts.value: The MAS public entry supplies a listing date and company details, but no penalty, order, allegation or enforcement disposition. No other regulator action against Coinremitter Pte Ltd. was located in the MAS pages searched.

facts.label: Security certification
facts.value: Site markets security controls such as email verification and account protection, but no independently scoped security certification or audit report was found on the product/legal pages checked.

facts.label: Other required accounts
facts.value: A separate card processor is not required for gateway checkout. A merchant business bank account in its own name is required for verification and payout.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Czech Start: gateway setup, monthly service and cancellation are free. Card processing is free up to CZK 50,000 per month during the first six calendar months; this corresponds to a maximum CZK 300,000 if the merchant reaches the cap each month.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Slovak Start: the same six-month introductory period waives gateway monthly charges and card fees up to EUR 2,000 per month; the page advertises the overall six-month cap as EUR 12,000.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Czech Easy and Profi: monthly gateway management is CZK 100, waived when monthly transaction volume is over CZK 100,000; no setup or cancellation charge is listed.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Slovak Easy and Profi: monthly gateway management is EUR 4, waived when monthly volume is over EUR 4,000; setup and cancellation are free.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: The monthly gateway fee is assessed once per merchant business ID even if the business has several gateway shops; volume across gateway and terminals can count toward the waiver.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Start switches to Easy from month seven. Above the Start monthly card-free threshold and on its other listed payment methods, the stated flat fee is 1% + CZK 0 in Czechia or 1% + EUR 0 in Slovakia, with method-specific local-currency exceptions.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Custom pricing is individually quoted above CZK 3 million/month in Czechia or EUR 120,000/month in Slovakia; no public custom fixed fee is shown.

facts.label: Fixed costs and free plan
facts.value: Current terms say Comgate’s provider fees do not include VAT (DPH). Treat each listed gateway price as exclusive of VAT, not VAT-inclusive.

facts.label: International card cost
facts.value: Card acceptance for cards issued outside the EEA requires approval; no additional universal cross-border-card markup is stated beyond plan card rate and the 0.15% non-domestic-currency surcharge.

facts.label: Currency conversion cost
facts.value: Comgate adds 0.15% for card payments in a currency other than the merchant’s domestic currency.

facts.label: Currency conversion cost
facts.value: When a buyer’s card account uses a different currency from the checkout currency, the buyer’s issuing bank performs conversion at its own current rate; the pages do not publish a Comgate FX spread or benchmark rate.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Czech Start and Easy: Czech, Slovak and Polish bank transfers, Czech meal/benefit cards and listed deferred/instalment options are generally 1% + CZK 0, except methods whose schedule uses EUR or PLN.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Czech Profi bank transfers: Czechia 0.62% + CZK 0; Slovakia 0.62% + EUR 0; Poland 1.16% + PLN 0.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Slovak Start/Easy: bank transfers in Slovakia, Czechia and Poland are 1% + EUR 0 on the Slovak Start/Easy list; the listed Polish Twisto methods use PLN 0 fixed amount.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Slovak Profi bank transfers: Slovakia 0.62% + EUR 0; Czechia 0.62% + CZK 0; Poland 1.16% + PLN 0.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Czech Profi deferred methods Twisto, Skip Pay and PlatímPak: 0.4% + CZK 0; Twisto, Skip Pay and ESSOX three-part payments: 1.9% + CZK 0; Cofidis/ESSOX/Home Credit instalments: 0% + CZK 0.
