facts.value: Slovak Profi: Skip Pay three-part payment is 3.3% + EUR 0; Tatra banka instalments are 0% + EUR 0.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Polish Profi Twisto deferred payment is 0.8% + PLN 0; Twisto three-part payments are 1.9% + PLN 0.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: Czech Profi meal/benefit cards: Edenred and Chèque Déjeuner/Up are 1.6% + CZK 1; Lidl Naše stravenka is 2.9% + CZK 1; Benefit Plus is 5.5% + CZK 1.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: No one fee is published for every individual bank, wallet or QR option; methods and account fees depend on the enabled payment market and selected tariff.

facts.label: Subscription and billing surcharge
facts.value: Recurring card charges use the selected card transaction tariff; no separate recurring-billing percentage is listed.

facts.label: Subscription and billing surcharge
facts.value: Seat, usage or invoice billing charges are not described in the gateway’s subscription documentation.

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons
facts.value: The gateway price pages do not advertise tax calculation, tax filing or tax-remittance services.

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons
facts.value: Optional gateway extras include a 3-D Secure bypass (CZK 0.30 in the Czech tariff; EUR 0.01 in the Slovak tariff), and merchant hotel-portal card processing at listed separate rates.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: A refund costs CZK 5 per individual refund on the Czech tariff or EUR 0.20 on the Slovak tariff; full and partial refunds are supported.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: Card and deferred-method refunds must go through Comgate; bank-button, QR and PSD2 payments may be refunded directly by the merchant to the payer’s bank account.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: Refund processing needs sufficient later payment volume or funds in the merchant’s virtual account; otherwise money may be held while the refund is pending, and a request can expire after 14 working days.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: The public pages do not state generally whether the original transaction fee is credited back when a payment is refunded.

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility
facts.value: A card chargeback costs CZK 990 under the Czech fee schedule or EUR 40 on the Slovak schedule.

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility
facts.value: The customer’s card bank initiates a chargeback. The merchant bears the transaction loss, chargeback consequences and requested sales/delivery evidence; Comgate may deduct chargebacks, penalties and related liabilities from payouts or other amounts it owes.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Standard payout to a CZK bank account in Czechia and EUR bank account in the EU is listed as free in the Czech and Slovak schedules.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Optional Czech payout charges: CZK 30 for CZK transfer to a bank outside Czechia; CZK 100 for payout to accounts in PLN, HUF, USD, GBP, RON, NOK or SEK.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Optional Slovak schedule charges: CZK 30 for CZK payout to a bank outside Czechia; EUR 4 for payouts in PLN, HUF, USD, GBP, RON, NOK or SEK.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Daily, weekly and monthly payout cycles are free to select. Optional 100% payout (send gross and invoice fees monthly) adds 0.1% to transaction fees under Profi.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: The pages do not state the receiving bank’s intermediary or incoming transfer charges.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No universal minimum merchant payout amount is stated in the payout help or current gateway prices.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: The published minimum gateway payment amounts are CZK 1, EUR 0.10, PLN 1, HUF 100, USD 1, GBP 1 and RON 5.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: A general maximum transaction amount or merchant account collection cap is not published; the seller may not impose card-payment minimums or maximums under the terms.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: Some buyer financing methods publish individual limits: e.g., Czech Skip Pay three-part payments CZK 1,000–60,000; Slovak Skip Pay EUR 30–3,000; Czech ESSOX split CZK 2,000–30,000; Czech Cofidis instalment CZK 2,000–50,000.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: The default payment link expiry is seven days and can be set from 30 minutes to seven days; this is a time limit, not a charge limit.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Comgate says it contracts with businesses based in Czechia and Slovakia.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Applicants based elsewhere receive individual assessment; Comgate does not publish a complete list of other accepted seller countries.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: The Slovak onboarding form accepts a company or trade/business name and business ID. This supports registered companies and registered sole-trader businesses applying in a business capacity.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Comgate does not say that an unregistered individual acting only as a private person can open a merchant gateway account; foreign legal-form acceptance is case-reviewed.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Onboarding requests a business account for payouts and a small identification transfer from that account: CZK 1 or EUR 0.10, returned after verification.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: A foreign business is assessed individually. To activate a foreign settlement currency, the merchant must supply a bank statement for an account able to receive that currency.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Contract onboarding requires business name, registration ID, address, contacts, payout account, business activity, shop URL and developer details.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: The seller’s site must show legal name, registered address and business ID, contact details, products and prices, order flow, terms, complaints/refunds, privacy policy, delivery/payment terms and HTTPS.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Comgate says two identity documents and proof of ownership of the payout account are needed; its Czech page also describes a returned identification payment.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: The public pages do not give one document checklist for every foreign country or legal form.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Signup begins with an inquiry and online contract; Comgate’s team follows up and guides the setup. It is not immediate self-serve activation.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Start is for merchants without prior card-acceptance history. Custom is marketed for monthly processing above CZK 3 million in Czechia or EUR 120,000 in Slovakia.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: No general minimum revenue or company-age requirement for ordinary gateway applicants was stated.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: The gateway is for businesses taking online payment for their own goods or services. Ordinary physical-goods stores and services fit the stated core use, subject to review.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Digital products, software licences, online courses and SaaS are not each given a simple blanket approval in the public onboarding pages; the restricted-business list still applies.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Web hosting, remote-server rental, free website hosting and certain internet/data/telecom services are listed as prohibited card-payment activities.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Comgate’s prohibited list includes marketplaces processing other sellers’ goods, crypto exchanges/wallets/mining/ICOs, gambling, pornography/erotic webcam services, adult services, exchange offices, real-estate agents, alcohol, e-cigarettes, drugs, most weapons and illegal activity. Terms also prohibit processing transactions for another business or for a transaction unrelated to the approved shop.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Some sectors are high-risk rather than automatically prohibited. Comgate requires special review and may impose different terms; examples include travel, pharmacies, accommodation and financial services.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Club/group memberships and some recurring memberships are named as high-risk; a recurring card feature does not mean every membership model is accepted.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Buyer card-issuing countries are configured for each merchant. Only cards issued in the merchant’s allowed countries can be used; support may extend the list.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Card acceptance for cards issued outside the EEA requires approval. Local bank-transfer and instalment methods are market-specific, especially Czechia, Slovakia and Poland.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: A complete public country-by-country buyer acceptance matrix is not published outside merchant-specific settings.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Terms permit Comgate to temporarily hold transaction payouts where fraud or a possible refund, scheme fine or related investigation is suspected; release depends on investigation and authorities where involved.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: Comgate’s migration blog says card-acquirer approval may take about 14 days after the gateway begins live operation; this is an estimate in a blog guide, not a service guarantee.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: No guaranteed review time for identity, business, website or foreign-seller approval is stated.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Comgate is a licensed payment institution and gateway. The merchant contracts to sell its own goods or services to the payer; Comgate routes and settles payment.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Deferred-payment and instalment offers are supplied by named external providers through the gateway. Those providers set the buyer credit contract; Comgate pays the merchant under the gateway schedule.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Gateway checkout supports CZK, EUR, PLN, HUF, USD, GBP, RON, NOK and SEK. A foreign currency must be requested and approved.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: The currency used for a payment must have an enabled method for the applicable market. Czech bank methods use CZK, Slovak methods use EUR, and Polish buttons use PLN in the published settlement tables.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Card checkout accepts Visa, Visa Electron, Mastercard and Maestro; Apple Pay and Google Pay use cards stored in those wallets.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Bank methods include PSD2/open-banking payment initiation, online bank buttons, QR transfer and bank transfer without instant confirmation; Polish BLIK is listed with bank transfers.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Czech deferred methods include Twisto, Skip Pay and PlatímPak; Czech instalments include Twisto, Skip Pay, ESSOX, Cofidis and Home Credit, with the method type and plan varying by provider.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Slovak methods include bank transfers, Tatra banka instalments and Skip Pay three-part payments. Poland has bank buttons/BLIK and Twisto deferred or three-part payments.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: The general help-method page also lists PayPal, but current 2026 Start/Easy/Profi gateway price pages do not list a PayPal fee or confirm merchant availability.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time checkout for a single order is the gateway’s core use.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Automatic repeat charges are supported for card payments after Comgate approves and activates the feature. Apple Pay/Google Pay do not provide card expiry data for this feature.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: The Client Portal can create a recurring series after customer consent, without an integration change. Repeating the initial payment is the documented manual flow.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Public docs do not identify recurring availability for every card wallet, charge currency or seller market; recurrent use is not described for bank transfers or BNPL.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Comgate provides card-on-file recurring collection, variable repeat amounts, manual/API entry and customer payment-status emails.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Public docs do not describe native seat/usage billing, trial management, proration, plan changes, coupons or a subscription dunning suite.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: If a customer’s card changes, the merchant creates and obtains consent for a new initial recurring payment.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Comgate offers a hosted payment gateway reached by redirect, an embedded gateway presentation, a Checkout SDK for card/Apple Pay/Google Pay, and mobile-app SDK integration.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Payment links can be created in the merchant portal for email, chat, phone or edited orders; they can also start a recurring or pre-authorisation payment.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Checkout branding can be adjusted with the merchant logo/background; a custom checkout domain was not stated in the integration pages checked.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Custom shops integrate through the API; Comgate publishes cURL, PHP, Java and Python examples plus API documentation.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Comgate Checkout SDK supports card, Apple Pay and Google Pay within the cart. It also documents native Android and iOS app SDKs.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: The gateway reports changed payment status by server notification and supports return URLs; the merchant should verify status server-side. Test mode uses a test parameter and simulated bank/provider; the portal includes test payments, communication logs and error information.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Official plugins and setup guides cover more than 100 commerce platforms; open-source packages are also listed.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: The seller supplies the goods/services, controls its shop prices and is responsible for its merchant obligations. Comgate sells payment acceptance and is not the merchant of record.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: No Comgate tax calculation, registration, tax-return filing or remittance coverage matrix is published.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Comgate sends payer email notifications for payment status, successful payment, reminders and cancellations; sellers can configure notification settings.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Seller billing exports and invoices for Comgate fees are available in the merchant portal. A buyer invoice/tax-invoice generator, VAT-ID collection or tax-exempt workflow is not described.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: The payout method documented for gateway proceeds is transfer to a verified bank account; it must support the selected payout currency. Public pages reviewed do not establish another payout channel.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Gateway checkout supports CZK, EUR, PLN, HUF, USD, GBP, RON, NOK and SEK; each foreign currency must be enabled using proof of a receiving account. The public portal guide shows standard pre-set payout accounts for CZK and EUR; other account currencies require setup and approval.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Daily is the default gateway schedule. Funds are sent each working day after Comgate receives them; actual transfer timing depends on method and payment time.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Daily card settlement: Visa CZK D+2, Visa EUR D+1; Mastercard CZK and EUR D+1.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Daily bank settlement: Czech QR/offline/buttons paid by 14:00 are D+1 and later payments D+2; Slovak EUR transfers follow the same cutoff; Polish buttons are D+2/D+3.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Deferred and instalment methods settle D+1 when received by 14:00 or D+2 later that day, under the daily schedule.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Merchants can choose daily, weekly or monthly cycles. Weekly funds received Monday–Sunday are paid the following Monday; monthly funds are sent the first business day of the next month.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Optional simplified daily payout groups all of a day’s payments: CZK D+2, EUR D+1, PLN and other currencies D+3.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: Comgate reports payment status and supports merchant APIs and platform integrations, but no digital-product delivery, licence-key, course-access or membership provisioning service was found.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: The gateway does not offer a documented marketplace/split-settlement product; terms prohibit the merchant from processing transactions on behalf of third parties.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: Comgate is a card/bank-payment gateway, not a crypto checkout provider; its policy prohibits crypto exchanges, crypto wallets, mining and ICO activity.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto checkout or crypto balance/custody service is offered in the reviewed gateway product.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: Not applicable: Comgate publishes fiat payment and bank payout currencies, but no crypto-to-fiat or crypto payout path.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto payment network, confirmation or crypto refund method is offered.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: no self-hosted or hosted crypto processor/software is offered. The gateway itself is a hosted online service.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Merchant transaction and settlement statements can be downloaded in CSV, ABO and PDF or retrieved through API; daily/monthly exports and accounting integrations are described.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Public docs do not state that stored card tokens or recurring credentials can be exported to another processor.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: The service contract is indefinite. Either side can terminate by notice with a two-month notice period, starting on the first day of the month after notice is received; the public contract says no cancellation penalty or fee.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Remaining funds continue under ordinary settlement rules, but suspicious transactions, chargebacks or unpaid merchant obligations can be withheld or offset. A public fixed post-closure release time is not stated.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: The contracting operator is Comgate a.s., formerly ComGate Payments, a.s.; the company report records the name change on 18 January 2024.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Comgate a.s. is 100% owned by CGX a.s., according to Comgate’s 2024 annual report.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Czech contact channels are email, phone, online chat and support portal; published hours are weekdays 08:00–20:00.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Slovak help/contact pages publish the local email and phone support route, also weekdays 08:00–20:00. The company does not give a guaranteed response time.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: The Czech site currently advertises online gateway pricing, onboarding, active API/help pages and current 2026 tariffs.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Comgate a.s. is a Czech licensed payment institution supervised by the Czech National Bank, with authority to provide payment services across the EU. It says it became a Visa and Mastercard acquirer in 2024 and is a direct card-scheme member.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Comgate states it annually renews PCI DSS Level 1 certification. The public pages checked did not provide a certificate number or current expiry date.

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility

facts.label: Business verification

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size

facts.label: Supported product types

facts.label: Required external accounts
facts.value: No separate payment processor or provider account is required; a merchant needs its own destination wallet and a callback endpoint for custom integration.

facts.label: Callback-domain requirement
facts.value: Custom API addresses require a verified callback domain. Plugin callbacks use the store domain, which also needs verification.

facts.label: Setup and monthly fees
facts.value: CryptAPI publishes no setup or monthly fee for the standard API or plugins.

facts.label: Volume measurement and effective date
facts.value: The rate uses total volume from the previous 30 days. The current tier table took effect November 1, 2026.

facts.value: Under $250,000 of prior-30-day volume: 1.00% per payment.

facts.label: Processing tier $250,000–$999,999
facts.value: $250,000 to $999,999 of prior-30-day volume: 0.90% per payment.

facts.label: Processing tier $1,000,000–$2,499,999
facts.value: $1,000,000 to $2,499,999 of prior-30-day volume: 0.80% per payment.

facts.label: Processing tier $2,500,000–$4,999,999
facts.value: $2,500,000 to $4,999,999 of prior-30-day volume: 0.70% per payment.

facts.label: Processing tier $5,000,000–$9,999,999
facts.value: $5,000,000 to $9,999,999 of prior-30-day volume: 0.60% per payment.

facts.label: Processing tier $10,000,000–$19,999,999
facts.value: $10,000,000 to $19,999,999 of prior-30-day volume: 0.40% per payment.

facts.label: International card surcharge
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no card-issued-country pricing schedule for this product.

facts.label: Fiat price conversion
facts.value: The API converts between listed fiat currencies and supported crypto at a rate refreshed every five minutes; WooCommerce uses it to quote the order in crypto.

facts.label: Exchange spread or conversion fee
facts.value: No separate quote spread or exchange add-on is listed; CryptAPI says it does not exchange received crypto into fiat or another coin.

facts.label: Automatic fiat settlement
facts.value: A bank payout or conversion of crypto proceeds into fiat is not offered in the public API flow.

facts.label: Local payment-method costs
facts.value: Not applicable: local bank, card, wallet and cash payment methods are not offered.

facts.label: Recurring-payment surcharge
facts.value: A separate recurring-payment percentage or fixed fee is not published.

facts.label: Tax, fraud or checkout add-ons
facts.value: No tax-calculation, filing or separately priced fraud add-on is described in the fees, product or legal pages checked.

facts.label: Gas and network priority
facts.value: The create endpoint supports network priority only for Bitcoin, Ethereum/ERC-20 and Litecoin; higher network fees may affect forwarding speed.

facts.label: Provider refund and reversal
facts.value: CryptAPI terms say crypto transfers are final and that CryptAPI cannot cancel, reverse or refund a completed cryptocurrency transaction.

facts.label: Merchant-issued refund process
facts.value: A merchant can choose to send a separate transfer from its own wallet, but CryptAPI does not document a refund workflow or refund fee schedule.

facts.label: Disputes and chargebacks
facts.value: CryptAPI does not offer chargebacks; the merchant is responsible for customer disputes and any voluntary return transfer.

facts.label: Processing fee and deduction
facts.value: The current schedule deducts 1.00% to 0.25% according to prior-30-day USD volume; fees are withheld from the crypto forwarded to the merchant.

facts.label: Blockchain forwarding fee
facts.value: A separate blockchain/network fee applies for forwarding each transaction; the supported-asset matrix shows a daily estimate per ticker and the fee estimator can recalculate it.

facts.label: Minimum service-fee wording
facts.value: The home, plugin and fee FAQ mention a minimum fee for BTC, BCH and LTC; current API information says there is no minimum service fee, while the asset matrix shows minimum payment and network-fee data.

facts.label: Separate payout fee
facts.value: There is no bank or exchange payout step in the standard product; the only published transfer cost is the blockchain fee for forwarding to wallet address(es).

facts.label: Minimum payout balance
facts.value: Not applicable to a standard payment: funds are forwarded transaction by transaction after confirmation, rather than accumulated in a CryptAPI payout balance.

facts.label: Minimum incoming payment
facts.value: The minimum payment differs by asset and network; CryptAPI ignores payments below its listed threshold, and the full current values are recorded by ticker in C01.

facts.label: Minimums for multi-address splits
facts.value: When splitting to N outputs, the minimum is multiplied by 1 + (N - 1) / 3; the API supports up to 20 addresses.

facts.label: Seller-country availability
facts.value: The product is marketed globally, but CryptAPI does not publish a complete seller-country allowlist in its terms, API docs or country pages checked.

facts.label: Restricted seller and transaction locations
facts.value: The terms name Iran, Syria, North Korea, Cuba, Belarus, Russia, Crimea including Sevastopol, and the Donetsk and Luhansk regions; they say access will be blocked when discovered.

facts.label: Other country limits
facts.value: The terms also reserve restrictions when local law or regulatory requirements require them, without listing additional countries.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Standard API use does not require an account, but the terms do not clearly say whether unregistered individuals or sole traders may use every feature.

facts.label: Local bank and payout account
facts.value: No bank account or separate payout account is required for the standard crypto flow; the merchant supplies a wallet address for each asset/network.

facts.label: Seller residency or local registration
facts.value: No seller-residency or local-incorporation checklist is published for the no-account API.

facts.label: Account and API key for standard API use
facts.value: CryptAPI says there is no registration, account or API key required to create payment addresses with the standard API or plugins.

facts.label: KYC and KYB policy
facts.value: The no-account pages say no sign-up is needed, while the privacy policy says KYC/KYB is mandatory at account creation and terms allow later identity checks.

facts.label: Risk-triggered documents
facts.value: Terms permit CryptAPI to request information or documents and perform additional due diligence when transaction monitoring flags potential risk.

facts.label: Callback-domain verification
facts.value: A merchant must verify the host used in callback URLs, once, by DNS TXT record or a specific HTTPS file; there is no account for this step.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Open API access is self-service and does not require a signup or sales approval; a callback domain must be verified before address creation.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No minimum revenue, processing volume or company size is stated for standard API use.

facts.label: Supported seller products
facts.value: The terms describe accepting crypto for websites selling goods or services; they do not provide a full approved-product list.

facts.label: Physical and digital fulfillment
facts.value: WooCommerce documentation includes virtual-product order handling; the merchant store, not CryptAPI, supplies the item or digital access.

facts.label: Prohibited business categories
facts.value: Terms prohibit pornography and sexual services, unlawful gambling, illegal drugs, counterfeit or stolen goods, and other illegal or deceptive activity.

facts.label: Compliance and sanctions restrictions
facts.value: Terms allow blocking activity involving sanctioned persons or restricted locations and allow rejection, suspension or delay of suspicious transactions.

facts.label: Buyer-country coverage
facts.value: The API supports crypto transactions without a published buyer-country or buyer-payment-method matrix.

facts.label: Restricted customer activity
facts.value: The terms restrict business or transfers connected to the places listed in F03 and reserve action on transactions subject to sanctions or law.

facts.label: Transaction review and delay
facts.value: Terms permit CryptAPI to hold, delay, reject or cancel a pending forwarding when law, sanctions, technology or suspicious-activity review requires it.

facts.label: Public reserve policy
facts.value: A standard reserve schedule, rolling reserve or fixed hold period is not published.

facts.label: Approval time
facts.value: There is no public business-approval estimate for the account-free API; the docs do not promise a time for domain verification or DNS propagation.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: CryptAPI describes itself as a cryptocurrency payment gateway and API; it is not described as a merchant-of-record or subscription-billing service.

facts.label: Seller to the buyer
facts.value: The merchant sells to the buyer, sets the price and fulfills the order; CryptAPI creates the payment address, forwards crypto and sends payment notifications.

facts.label: Merchant of record
facts.value: CryptAPI does not publish a merchant-of-record offer; the public flow identifies the merchant as the seller.

facts.label: Customer payment currencies
facts.value: Customers pay in the selected supported cryptocurrency or token; fiat currency is used to quote a crypto amount, not as a payment rail.

facts.label: Fiat quote and display currencies
facts.value: The quote API lists USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, JPY, AED, MYR, IDR, THB, CHF, SGD, RUB, ZAR, TRY, LKR, RON, BGN, HUF, CZK, PHP, PLN, UGX, MXN, INR, HKD, CNY, BRL, DKK, TWD, AUD, NGN, SEK, NOK, UAH and VND.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Cryptocurrency payments are the only published method; no bank transfer, card, cash or local wallet rails are offered in the standard product.

facts.label: Cards and alternative local methods
facts.value: Card and local payment-method pricing is not applicable because the product accepts crypto assets and tokens.

facts.label: One-time payment support
facts.value: The create-address API and plugins support individual customer payments to a merchant wallet.

facts.label: Recurring payment integration
facts.value: The WooCommerce plugin changelog says it added support for the WooCommerce Subscriptions plugin.

facts.label: Renewal collection mechanics
facts.value: Current public docs do not explain automatic recurring collection, renewal retries, supported renewal intervals or whether a buyer must initiate each crypto payment.

facts.label: Subscription billing tools
facts.value: Seats, usage metering, trials, coupons, proration, dunning and failed-payment recovery are not described as CryptAPI billing features.

facts.label: Order state and repeat payments
facts.value: The API sends pending and confirmed payment events; stores must apply their own order and renewal rules.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: The product does not document a CryptAPI-hosted checkout; its API returns a payment address for the seller to show in its own flow.

facts.label: Payment links and QR codes
facts.value: The API creates a payment address and QR code for a seller to display or share; a public hosted link service is not documented.

facts.label: Checkout and theme options
facts.value: WooCommerce offers configurable payment-method wording and selected coins; custom checkout styling remains merchant-controlled.

facts.label: API and libraries
facts.value: Public API documentation covers address creation, conversion, QR codes, logs, estimates and service information; official libraries are listed for PHP, Python, Node.js and Django.

facts.label: Callbacks and webhooks
facts.value: Callbacks can report pending and confirmed events, include transaction IDs and fee/value fields, and use GET or POST/JSON options.

facts.label: Official e-commerce plugins
facts.value: Official plugin docs cover WooCommerce, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop and WHMCS.

facts.label: Test mode and sandbox
facts.value: No testnet sandbox is documented for production CryptAPI payments; the official test guide shows a small live payment on a verified domain.

facts.label: API version and compatibility notice
facts.value: The current API docs use api.cryptapi.io; the official blog says older integration notes had an upcoming API URL change and the current docs use the API host.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities
facts.value: The merchant is the seller; CryptAPI does not publish sales-tax calculation, collection, registration, filing or remittance features.

facts.label: Tax scope and jurisdiction
facts.value: No country-by-country tax coverage or tax advice is published for CryptAPI.

facts.label: Payment receipts and records
facts.value: Callbacks and the logs endpoint expose payment values, transaction IDs, forwarding values and status; optional email alerts require address verification.

facts.label: Tax invoices and buyer tax IDs
facts.value: No tax invoice generation, VAT/GST ID collection or tax-exempt checkout is described in the invoice/API documentation checked.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: CryptAPI forwards crypto to the wallet address supplied by the merchant; bank payout, PayPal and fiat wallet payout are not offered in the standard product.

facts.label: Multiple payout addresses
facts.value: The API can divide one payment across up to 20 output addresses using a seller-specified percentage split.

facts.label: Balance and payout currency
facts.value: Payouts remain in the selected cryptocurrency/token and network; CryptAPI does not state that it holds a fiat balance for the merchant.

facts.label: Fiat bank settlement currencies
facts.value: No fiat bank-settlement currencies or bank payout method are published.

facts.label: Forwarding trigger
facts.value: CryptAPI forwards after the payment reaches the requested confirmation count; the callback can report an earlier pending transaction when enabled.

facts.label: Time to confirmation and wallet receipt
facts.value: Exact receipt time depends on the asset network and congestion. WooCommerce docs give typical examples of BTC up to 11 minutes and ETH under one minute; these are not service guarantees.

facts.label: Digital delivery
facts.value: CryptAPI does not host downloads, software licences, memberships or course access; the seller's store controls fulfillment after the payment callback.

facts.label: Receipt and order workflow
facts.value: The WooCommerce plugin updates the store order from payment callbacks; a separate customer delivery platform is not required by CryptAPI itself.

facts.label: Multi-address splitting
facts.value: One payment can be divided among up to 20 destination addresses with specified percentages.

facts.label: Marketplace seller onboarding
facts.value: A marketplace account, connected submerchant onboarding or identity-separated seller payouts are not documented.

facts.label: Custody model
facts.value: CryptAPI says it is non-custodial and does not maintain crypto balances for users; it generates an incoming address and forwards confirmed funds to the user-supplied wallet.

facts.label: Control of destination
facts.value: The merchant selects the destination wallet address; changing the destination for an existing callback/address requires creating a different callback URL.

facts.label: Crypto settlement path
facts.value: After confirmation, the same asset is forwarded to the merchant wallet, minus the service percentage and blockchain forwarding cost.

facts.label: Conversion, stablecoins and fiat
facts.value: No exchange of proceeds into fiat or another asset is offered; convert=1 adds a fiat-equivalent value to the callback only.

facts.label: Payment status and confirmations
facts.value: Callbacks can report pending when first seen and confirmed after the requested blockchain confirmations; the minimum confirmation parameter is one.

facts.label: Under-minimum payments
facts.value: Payments below the ticker minimum are ignored and the funds are not recoverable through CryptAPI.

facts.label: Partial payments and overpayments
facts.value: The WooCommerce plugin changelog says it added partial-payment handling and a payment tolerance option; the exact current tolerance setting depends on plugin configuration.

facts.label: Wrong token or wrong network
facts.value: A payment sent in an unsupported token/network combination may be ignored or stuck; terms disclaim recovery for wrong or delisted chains.

facts.label: Refunds and reversals
facts.value: Blockchain transfers are final; CryptAPI has no reversal or refund facility. Any voluntary merchant refund is a separate wallet transfer, and CryptAPI publishes no refund workflow.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: CryptAPI hosts the payment API and address-forwarding service; plugin users install and maintain their own commerce store, and custom users maintain callback infrastructure and wallets.

facts.label: Transaction history lookup
facts.value: The logs API can retrieve payment callbacks by callback URL, including transaction IDs, values, confirmations and status.

facts.label: Bulk export and data retention
facts.value: A bulk export/migration facility and a fixed retention period for transaction logs are not published.

facts.label: Account cancellation
facts.value: No standard API account exists to cancel; a merchant can stop creating addresses and stop using its own callback integration.

facts.label: Data deletion and post-use records
facts.value: The privacy policy gives data-rights contact details but does not publish a universal post-use deletion deadline for callback or transaction records.

facts.label: Current product and name
facts.value: CryptAPI is a crypto payment API and set of e-commerce plugins. Its API creates a payment address, then forwards a confirmed payment to the merchant's wallet.

facts.label: Legal operator
facts.value: The current terms and About page identify CryptAPI Inc. as the operator.

facts.label: Operator country and address

facts.label: Parent, acquisition or rebrand
facts.value: The official About page, terms, blog, press page and changelog do not name a parent or announce an acquisition or rebrand.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: CryptAPI publishes support through its contact page, contact form and live chat; the help center provides setup guides.

facts.label: Support hours and language
facts.value: Support hours and a complete list of support languages are not published in the contact and help pages checked.

facts.label: Current operation and announcements
facts.value: The product site, API docs, blog and changelog are live; the latest blog post found was the October 20, 2026 fee-tier update.

facts.label: Product and network changes

facts.label: Legal operator
facts.value: CryptAPI Inc. is named in the current terms and privacy policy as the operator, registered in Panama.

facts.label: Published financial licence
facts.value: CryptAPI does not state a financial licence number or regulated-service authorization in its terms, About page or privacy policy.

facts.label: Panama regulator notices

facts.label: Merchant account dependency
facts.value: Direct checkout requires a Crypto.com Pay merchant account with generated keys; merchants do not have to replace existing gateways.

facts.label: Buyer account dependency
facts.value: Crypto.com App checkout requires a Crypto.com App account; on-chain payment can use an external wallet.

facts.label: Transaction fee
facts.value: Merchant API docs state that Crypto.com Pay for Business has no transaction fee.

facts.label: Payout fee existence
facts.value: Pay charges a fee for all merchant payout settlements.

facts.label: Payout fee amount
facts.value: The actual payout fee is shown only in the Merchant Dashboard payout page; no general amount or schedule is public.

facts.label: Setup and monthly cost
facts.value: No general setup, monthly, or inactivity fee was published on the merchant product, API fee, signup FAQ, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: International card fee
facts.value: No merchant international-card surcharge is published for the direct merchant service; the on-ramp page gives no separate international card markup.

facts.label: Buyer crypto conversion
facts.value: When the buyer chooses a crypto asset different from the pricing currency, Pay quotes a market-rate conversion at payment time and says it charges no additional Pay conversion fee.

facts.label: Merchant balance conversion
facts.value: Merchants can enable credit to a default wallet currency; the help page says Pay converts at the market rate at payment time without an additional Pay conversion fee.

facts.label: Network fees
facts.value: Buyers using external wallets pay blockchain network fees; refunds and small crypto settlements may also incur network fees.

facts.label: Local payment method pricing
facts.value: Not applicable to direct merchant checkout methods, which are Crypto.com App or supported crypto wallets rather than local bank methods.

facts.label: Subscription surcharge
facts.value: No separate subscription billing surcharge is published; the API states no transaction fee, while contract-specific terms remain in the commercial agreement.

facts.label: Tax calculation service
facts.value: Pay does not promise to calculate, collect, file, or remit seller sales tax; the seller is responsible for tax duties.

facts.label: Tax/fraud add-on price
facts.value: No separate tax, fraud-screening, or risk add-on rate is published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Refund flow
facts.value: Merchants can issue full or partial refunds from the dashboard; App payments return to the customer’s App, and on-chain refunds use a customer-provided wallet/claim flow.

facts.label: Refund amount and currency
facts.value: Refunds are crypto and target the same value in the original pricing currency, using the rate at refund time; the crypto amount can therefore differ from the payment amount.

facts.label: Refund fees
facts.value: No standard refund processing fee is published; applicable blockchain network fees may be deducted, and bank/issuer charges can affect received value.

facts.label: Dispute responsibility
facts.value: Merchant is responsible for customer support, sales, delivery, and refunds; Crypto.com can debit a refunded or disputed amount from the account or seek reimbursement.

facts.label: Crypto transaction reversals
facts.value: Confirmed crypto payments do not have a card issuer chargeback route in the documented checkout; terms still allow Pay to reverse, freeze, or withhold for legal, fraud, risk, or complaint reasons.

facts.label: Dispute fee
facts.value: A fixed dispute or chargeback fee for direct crypto checkout was not found in the merchant terms or fee documentation checked.

facts.label: Merchant payout fee
facts.value: A payout fee applies to every settlement request; its standard amount is visible only in the account dashboard.

facts.label: Fiat intermediary charge
facts.value: Correspondent/intermediary bank transmittance charges may apply to fiat payouts and are outside Crypto.com’s control.

facts.label: Crypto payout network charge
facts.value: Small crypto settlements may incur a minimum blockchain fee; exact payout charge is shown in the dashboard.

facts.label: Fiat payout minimums
facts.value: Minimum settlement amounts are USD 100, EUR 130, AUD 150, GBP 100, and AED 300.

facts.label: Crypto payout minimums
facts.value: Minimum settlement amounts are BTC 0.01, ETH 0.1, CRO 500, and USDC 100.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: API docs point to per-currency minimum pricing in the dashboard and show daily/annual amount-limit errors, but public docs give no numeric limits.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Crypto.com does not publish a complete country list for businesses that can open a direct Pay for Business merchant account.

facts.label: Country-specific UAE checkout
facts.value: The UAE launch allows eligible UAE-resident customers to pay Dubai Duty Free; the merchant receives AED.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Public merchant onboarding and terms do not state whether sole traders, unincorporated individuals, or each company form are accepted by country.

facts.label: Local bank requirements
facts.value: Fiat payouts go to a seller’s bank account; EUR payout requires a bank account in a SEPA country. Other fiat currencies are said to reach most international banks through partners, subject to intermediary fees.

facts.label: Local presence and entity accounts
facts.value: Sellers must comply with local law and cannot use Pay where the service is restricted or unlawful; each separate legal business entity needs its own account.

facts.label: Multiple legal entities
facts.value: Merchants with separate legal business entities must open separate Pay accounts; businesses under one company may share one account.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Merchants must register and pass review; live mode is enabled only for KYC-approved accounts.

facts.label: Verification documents
facts.value: Terms say Crypto.com may request ultimate beneficial owner and senior-management identity information, tax ID, government ID, and further risk or identity evidence.

facts.label: Sales-channel review
facts.value: Sellers must identify sales channels approved by Crypto.com; live redirect domains can require compliance approval.

facts.label: Document language
facts.value: The global terms say application documents should be in English except where applicable law permits otherwise; a certified translation may be required.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Direct merchant registration is open through the website; signup is not limited to an invitation in the current FAQ.

facts.label: Approval estimate
facts.value: Crypto.com says review takes a few business days and that it will email the result and next steps.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No public revenue, transaction-volume, or time-in-business threshold was found in the signup FAQ, product page, or merchant terms.

facts.label: Goods, services, and donations
facts.value: The global terms allow merchant transactions for goods, services, or donations, subject to the prohibited-activity rules.

facts.label: Online stores
facts.value: Product materials show online shops using checkout plugins or a few lines of integration code.

facts.label: Physical store payments
facts.value: Crypto.com advertises a dedicated merchant app for in-store acceptance; the merchant FAQ says offline integrations are currently being worked on with selected merchants.

facts.label: Subscriptions
facts.value: Crypto subscriptions are offered only to customers paying through Crypto.com App.

facts.label: Prohibited businesses
facts.value: Terms prohibit, among other categories, tobacco, pharmaceuticals, drugs, firearms, gambling, forex/CFDs, unlicensed stored-value products, pyramid schemes, IP-infringing goods, adult content, pornography, and illegal activity.

facts.label: Seller compliance duties
facts.value: Sellers must comply with law, screen suspicious transactions, and are responsible for the legality and quality of their offering.

facts.label: Buyer-country list
facts.value: A full buyer-country acceptance list for direct merchant checkout was not found in the payment-currency, merchant FAQ, product, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Sanctions and legal restrictions
facts.value: Merchant use is barred where Crypto.com has restricted the service or where crypto handling is unlawful; U.S. terms also bar sanctioned/embargoed persons and locations.

facts.label: Regional wallet limitation
facts.value: The external-wallet on-chain payment option is not available to U.S. merchants.

facts.label: Reserves
facts.value: U.S. terms allow an initial or rolling reserve as agreed in the Commercial Agreement and allow additional reserves or guarantees later.

facts.label: Settlement holds
facts.value: Terms allow delayed settlement or withheld balances during bank issues, business-risk changes, disputes, suspected fraud, legal review, or complaints.

facts.label: Approval estimate
facts.value: The public approval estimate is a few business days after application.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: The merchant terms describe Pay as an acquiring and authorising processor for digital-asset payments.

facts.label: Seller and funds role
facts.value: Merchant sells and is responsible for the goods, delivery, support, and refunds; Crypto.com and its partners receive, temporarily hold, and disburse confirmed customer funds as the merchant’s agent.

facts.label: Stripe distribution route
facts.value: Stripe announced that its merchants can offer Crypto.com Pay in Stripe Checkout; Stripe converts the crypto payment to the business’s preferred local fiat currency and deposits it to the bank.

facts.label: Fiat pricing currencies
facts.value: Current merchant help lists AED, ARS, AUD, BHD, BRL, CAD, CHF, CLP, CNY, COP, CZK, DKK, DOP, EGP, EUR, GBP, HKD, HNL, ILS, INR, ISK, JOD, JPY, KES, KWD, MAD, MDL, MOP, MXN, MYR, NOK, NZD, OMR, PEN, PHP, PLN, QAR, RON, SAR, SEK, SGD, THB, TND, TRY, TWD, USD, UYU, and VND.

facts.label: Crypto pricing currencies
facts.value: The same help page lists BTC, CRO, ELIZAOS, and ETH as pricing currencies.

facts.label: Currency documentation difference
facts.value: The current merchant FAQ is dated 2026-02-03; the API reference contains a different legacy fiat list.

facts.label: Crypto.com App payment
facts.value: Customers using Crypto.com App can select an available crypto asset and scan the checkout QR code to pay.

facts.label: External wallet payment
facts.value: When enabled by the merchant, buyers can pay through other wallets, including MetaMask, WalletConnect, Ledger, and Crypto.com DeFi Wallet.

facts.label: Card on-ramp separation
facts.value: The separate Pay On-ramp feature lets users buy crypto with Visa/Mastercard, Apple Pay, or Google Pay on supported partner apps; it is not the direct merchant checkout fee.

facts.label: Payment method scope
facts.value: Direct merchant API/docs describe Crypto.com App and external crypto wallets; the product page also mentions one-time card payments in a no-integration context.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Direct merchant checkout supports one-time purchases paid in crypto.

facts.label: Automatic recurring payments
facts.value: Automatic recurring collections are available through subscriptions, but only for customers using Crypto.com App.

facts.label: Subscription funding limit
facts.value: Future periods are collected automatically only if the customer has sufficient funds in their Crypto.com App wallet; both sides can cancel.

facts.label: Subscription setup and controls
facts.value: Merchants create customer, product, and pricing-plan records; the dashboard can create product/pricing details and review active subscriptions.

facts.label: Dunning and failed-payment recovery
facts.value: A retry schedule, dunning messages, grace periods, usage metering, seat billing, and proration policy were not found in the subscription help or API pages checked.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Checkout redirects to a Crypto.com Pay payment page or opens a popup from an embedded Pay button.

facts.label: No-code invoice collection
facts.value: A merchant can email an invoice from the dashboard without integrating a website checkout.

facts.label: Embedded / custom-domain checkout
facts.value: Button SDK, redirect, mobile WebView, and plugins are documented; custom domain white-labeling was not found in those guides.

facts.label: API and SDK
facts.value: Pay publishes REST API, button SDK, API keys, payment creation/retrieval/cancel, and refund endpoints.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: The merchant configures webhook channels and signature secrets for payment events.

facts.label: Test mode
facts.value: Test keys and dashboard test mode simulate checkout without affecting live data or using payment networks.

facts.label: Shopify integration
facts.value: A Crypto.com Pay Shopify plugin is documented with connect, test, live, and disconnect steps.

facts.label: Other ecommerce plugins
facts.value: Official setup guides are available for WooCommerce, PrestaShop, Magento 2, OpenCart, Ecwid, and nopCommerce.

facts.label: API stability
facts.value: The API reference says the API remains under heavy development and may have breaking changes with advance notice.

facts.label: Seller tax duties
facts.value: Seller alone determines applicable tax and must withhold, collect, report, and remit it to tax authorities.

facts.label: Tax on provider fees
facts.value: U.S. terms say provider fees exclude applicable VAT/sales/turnover tax unless the commercial agreement says otherwise; tax on fees may be added.

facts.label: Buyer invoices
facts.value: Dashboard invoices can include recipient email, due date, fiat currency, items, quantity, unit price, note, and internal reference, then be emailed to the customer.

facts.label: Tax invoice compliance
facts.value: The invoice guide does not state whether generated invoices meet local VAT/GST tax-invoice requirements or support tax IDs/exemptions.

facts.label: Payment receipts
facts.value: Terms require the merchant to provide a receipt or payment confirmation when funds are received.

facts.label: Fiat seller payout method
facts.value: Fiat settlement is sent to the merchant’s bank account through payment partners.

facts.label: Crypto seller payout method
facts.value: Crypto settlement is sent to the merchant’s nominated digital-asset wallet address.

facts.label: Fiat balance/payout currencies
facts.value: Published fiat settlement currencies are USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, and AED.

facts.label: Crypto balance/payout currencies
facts.value: Published crypto settlement assets are BTC, ETH, CRO, and USDC.

facts.label: Payment credit timing
facts.value: The merchant API says successful crypto payments are credited to the merchant balance; overview help describes crypto settlement as instant.

facts.label: Fiat bank payout timing
facts.value: Business overview advertises quickest T+1 fiat payouts, but current settlement help does not set a guaranteed payout schedule or bank-arrival time.

facts.label: Crypto withdrawal timing
facts.value: The overview calls crypto settlements instant, while exact external-wallet payout processing conditions are account/dashboard based.

facts.label: Product delivery
facts.value: Seller remains responsible for delivering products, services, access, returns, and warranty; no merchant digital-file hosting or licence delivery is described.

facts.label: Merchant catalogue promotion
facts.value: Merchants can submit a shop to the Pay Catalogue for review and may use promotional banners/CRO rebates.

facts.label: Acquirer sub-merchants
facts.value: Crypto.com invites payment acquirers to onboard sub-merchants, with a sub-merchant identifier in payment and refund APIs.

facts.label: Split payouts
facts.value: A direct split-payment or multi-seller payout feature for an ordinary merchant account was not found in the API reference or merchant FAQ.

facts.label: Crypto.com App assets
facts.value: App checkout payment assets are BTC, ETH, USDT, XRP, USDC, DOGE, BCH, ADA, LINK, LTC, PYUSD, SHIB, CRO, UNI, DOT, AAVE, ALGO, FIL, CRV, COMP, THETA, ENJ, SNX, APE, LRC, WBTC, YFI, KSM, KNC, and LION.

facts.label: External-wallet coins and networks
facts.value: Published on-chain pairs are Cronos: CRO/ETH/USDC/USDT; Cronos POS: CRO; Bitcoin: BTC; Ethereum ERC-20: CRO/ETH/USDC/USDT; Polygon: POL/ETH/USDC/USDT; Solana: USDC; Optimism: ETH/USDC; Arbitrum One: ETH/USDC; zkSync Era: ETH.

facts.label: Custody of merchant funds
facts.value: Crypto.com holds confirmed transaction balances in the Merchant Account until it settles them in fiat or a merchant-selected digital-asset wallet.

facts.label: Buyer external-wallet custody
facts.value: External-wallet buyers initiate an on-chain transfer from their selected wallet; merchant proceeds are still credited to the Pay Merchant Account before payout.

facts.label: Fiat settlement route
facts.value: Merchants may request fiat settlement to a bank in USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, or AED, subject to currency and bank-country rules.

facts.label: Crypto settlement route
facts.value: Merchants may request BTC, ETH, CRO, or USDC settlement to a wallet; CRO and USDC use Ethereum in the published settlement table.

facts.label: Stablecoin settlement
facts.value: USDC on Ethereum is the only published stablecoin payout asset in the merchant settlement list.

facts.label: Settlement conversion
facts.value: Pay converts incoming crypto to the selected default balance currency at the payment-time market rate; its help says no additional Pay conversion fee, while payout fees remain separate.

facts.label: On-chain confirmations
facts.value: External-wallet payments are shown pending after the first network confirmation and confirmed after the 12th network confirmation in the customer help flow.

facts.label: Expiry and underpayment
facts.value: Payments sent late (20 minutes for BTC; 10 minutes for other coins), underpaid, or duplicated may be unresolved and returned minus network fees; overpayment is returned only for the excess.

facts.label: Wrong coin or network
facts.value: Wrong-currency payments are reviewed case by case and refunds are not guaranteed; unsupported assets or networks are not guaranteed to be returned.

facts.label: Refund route
facts.value: App payments return to the customer’s App balance; external-wallet payments use an email claim/refund address; refunds are made to the original pricing value and can cost network fees.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Crypto.com hosts and maintains the merchant checkout, API, dashboard, and plugins; sellers do not run their own Pay server.

facts.label: Payment and balance exports
facts.value: Merchants can export payment reports with IDs, status, amount, refund, fee, credit currency, and order details, plus balance reports for payments, refunds, conversions, and payouts.

facts.label: Customer/payment migration
facts.value: No public migration tool or transfer of customer payment authorizations to another provider was found in the merchant docs checked.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Merchant can request closure by emailing pay@crypto.com from the registered address; pending customer refunds should be settled and balances withdrawn first.

facts.label: Remaining funds after closure
facts.value: Terms allow recovery of remaining balances subject to minimum transfer amount and fees, unless law, court order, suspected fraud, or criminal activity prevents release.

facts.label: Dashboard/data access after closure
facts.value: Closing the account removes access to account information and prevents further payments, refunds, or payouts through that account.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: Crypto.com Pay for Business is a hosted crypto merchant checkout, invoice, subscription, and balance/payout service.

facts.label: Global agreement provider
facts.value: The global merchant terms name Foris DAX Global Limited, an Irish company, together with its affiliates as the service provider.

facts.label: U.S. agreement provider
facts.value: The U.S. merchant terms name Foris DAX, Inc., a Delaware corporation and registered money services business.

facts.label: Current product changes
facts.value: The company announced Stripe checkout distribution on 2026-01-06, Yuno distribution on 2026-01-27, and a UAE merchant checkout at Dubai Duty Free on 2026-08-05.

facts.label: Merchant support
facts.value: Merchant help directs sellers to email pay@crypto.com for Pay account and integration support.

facts.label: Support hours and response time
facts.value: Public merchant pages do not state support hours or a standard response-time target; terms say complex complaints may take up to 45 days.

facts.label: Current service availability
facts.value: Crypto.com’s live status page listed Checkout, Invoice, Subscriptions, Refunds, and Merchant Dashboard as operational on the checked date.

facts.label: Current merchant operation
facts.value: Merchant registration is open and the current merchant FAQ and product pages remain available.

facts.label: Product retirement, acquisition, or rebrand
facts.value: Crypto.com’s company-news pages and merchant help showed current product use and no notice that direct Pay for Business is retired, acquired, or rebranded.

facts.label: UAE product expansion
facts.value: Dubai Duty Free announced Crypto.com Pay checkout in August 2026, with AED merchant settlement and eligible UAE-resident buyers.

facts.label: Ireland VASP status
facts.value: In an August 25, 2025 warning, the Central Bank of Ireland described Foris DAX Global Limited as a registered VASP; the CBI says Ireland’s VASP registration is for AML/CFT purposes and is not a general payments authorisation.

facts.label: U.S. regulatory statement
facts.value: U.S. Pay terms name Foris DAX, Inc. and call it a registered money services business.

facts.label: UAE Stored Value Facility licence
facts.value: CBUAE lists Foris DAX Middle East FZE as a Stored Value Facility licensee; Crypto.com’s Dubai launch ties a regulated Pay checkout to AED settlement.

facts.label: UAE virtual-asset licence scope
facts.value: VARA lists Foris DAX Middle East FZE as an active VASP for specified broker-dealer, investment, lending, and exchange activities.

facts.label: Regulatory notice about impersonation
facts.value: On 2025-08-25, the Central Bank of Ireland warned about a “Cryptocom (Clone)” that had copied Foris DAX Global Limited’s details and said the clone had no connection with the company.

facts.label: Merchant security certification
facts.value: A current product-specific security certification or audit scope for Crypto.com Pay for Business was not identified in the merchant terms, API docs, or security information checked.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: In Peru, Flow's payment receipt is not a boleta or factura; the seller must issue the applicable SUNAT document.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices

facts.label: Payout timing

facts.label: Payout timing

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
