facts.label: Separate account / provider dependency
facts.value: Merchant needs an approved Geidea merchant account and a settlement bank account. Direct API use needs credentials; Tabby and Tamara require merchant registration with those providers.

facts.label: Third-party gateway dependency
facts.value: Geidea's direct API and hosted checkout are its own processing integrations; no additional gateway is listed as universally required.

facts.label: Saudi online fixed fees
facts.value: Online payment gateway and Pay by Link each list SAR 499 one-time setup and SAR 99 monthly; both subject to 15% VAT.

facts.label: Saudi cancellation charge
facts.value: Gateway and Pay by Link schedule lists early cancellation at remaining contract months multiplied by SAR 99, up to 24 months.

facts.label: UAE / Egypt fixed online price
facts.value: No general public setup or recurring gateway fee is listed for UAE or Egypt. UAE agreement says merchant transaction fees are set in the application form; Egypt pages route merchants to sales.

facts.label: Terminal hardware price, separate scope
facts.value: The online pages do not publish a current POS-terminal purchase price. Terminal product is separate from the online gateway and CNP rates above.

facts.label: Saudi international cards
facts.value: The KSA online schedule states one credit-card rate and does not distinguish domestic from foreign-issued credit cards. No separate international surcharge appears in that schedule.

facts.label: UAE / Egypt international-card uplift
facts.value: Public country terms and product pages do not disclose a separate foreign-issued-card price for UAE or Egypt online payments.

facts.label: Currency conversion / cross-border conversion
facts.value: Geidea publishes configurable transaction currencies but no general FX markup, rate source, cross-border conversion fee or payout conversion fee.

facts.label: Local non-card method pricing
facts.value: No separate public fee schedule was found for digital wallets, instalments, BNPL or Egypt local wallet/QR methods.

facts.label: Egypt local-wallet / QR pricing
facts.value: The Egypt guides confirm Meeza Digital and bank instalments but do not publish merchant fees for Meeza, ValU or Souhoola.

facts.label: Subscription surcharge
facts.value: No separate public recurring-billing or subscription surcharge is stated; the KSA CNP schedule lists online card rates, while plan-specific charges may be in the merchant agreement.

facts.label: Tax / fraud / add-on services
facts.value: Pay-by-Link APIs can calculate tax; KSA agreement says optional add-ons incur charges only if requested. Public prices for tax calculation, fraud tools or other add-ons were not found.

facts.label: Refund handling
facts.value: Dashboard and API support full or partial refunds for completed/captured transactions; refund is limited to the original amount and payment method.

facts.label: Refund fee and returned processing charge
facts.value: Public material does not clearly say whether the original processing fee is returned or whether online refunds carry a separate fee.

facts.label: Refund arrival time
facts.value: FAQ says a refund typically reaches the customer's account/card in 5–10 days, with possible delays across acquirer and issuer processes.

facts.label: Dispute responsibility
facts.value: Merchant bears chargeback losses, returned transaction amounts and related costs; Geidea may withhold disputed proceeds and debit later settlements or the bank account.

facts.label: Dispute evidence and fee
facts.value: Saudi CNP terms give three working days for Visa/Mastercard and one working day for Mada evidence. No fixed online chargeback fee is stated in the CNP schedule.

facts.label: Payout costs
facts.value: Public online payout or bank-transfer fees are not generally stated for KSA, UAE or Egypt.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No general minimum payout amount is published for KSA, UAE or Egypt online merchants.

facts.label: Online transaction lower bound
facts.value: Payment-link API amount must be greater than 0.01 in the selected currency and has at most two decimal places; currency must be configured for the account.

facts.label: UAE monthly volume threshold
facts.value: UAE agreement requires AED 10,000 monthly transaction volume or another approved amount. It gives a shortfall charge as AED 110 in clause 4.5 and AED 109 in clause 13.14.

facts.label: Maximum charge / account limits
facts.value: No general maximum online charge or public account processing cap was found for the three markets.

facts.label: Merchant countries
facts.value: Geidea's developer FAQ lists merchant availability in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Egypt.

facts.label: Sellers outside the three markets
facts.value: Public documentation does not say that merchants based outside Saudi Arabia, UAE or Egypt can open a Geidea merchant account.

facts.label: Saudi seller forms
facts.value: Saudi terms allow a sole trader or company/other accepted business entity. A sole trader must be a Saudi citizen or legal resident; a company must be authorized to conduct business in Saudi Arabia.

facts.label: UAE and Egypt seller forms
facts.value: Public current pages identify local merchant services, but the reviewed UAE agreement and older Egyptian Arabic terms do not give a clear, current accepted-form matrix for individuals, sole traders and companies.

facts.label: Saudi local presence and bank
facts.value: Saudi seller must be a Saudi citizen or legal resident; company must be authorized to do business in KSA. Settlement goes to the merchant's named settlement bank account.

facts.label: UAE bank requirement
facts.value: UAE agreement defines the payout account as an account held by the merchant at a UAE bank, in the merchant's own name.

facts.label: Egypt local presence / bank
facts.value: Current public Egypt gateway pages do not state the full residency, commercial-registration or settlement-bank requirements.

facts.label: Saudi verification
facts.value: Merchant must provide complete and current registration, trade-license, shareholder/beneficial-owner and KYC details; Geidea may request underwriting and financial information.

facts.label: UAE / Egypt verification detail
facts.value: The UAE privacy notice lists identity, business licence, tax/registration, bank and beneficial-owner data that may be collected. A complete public document checklist is not stated for UAE or Egypt online merchants.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Product pages offer a Get Started route and invite merchants to provide basic business information; developer docs say a test account can be created before going live.

facts.label: Minimum size / approval time
facts.value: No public minimum revenue, monthly volume or guaranteed underwriting approval time was found for online gateway onboarding in KSA, UAE or Egypt.

facts.label: Supported online products
facts.value: Merchants may use the service for their own lawful, licensed goods and services, subject to Geidea approval and scheme rules. Public terms do not enumerate digital-product categories one by one.

facts.label: Digital content / service fit
facts.value: Geidea documents subscriptions for SaaS and recurring services, and contracts cover goods and services sold by the merchant.

facts.label: Prohibited / restricted activity
facts.value: Transactions must be lawful, match the merchant's licensed and approved activity, follow scheme rules and avoid prohibited-country or sanctioned-party activity.

facts.label: Specific high-risk categories
facts.value: No current public list was found that settles Geidea's treatment of adult content, gambling, crowdfunding, AI services or marketplaces across all three markets.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Geidea's payment methods and card acceptance depend on seller market, issuer, method and risk controls; the public docs do not give a complete country-by-country buyer acceptance table.

facts.label: Holds and reserves
facts.value: Geidea may hold disputed or suspicious proceeds, set off chargebacks/refunds and retain settlement after termination for possible chargebacks for up to 540 days after the last transaction under Saudi CNP terms.

facts.label: UAE withholding
facts.value: UAE agreement allows partial or full settlement withholding for non-conforming, suspicious or irregular activity and deduction of chargebacks.

facts.label: Approval time
facts.value: No public guaranteed or typical approval time for identity, website, product or payout review was found.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Payment gateway/acquirer and payment-link service; it processes customer payments for the merchant.

facts.label: Seller in buyer transaction
facts.value: The merchant sells its own goods or services to the customer; Geidea provides processing and does not describe itself as seller or merchant of record.

facts.label: Configurable charge currencies
facts.value: Checkout API supports configured account currencies; the docs list SAR, EGP, AED, QAR, OMR, BHD, KWD, USD, GBP and EUR. Multicurrency must be enabled through support.

facts.label: Payment-link currency claim
facts.value: Saudi marketing page advertises payment links in 180+ currencies, while API docs limit transactions to currencies configured for the merchant account.

facts.label: Saudi methods
facts.value: Saudi checkout supports card networks including Mada, Visa and Mastercard; official FAQ also lists Amex, JCB, CUP, Apple/Google/Samsung Pay, STC Pay, Tabby and Tamara, with activation and eligibility varying by account.

facts.label: UAE methods
facts.value: UAE gateway advertises local and international cards, mobile wallets and BNPL. The FAQ lists major card schemes, Apple/Google/Samsung Pay, Visa instalments, Tabby and Tamara.

facts.label: Egypt methods
facts.value: Egypt gateway lists Meeza, Visa and Mastercard, wallets and bank instalments; FAQ also lists ValU and Souhoola. Meeza Digital wallet and QR are described in Egypt docs.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Standard card checkout and one-time payment links are supported in all three published merchant markets.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Card auto-debit subscriptions and recurring payment links/scheduled invoices are supported.

facts.label: Recurring method limits
facts.value: Public recurring API guidance centers on card-on-file/token transactions. Geidea does not publish a complete recurring-eligibility table for wallets, BNPL or local methods across the three countries.

facts.label: Recurring payment links
facts.value: Recurring payment links schedule sending a link or invoice for payment; they are not the same as automatic card deductions.

facts.label: Billing controls
facts.value: Subscription API supports recurring amount, interval, start/end date, number of payments, fixed/variable amount and two retry attempts after an automatic debit failure.

facts.label: Other subscription features
facts.value: Public docs do not establish packaged seat/usage billing, trials, coupons, proration, customer self-service portal or broader dunning controls.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Checkout supports a hosted page and web integration; regional product pages describe redirect, pop-up and embedded checkout.

facts.label: Payment links / invoices
facts.value: Portal and API links support one-time, quick, static/multi-customer and digital-invoice use; links can be shared by SMS, email and social channels.

facts.label: QR payments
facts.value: Geidea's market pages and Egypt portal docs describe payment QR codes generated from links.

facts.label: Branding / custom domain
facts.value: Checkout and links can use merchant logos, colors, fonts and branding. The pages reviewed do not establish custom-domain hosting.

facts.label: API and environment
facts.value: Developer docs provide checkout/session, payment, refund, subscription and payment-link APIs with separate KSA, UAE and Egypt endpoints.

facts.label: Plugins and mobile SDKs
facts.value: Official resources list Shopify, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop and WooCommerce; docs include WooCommerce and Android SDK guidance.

facts.label: Webhooks / callbacks
facts.value: API and help docs support HTTPS callback URLs/webhooks for payment status notifications.

facts.label: Test environment
facts.value: Geidea provides sandbox/test accounts and test cards covering success, failure and 3-D Secure scenarios.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: FAQ reports PCI DSS 4.0 certification and 3-D Secure; hosted checkout keeps card details with Geidea or its gateway service provider.

facts.label: Seller / tax role
facts.value: Merchant remains the seller and responsible for its goods, services, purchase terms, delivery and refunds. Geidea is a processor, not a public merchant-of-record offer.

facts.label: Tax calculation vs filing
facts.value: Pay-by-Link APIs support automatic tax calculations, but public docs do not say Geidea registers, files or remits merchants' sales taxes.

facts.label: Receipts and digital invoices
facts.value: Payment links create digital invoices and transaction receipts; merchant receipts must include seller, amount, currency, transaction and delivery details.

facts.label: Tax invoice IDs / tax-exempt purchases
facts.value: Public sources reviewed do not establish country-wide tax-invoice compliance, seller VAT ID handling or tax-exempt workflow.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: Payout is to the merchant's designated bank account in Saudi and UAE terms. Egypt payout method is not clearly stated in current public docs.

facts.label: Egypt payout method
facts.value: Egypt public gateway and docs do not clearly state whether merchants are paid only by local bank transfer or may select another payout method.

facts.label: BNPL settlement exception
facts.value: Tabby/Tamara flows in KSA/UAE settle from the BNPL provider into the merchant settlement account, separate from ordinary Geidea gateway card payout.

facts.label: Payout currency
facts.value: The reviewed agreements require a local merchant bank account but do not give a complete payout-currency matrix for KSA, UAE and Egypt.

facts.label: Saudi online settlement timing
facts.value: A fixed online settlement cycle is not given in the CNP price schedule; timing and bank details depend on merchant-specific terms and risk review.

facts.label: UAE online settlement timing
facts.value: UAE proceeds are credited at the frequency selected in the Merchant Application Form; the public agreement gives no universal frequency.

facts.label: Egypt online settlement timing
facts.value: Public Egypt materials reviewed do not state a current standard settlement delay or schedule for online transactions.

facts.label: Product delivery / access
facts.value: Geidea provides checkout and billing tools but public documentation does not describe hosted digital-file delivery, software-license fulfillment or membership access provisioning.

facts.label: Split payments / marketplace
facts.value: Public docs reviewed do not establish a marketplace or split-payment product for paying out to multiple sellers.

facts.label: Crypto assets / networks
facts.value: Not applicable to the reviewed Geidea payment-gateway offer: public methods are cards, wallets, local payment methods and BNPL; no crypto checkout is described.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable to the reviewed fiat payment gateway; the docs describe card/token and bank-payment flows, not crypto wallets or custody.

facts.label: Crypto conversion / payout
facts.value: Not applicable to the reviewed offer; no crypto settlement path is documented.

facts.label: Crypto completion / refunds
facts.value: Not applicable to the reviewed offer; payment completion and refund docs cover fiat card and wallet transactions.

facts.label: Crypto hosting / maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable to the reviewed hosted gateway; no crypto software deployment or self-hosted payment server is described.

facts.label: Reporting / exports
facts.value: Merchant portal provides transaction status, dashboard and reports. Public docs reviewed do not specify all export formats or whether customer/payment data can be exported in bulk for migration.

facts.label: Provider migration
facts.value: No official migration path for moving stored cards, subscriptions or customer payment tokens to another provider was found.

facts.label: Saudi online contract term
facts.value: Saudi CNP agreement runs two years, then renews in one-year periods; non-renewal requires three months' written notice before the term ends.

facts.label: Saudi cancellation / cooling-off
facts.value: Merchant may terminate within 10 business days without compensation; after that, cancellation fees are in the CNP schedule at SAR 99 per remaining month up to 24 months.

facts.label: UAE and Egypt closure
facts.value: UAE agreement permits termination on 30 days' written notice, with additional immediate-termination grounds; Egypt Arabic terms let Geidea terminate services and preserve accrued claims.

facts.label: Release of remaining funds
facts.value: Saudi agreement allows post-termination funds to be held for possible chargebacks up to 540 days; no unconditional fixed release date for all remaining balances is stated.

facts.label: Current product name
facts.value: Geidea Payment Gateway, with hosted checkout and Pay by Link for online payments.

facts.label: Current owner / historical investment
facts.value: Current shareholder or controlling owner is not stated in the official company materials reviewed. Geidea's About page records a SAR 1 billion Gulf Capital investment in 2019; Gulf Capital's own 2018 release calls it a strategic stake.

facts.label: Saudi support
facts.value: Saudi pages list phone/email support and hours Sunday–Thursday, 9 AM–9 PM, closed Friday.

facts.label: UAE support
facts.value: UAE site lists the 800434332 support line, email and Dubai address; specific support hours were not stated on the page.

facts.label: Egypt support
facts.value: Egypt site lists 15757 and customersupport.eg@geidea.net; public support hours were not found.

facts.label: Operating status
facts.value: Current regional sites and developer docs advertise and document the online gateway and payment links for KSA, UAE and Egypt.

facts.label: Saudi legal entity / regulator
facts.value: Contracting entity is Geidea Co. for Technology Company, supervised by the Saudi Central Bank; company site lists CR 1010332533.

facts.label: UAE legal entity / regulator
facts.value: UAE contracting entity is Geidea Payment LLC, licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE; UAE privacy page lists commercial registration and licence numbers.

facts.label: Egypt legal/regulatory entity
facts.value: The current public Egypt pages reviewed do not state a clear contracting entity, regulator or licence number for online gateway merchants.

facts.label: Security certification
facts.value: Geidea FAQ states PCI DSS Level 4.0 certification and 3-D Secure use.

facts.value: International cards are conditionally supported, but no separate international-card rate, issuer-country add-on or universal foreign-card fee was published.

facts.label: Local-method cost

facts.label: Local-method cost

facts.label: Local-method cost

facts.label: Local-method cost

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons
facts.value: No public sales-tax calculation, registration or filing add-on price was found.

facts.value: iugu's fee is not returned to the merchant when a payment is refunded, cancelled, disputed or reversed.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: Credit-card payments can be refunded partially or fully for up to 180 days after approval.

facts.label: Refund costs

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility
facts.value: The seller bears losses, chargeback-related amounts and network or operational penalties; a universal public chargeback fee amount was not published.

facts.label: Payout cost

facts.value: A universal minimum withdrawal amount was not published; the contract requires a valid withdrawal account and limits withdrawal to available balance.

facts.label: Payment and account limits

facts.label: Payment and account limits

facts.label: Payment and account limits

facts.value: A person without a company may apply for the Link product as an individual, depending on the business model.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Virtual POS requires verification of an IBAN belonging to the applicant or company.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: The public onboarding and terms do not state whether a foreign bank account or foreign company bank account is accepted.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Virtual POS application asks for signature circular, tax plate, company partners’ identity documents, and a verified applicant/company IBAN.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: The website must be live and ready, show products and prices, have SSL, and publish privacy, distance-sale, delivery/returns, about, and contact information.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Signup starts online through an account and application form; documents and agreements are submitted through the merchant panel and the application is reviewed.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: No minimum revenue or transaction volume for ordinary signup is published. The ₺20,000 monthly-sales figure on the POS page is a pricing qualifier.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Subscription materials explicitly list SaaS, ecommerce/marketplaces, education and services among possible business sectors.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: A general public approval list for downloadable software, ebooks, courses, memberships, and all physical-goods categories was not found.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Terms allow iyzico to suspend or stop service for unlawful or policy-violating activity and give examples including illegal goods, unlawful gambling, terrorism, and intellectual-property violations.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Help Centre also flags categories such as adult content, tobacco, forex, debt collection, and illegal drugs as restricted or unsuitable for some offers.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Link and Multi Currency pages say buyers can pay from abroad using supported international cards and currencies.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Foreign-card processing can be disabled or require activation for an account; no comprehensive supported/blocked buyer-country list is published.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: A complete prohibited or supported buyer-country list for card payments was not found.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Help Centre describes a standard 3-week hold related to chargeback risk and says the hold may shorten based on volume and products.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Terms allow iyzico to withhold, block, set off, or deduct refunds, disputes, fees, and other amounts due from funds payable to a merchant.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: No general time estimate for business verification or approval was found.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: iyzico is a payment gateway and payment service provider, not a merchant of record. The merchant sells and invoices its own goods or services.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Marketplace payments can route a buyer payment to iyzico and split the proceeds between the platform and its sub-seller.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Standard domestic checkout is in TRY. Multi Currency adds USD, EUR, GBP, RUB, CHF, and NOK for Visa and Mastercard transactions.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Foreign-currency payments are converted to TRY using the Central Bank rate for the transaction date, with a conversion fee at payout.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Card API documentation supports Visa, Mastercard, TROY, and American Express cards, subject to the enabled product and account settings.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: iyzico supports 3D Secure and non-3DS card flows; iyzico may require 3DS for riskier business models.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: iyzico Link creates a shareable payment page without a seller-built checkout.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Help Centre describes iDEAL, Sofort, Giropay, and Qiwi as requestable alternative methods for eligible Virtual POS accounts.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: iyzico’s listed instalment card families are Bonus, World, Maximum, CardFinans, Paraf, Axess, and Advantage.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Developer API examples expose 2, 3, 6, 9, and 12 instalment choices; the BIN query returns options for the specific card and amount.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: iyzico ile Öde can use iyzico balance, a saved or new card, protected bank transfer/EFT, and eligible bank shopping credit.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Standard Virtual POS and Link support single payments.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Subscription Method supports automatically charged recurring plans on saved cards after one integration.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Subscription plans can run daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or at other configured intervals; alternative payment methods do not support instalments and are not documented as subscription rails.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Subscription plans support trials and can be configured in the panel or API; the card is collected at trial start so charging can begin when the trial ends.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Subscription documentation describes plan creation and recurring payment status notifications; public docs do not establish usage-based billing, seats, coupons, or prorated plan changes.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Virtual POS can show an iyzico checkout form during the seller’s checkout.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Link offers hosted payment pages with no website or code requirement; a custom domain for payment links is not published.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Public developer docs provide APIs for card checkout, 3DS, non-3DS, subscriptions, refunds, and marketplaces.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Webhooks notify the merchant about payment outcomes and recurring charges; HTTPS is required, and failed notifications are retried up to three times at 15-minute intervals.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Sandbox environment and test cards are documented.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Official platform guides are available for WooCommerce and Shopify; the WooCommerce guide describes enabling iyzico from the store’s payment settings.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Fraud review can return a pending status and notify the seller by email or callback; the merchant should hold fulfilment until review completes.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: The merchant is responsible for its own sale, customer invoice, product tax, and legal duties; iyzico is not the seller of record.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: No provider-run sales-tax/VAT registration, calculation, filing, or remittance coverage by country is published.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: The merchant issues the buyer invoice for the full price; iyzico issues the merchant a service/commission invoice periodically.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Business tax identifiers are required as part of company onboarding; automated tax-exempt purchasing or buyer tax-ID invoice collection is not documented.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Business payouts go to the seller’s declared bank account/IBAN.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Standard seller payout is in TRY; foreign-currency card sales convert into TRY before payout.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Marketplace docs support foreign payment currencies including USD, EUR, GBP, RUB, CHF, and NOK; payout currency handling can depend on the platform contract.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Virtual POS marketing page advertises next-day payment.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Help Centre says company sellers receive Monday–Sunday sales on the following Wednesday; individual Link sellers receive funds on the first Wednesday at least 7 days after the sale.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: The same Help Centre also describes weekly batches running Wednesday–Tuesday and a 3-week hold before settlement, which conflicts with its simpler next-Wednesday wording and the next-day marketing claim.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: A current early-payout option and fee are not stated on the pricing, Help Centre, or terms pages. An older iyzico FAQ blog mentioned an “Erken Ödeme” option at ₺390 per year, but the current pages do not confirm it remains available.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: iyzico provides payment processing and subscription billing; no digital-file delivery, licence-key fulfilment, or membership-access product was found in the product pages and docs.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Marketplace product supports multiple sellers in a cart and splits settlement between platform and sellers.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Sellers do not need to apply to iyzico separately as sub-merchants, and Help Centre says no separate seller entry or integration fee is charged.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: iyzico’s checked business offers and API docs cover card and alternative payment processing, not crypto checkout.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Not applicable: the checked iyzico merchant products do not offer crypto payment custody.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto checkout or crypto settlement route is offered in the checked product pages and docs.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: iyzico’s public payment and refund docs describe card and alternative-method transactions, not blockchain payments.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: iyzico is a hosted payment service, not a crypto checkout software package sellers must run.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Reconciliation documents support downloadable transaction and settlement records, including CSV reporting through SFTP.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: A public workflow for exporting and migrating stored card credentials or subscription customers to another processor was not found.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Terms allow termination or suspension for breach, risk, missing or changed business information, or prohibited sales.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Either party can end the framework agreement with one month’s written notice; a material breach can lead to termination if not fixed within one week after written notice. No general deadline for releasing remaining funds after closure is published.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: The product is iyzico Virtual POS, Link, and Subscription Method under the iyzico brand.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: PayU acquired iyzico in 2019; iyzico’s current career page says it operates within Prosus Group.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: iyzico completed the acquisition of Paynet on 13 February 2025.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: iyzico publishes support by help centre, email, phone, merchant-panel contact routes, and live chat in its customer information page.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Developer documentation is publicly available in Turkish and English; no paid support tier or guaranteed response speed is published.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Business terms say iyzico aims to answer merchant complaints within 7 days; cases needing a third party can take longer.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: iyzico’s business product pages and developer docs are live; the Central Bank register lists iyzi Ödeme ve Elektronik Para Hizmetleri A.Ş.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: The official press archive and blog were checked for acquisition, shutdown, and rebrand notices. The 2019 PayU acquisition and 2025 Paynet acquisition are the material changes found.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: The business terms name iyzi Ödeme ve Elektronik Para Hizmetleri A.Ş. as contracting provider; the Central Bank register lists the entity as an electronic money institution.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: iyzico states PCI DSS Level 1 certification; a public certificate scope and expiry date were not found.

apps.name: Kashier

free.text: No setup or monthly subscription fee for standard online acceptance

cells.payout: Same-day, T+1 or T+2 options; account-specific

facts.label: Required provider account
facts.value: Merchant needs an approved Kashier account and its test/live credentials to take online payments.

facts.label: Bank and finance partners
facts.value: Merchant needs an Egyptian payout bank account; installment/BNPL methods also depend on separate partner approval and account enablement.

facts.label: Standard online setup and monthly fees
facts.value: Standard eligible online acceptance: setup EGP 0 and monthly subscription EGP 0.

facts.label: Separate invoice-product pricing
facts.value: Kashier's invoice page calls invoice management free and also mentions a free trial; current standard pricing does not list invoicing among included features, and no trial length or paid plan price is published.

facts.label: Enterprise plan
facts.value: Enterprise pricing is custom and may include negotiated per-method rates and custom settlement schedules.

facts.label: Online checkout inclusions
facts.value: Pricing page says payment links, checkout and dashboard are included in standard online acceptance.

facts.label: POS hardware and in-person charge
facts.value: POS hardware and POS/in-store processing are separate from online standard pricing and are quoted by sales.

facts.label: International-card pricing
facts.value: International cards are accepted subject to account setup, but the public page says contact sales for their rate.

facts.label: International-card definition
facts.value: Public pricing does not define the issuing-country test or distinguish foreign-issued card classes and exceptions.

facts.label: Currency conversion cost and settlement
facts.value: The public conversion API only looks up FX rates; it does not convert a payment. The Egypt homepage says payment links can be priced in other currencies and settle in EGP, but no merchant FX markup or conversion basis is published.

facts.label: Mobile-wallet fee
facts.value: Mobile-wallet online pricing is quoted by sales; no public percentage or fixed fee was found.

facts.label: Bank installment fee
facts.value: Bank installment pricing is quoted by sales; no public merchant fee schedule was found.

facts.label: BNPL partner fees
facts.value: Kashier's public page lists partner finance options but provides no per-provider merchant fee schedule.

facts.label: Basata kiosk fee
facts.value: Basata kiosk rates are quoted by sales; no fixed public charge is stated.

facts.label: InstaPay fee
facts.value: No public merchant fee for InstaPay QR or request-to-pay was found.

facts.label: Apple Pay fee
facts.value: The Apple Pay guide says payments settle over the card rail, while the pricing page groups Apple Pay with wallet/kiosk methods whose rates are quoted by sales.

facts.label: POS transaction fee
facts.value: In-person/POS pricing is separate and quoted by sales.

facts.label: Seller payout fee
facts.value: Pricing page identifies payout pricing as a sales quote; no standard public fee is published.

facts.label: Recurring charge surcharge
facts.value: No separate recurring or tokenized-card surcharge is published.

facts.label: Managed billing fees
facts.value: Kashier has no managed subscription/billing-plan API, so no managed billing add-on price is published.

facts.label: Tax tools and filing add-ons
facts.value: Kashier advertises automatically calculated taxes on invoices, but the public material does not document tax determination, registration, filing or remittance services, or a separate tax-tool fee.

facts.label: Fraud add-on price
facts.value: No separate fraud-screening product fee or fraud add-on plan is published.

facts.label: Refund request fee
facts.value: Current pricing says refunds are not billed as transactions; the refund API supports full and partial refunds from available balance.

facts.label: Original processing-fee treatment after refund
facts.value: Public wording does not clearly state whether the original processing fee and its VAT are returned or retained after a refund.

facts.label: Dispute handling and merchant responsibility
facts.value: The merchant is liable for chargebacks, claims, expenses, fines and liabilities Kashier incurs; seller must provide evidence and comply with card-network rules.

facts.label: Chargeback/dispute fee
facts.value: No universal fixed dispute or chargeback fee is stated in the public pricing page or merchant agreement.

facts.label: Settlement payout fee
facts.value: Payout service pricing is quoted by sales; a standard free or fixed bank-payout fee is not stated.

facts.label: Outbound transfer fees
facts.value: The separate Payouts API offers fee inquiry by merchant account and transfer method; the API guide does not publish a universal fee schedule.

facts.label: Minimum settlement balance
facts.value: No public minimum balance for merchant sales settlement to a bank was found.

facts.label: Online transaction limits
facts.value: No general online payment-session minimum/maximum amount or merchant collection cap is published in the reviewed checkout docs.

facts.label: Method/account-specific limits
facts.value: InstaPay can reject collections that exceed merchant collection limits, but the actual limits are not public; other risk and account limits can be merchant-specific.

facts.label: Explicit seller market
facts.value: Egypt is the market explicitly named by Kashier's current product and developer pages.

facts.label: Seller signup outside Egypt
facts.value: Eligibility for merchants legally based outside Egypt is not published as a country list.

facts.label: Freelancer / individual sellers
facts.value: Kashier markets to freelancers and one-person businesses, but its public merchant terms do not explicitly say whether an individual without a registered business can contract.

facts.label: Company sellers
facts.value: Merchant terms require the applicant to have authority to enter the agreement and to be duly organized and authorized under the laws of Egypt or its place of organization and operation.

facts.label: Local registration and authorization
facts.value: Merchant represents that it is legally organized and authorized to do business in the places where it operates.

facts.label: Settlement bank
facts.value: Standard online pricing says scheduled settlements go to any Egyptian bank.

facts.label: Registration information
facts.value: Signup requires contact and business details, including email, first and last name, business name and phone; Kashier may verify the information and approve or reject risky accounts.

facts.label: KYC and business documents
facts.value: Kashier says its team reviews the message and business type; a full current list of identity, tax, business-registration and beneficial-owner documents is not published.

facts.label: Signup and approval route
facts.value: Public site offers a free-account route and a sales-assisted route; merchant terms require registration, verification as needed and approval unless Kashier deems the account risky.

facts.label: Minimum business size or monthly volume
facts.value: No public minimum revenue, sales volume or business size for standard online signup was found.

facts.label: Goods and services
facts.value: Merchant terms cover the merchant's own goods and services, subject to law, card-network rules and Kashier's Acceptable Use Policy.

facts.label: Software and SaaS
facts.value: Technical recurring card charging is documented, but the reviewed acceptable-use and seller pages do not expressly approve every SaaS or software business model.

facts.label: Digital downloads, courses and memberships
facts.value: No public product-by-product approval list was found for downloads, online courses, memberships or digital licenses.

facts.label: Restricted activity
facts.value: Illegal, deceptive, fraudulent, network-rule-breaking, high-chargeback-risk activity and listed prohibited categories are barred.

facts.label: Named prohibited categories
facts.value: The policy lists, among others, unlicensed financial services/securities, counterfeit or stolen goods, certain controlled drugs, weapons, pornography, unlicensed currency sales, certain crypto operators, and gambling without prior approval and permitted jurisdictions.

facts.label: Categories not individually resolved
facts.value: No separate current policy ruling was found for AI products, crowdfunding or marketplaces as broad categories.

facts.label: Buyer-country reach
facts.value: Kashier's Egyptian homepage says it accepts payments from customers worldwide, but it does not publish a buyer-country acceptance or sanctions matrix.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions by method
facts.value: A country-by-country buyer access list for cards, wallets, installments and local methods is not published.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Kashier may place a discretionary reserve where it considers the business high risk and will provide the merchant's percentage, period and conditions when imposed.

facts.label: Payout suspension
facts.value: Kashier may delay or suspend payouts for pending disputes, excessive/anticipated chargebacks or refunds, suspicious activity, legal requirements or court order.

facts.label: Public approval timing
facts.value: Public estimates say 24–48 hours for eligible merchant activation and next working day for most accounts to go live.

facts.label: Separate review stages
facts.value: No public stage-by-stage timing for identity, website, product, risk or payout review was found.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Payment gateway / payment service provider with hosted checkout, payment links, recurring card charging and separate payout tools.

facts.label: Seller of record
facts.value: The merchant sells its own goods or services; Kashier says it is an independent service provider and does not assume responsibility for the merchant's products or customer transactions.

facts.label: Payment-session charge currencies
facts.value: Payment session API lists EGP, USD, GBP and EUR as accepted currency codes; account capability and method eligibility still apply.

facts.label: Display currencies
facts.value: Hosted checkout can show a 151-currency display dropdown when currency conversion is enabled for the account; display currency does not change the charged amount or currency.

facts.label: Card payments
facts.value: Online cards include Visa, Mastercard and Meeza; Meeza is submitted as a card payment.

facts.label: Egyptian mobile wallets
facts.value: Mobile wallets are accepted online, but account enablement and applicable rate are not listed by wallet brand on the public pricing page.

facts.label: Apple Pay
facts.value: Kashier documents Apple Pay on the merchant's website through its SDK; merchant must use HTTPS and submit its website domain to Kashier for Apple verification.

facts.label: Bank-card installments
facts.value: Egyptian bank installment plans can be looked up by merchant and amount; the installment API requires EGP.

facts.label: BNPL and consumer finance
facts.value: Docs list valU, Octo, Souhoola, Contact, Mogo, Tru and Forsa as separate provider flows.

facts.label: Kiosk and cash-related methods
facts.value: Basata reference-code collection and Aman installment-at-kiosk are documented. The separate generic cash API operation only records a payment already taken elsewhere; it is not an online cash authorization.

facts.label: InstaPay QR and request-to-pay
facts.value: InstaPay can collect through a scannable QR or a request-to-pay sent to a known payer address.

facts.label: Other bank-transfer rails
facts.value: No public complete list of other buyer bank-transfer methods was found beyond documented InstaPay and bank installments.

facts.label: One-time payment
facts.value: One-time online transactions are supported through payment sessions and payment links.

facts.label: Recurring card payments
facts.value: Merchants can save a card token after an initial customer payment and charge it on later billing cycles.

facts.label: Recurring methods
facts.value: Recurring flow is card-token based; Meeza is expressly rejected for recurring-origin payments.

facts.label: Managed subscription system
facts.value: Kashier explicitly says it has no managed subscriptions or billing-plans API.

facts.label: Billing schedule and plans
facts.value: Billing cadence, plan catalog and subscription lifecycle are merchant-managed, not handled by a Kashier billing-plan service.

facts.label: Other billing features
facts.value: No managed trials, discounts, proration, metered usage, seats, credits, retries or dunning features were found in public recurring documentation.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Hosted checkout/payment session creates a Kashier checkout URL that the merchant can link to or embed in an iframe.

facts.label: Embedded checkout
facts.value: Kashier supports an embedded checkout/iframe option.

facts.label: Payment links
facts.value: Payment links can be created through the dashboard or API, then shared with customers.

facts.label: Payment pages and product links
facts.value: Merchants can create product/payment pages and itemized checkout from a product catalog.

facts.label: Custom checkout controls
facts.value: Docs support branding controls such as brand color, display language and checkout presentation; custom payment-domain support is not stated.

facts.label: REST API
facts.value: Kashier documents REST APIs for hosted sessions, direct card flow, payment links, refunds, payouts and account/reporting operations.

facts.label: Test environment
facts.value: Test and live environments have separate API keys; test payments do not move real money.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: Kashier sends payment and refund events to the merchant's server; docs explain signature verification, retries and event status handling.

facts.label: Official ecommerce plugins
facts.value: Official docs list WooCommerce, Shopify, PrestaShop, Magento, OpenCart, CS-Cart, booking plugins and other store integrations.

facts.label: Mobile SDKs
facts.value: Kashier documents iOS and Flutter SDK integrations; the developer site also advertises mobile SDKs.

facts.label: Card security and 3-D Secure
facts.value: Direct card integrations document card tokens and 3-D Secure; using the direct card form changes the merchant's PCI scope.

facts.label: Live rate limits
facts.value: Going-live docs state live checkout requests are limited to 1,000 requests per minute per IP; test environment has no rate limit.

facts.label: API capability gates
facts.value: Many API capabilities are off by default and must be enabled by Kashier per merchant; the dashboard API says new merchants have three baseline flags.

facts.label: Seller's tax role
facts.value: Kashier calls itself an independent payment service provider and says it does not take responsibility for the merchant's products or services; no merchant-of-record tax handling is offered in the reviewed pages.

facts.label: Tax calculation, collection and filing features
facts.value: No tax-calculation, registration, filing or sales-tax remittance feature/coverage list was found.

facts.label: Buyer payment confirmation
facts.value: The checkout and webhook flow provides transaction status; merchant can use webhooks for order fulfillment and custom receipt messages.

facts.label: Invoices and receipts
facts.value: Kashier documents online invoices with itemized lines, tax fields, downloadable PDFs and customer payment receipts.

facts.label: Tax-invoice compliance and buyer tax IDs
facts.value: Whether Kashier invoices meet Egyptian tax-invoice/e-invoice requirements, capture a buyer tax ID or handle tax-exempt sales is not published in the reviewed pages.

facts.label: Merchant settlement destination
facts.value: Standard pricing promises scheduled settlement to any Egyptian bank. The account API also supports a bank account or wallet as a payout destination.

facts.label: Settlement currency
facts.value: Kashier's current Egyptian homepage says cross-currency pricing settles in Egyptian pounds; payment-session charge currencies include EGP, USD, GBP and EUR.

facts.label: Settlement schedule
facts.value: Merchant-specific payout schedule appears in the Kashier dashboard and may be changed or suspended for disputes, refunds, risk activity or legal orders.

facts.label: Advertised settlement options
facts.value: Homepage describes same-day, T+1 and T+2 settlement options; pricing says enterprise accounts can arrange custom settlement cycles.

facts.label: Product catalog
facts.value: Kashier provides a product catalog used to create itemized payment pages and links.

facts.label: Digital fulfillment
facts.value: No hosted file delivery, software license issuance or membership-access fulfillment feature was found.

facts.label: Connected accounts / platform payments
facts.value: Kashier documents a gated platform feature for collecting on behalf of existing Kashier merchants; both the platform and connected merchant must be enabled, and the sub-merchant must authorize the connection.

facts.label: Multi-seller split fees
facts.value: Public pricing does not state a split-payment or marketplace fee schedule.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: Kashier's public offer is a fiat payment gateway and does not list crypto assets or networks for customer checkout.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable: no Kashier crypto checkout or crypto custody offer is documented.

facts.label: Crypto payout route
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto-to-crypto or crypto-to-bank payout product is documented.

facts.label: Crypto completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: Kashier does not publish a crypto payment flow.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no self-hosted crypto payment product in the public offer.

facts.label: Transaction and fee export
facts.value: Settlement API exports transaction-level batches with fees, VAT, settlement amount, ready date, method and channel.

facts.label: Payment-link export
facts.value: Merchants can export payment links; the documentation says the export is delivered by email.

facts.label: Customer and transaction records
facts.value: APIs can list transactions, payment-link customers and customer records; public developer docs describe record export routes.

facts.label: Card data migration
facts.value: No public card-token portability or migration route from Kashier to another processor was found.

facts.label: Merchant account closure
facts.value: Merchant may terminate the agreement by closing the Kashier account.

facts.label: Funds and data after account closure
facts.value: Reserve, debt and dispute terms can affect final payouts. Privacy policy says data is retained after account closure as needed for regulatory compliance and fraud monitoring, but gives no fixed retention period or universal final-funds release schedule.

facts.label: Closure fee and notice
facts.value: No account-closure fee or advance notice period is stated in the reviewed merchant terms, privacy policy or contact/onboarding pages.

facts.label: Current product and brand
facts.value: Kashier is an Egyptian payment gateway and payment platform for merchants.

facts.label: Product owner / parent
facts.value: Kashier's official LinkedIn company profile describes Kashier as a product of Elements Financial Technologies.

facts.label: Current ultimate owner
facts.value: Current ultimate shareholder or parent ownership beyond the product relationship above is not published in the reviewed official pages.

facts.label: Support channels, hours and languages
facts.value: Kashier publishes support at 15883 and support email; its Egypt homepage advertises local Arabic and English support 24/7.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Kashier's current pricing, country homepage, contact route and developer documentation present an active service. I found no acquisition, shutdown, sunset or rebrand notice in the About page, blog/archive or official-domain searches.

facts.label: Contracting entity
facts.value: Privacy policy identifies Kashier Payment Solutions as an Egyptian company; merchant agreement identifies Kashier as the gateway provider.

facts.label: Licence and oversight
facts.value: Kashier states that it is licensed and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt.

facts.label: Security certifications
facts.value: Kashier says it is PCI DSS Level 1 certified and SOC 2 Type II audited.

facts.label: Foreign bank or residence exception
facts.value: No public source checked confirms whether a foreign bank account, nonresident owner, or nonlocal business address can be used for any of the eight markets.

facts.label: Identity and business verification
facts.value: The account applicant must complete KYC, submit genuine information and required documents, and be verified and approved before processing live transactions.

facts.label: Saudi document examples
facts.value: The Saudi notice lists owner/representative name, National ID, Iqama or passport, Commercial Registration number, contact and address details, supporting documents, and merchant IBAN/bank details.

facts.label: KYC submission window
facts.value: Country terms say required information must be submitted within 14 days of registration; incomplete applications may be automatically terminated.

facts.label: Country-specific document checklist
facts.value: No complete standard identity and business document checklist for all eight seller countries was found.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Applicants can register a country account, but must contact sales or an account manager to activate live processing and the API role.

facts.label: Multi-country account setup
facts.value: A merchant operating in one or more of the eight listed countries may ask to add another country to one MyFatoorah account; separate country API tokens are used.

facts.label: Minimum business size or volume
facts.value: No public minimum revenue, employee count, or transaction volume was found.

facts.label: Digital products and SaaS
facts.value: The payment gateway page explicitly includes digital products, subscriptions, and apps/platforms among suitable uses.

facts.label: Courses and education
facts.value: The gateway page names course registrations and education payments; payment links are marketed for trainers, educational centers, and student subscriptions.

facts.label: Professional services
facts.value: Payment links are marketed to individual service providers, freelancers, designers, developers, consultants, and photographers.

facts.label: Physical products
facts.value: Product links and the gateway support product listings, quantities, customer delivery addresses, and shipping integrations for physical goods.

facts.label: Crowdfunding and marketplace activity
facts.value: Crowdfunding is explicitly listed as restricted. Marketplace use is offered through the separate, approval-required Multi-Vendor feature; the merchant may not process for unapproved sub-merchants.

facts.label: Restricted and prohibited categories
facts.value: Terms restrict, among other categories, gambling, unlicensed financial activity, adult content, illegal goods, unlicensed tobacco/e-cigarettes, weapons, unauthorized prescription drugs, pyramid schemes, securities, crowdfunding, and sanctioned parties or jurisdictions.

facts.label: Digital product category exceptions
facts.value: The regional terms specifically restrict Microsoft Office programs and keys, illegal file distribution, and adult e-commerce content.

facts.label: Restricted-activity update process
facts.value: MyFatoorah says restricted activities may be updated and may request more information, hold transactions, suspend, or terminate an account.

facts.label: Buyer-country coverage
facts.value: MyFatoorah's public FAQ says international transactions are supported, with currency conversion depending on the merchant's selected plan.

facts.label: Sanctioned and prohibited buyers or counterparties
facts.value: Country terms prohibit transactions involving listed sanctioned persons and several sanctioned countries/jurisdictions.

facts.label: Complete buyer-country allowlist
facts.value: No public complete allowlist of buyer countries, card-issuing countries, or method-specific buyer exclusions was found.

facts.label: Transaction holds
facts.value: MyFatoorah may hold suspicious or potentially unlawful payments for an unspecified period and request supporting evidence before settlement.

facts.label: Reserve policy
facts.value: MyFatoorah may retain an amount calculated from transactions of high-risk merchants; unused reserve is settled when the account closes.

facts.label: Exact reserve percentage and duration
facts.value: No universal reserve percentage or fixed holding duration is published.

facts.label: Approval timing
facts.value: A July 2025 official blog says activation takes less than 24 hours, but it is a marketing estimate and the current live-account guide still requires review and activation by an account manager.

facts.label: Per-country and complex-review timing
facts.value: No separate approval estimate for other countries, high-risk merchants, or multi-vendor suppliers was found.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Payment gateway and payment service provider, with hosted payment pages, payment links, invoices, recurring payment features, and optional multi-vendor settlement.

facts.label: Legal seller and delivery role
facts.value: The merchant sells and delivers its own products or services; MyFatoorah processes the payment and states it is not responsible for the merchant's products or services.

facts.label: Merchant-of-record status
facts.value: MyFatoorah does not present itself as the reseller or merchant of record for the gateway offer.

facts.label: Supported charge currencies
facts.value: The API documentation lists KWD, SAR, BHD, AED, QAR, OMR, JOD, and EGP for the regional country APIs.

facts.label: Cross-border payment currency
facts.value: A payment request may use a display or charge currency different from the gateway method currency; the API returns the method's PaymentCurrencyIso and service charge.

facts.label: Regional card methods
facts.value: MyFatoorah's docs list Visa/Mastercard, American Express, KNET, mada, UAE and Qatar debit cards, and Benefit.

facts.label: Wallets and local digital methods
facts.value: The docs list Apple Pay, Google Pay, STC Pay, Benefit Pay, Samsung Pay, Tamara, Tabby, Fawry, Egypt mobile wallets, and Meeza.

facts.label: Country-specific payment method availability
facts.value: The API's InitiatePayment response returns methods enabled for the account, method currency, whether embedded checkout is supported, and configured service charge.

facts.label: Hosted and embedded method support
facts.value: Hosted payment page supports enabled methods; embedded checkout supports cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and STC Pay, with other enabled methods redirecting when needed.

facts.label: Cash or offline voucher method list
facts.value: No complete list of country-specific cash, bank transfer, or voucher methods was found beyond the named methods in the docs and the account-generated method list.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time payments are supported through payment gateway checkout, invoices, one-time links, and product links.

facts.label: Automatic recurring collection
facts.value: MyFatoorah-managed recurring charges support daily, weekly, monthly, or custom intervals, but the documented managed recurring flow is available only in the V2 payment APIs and requires account-manager activation.

facts.label: Seller-managed recurring
facts.value: Vendor-managed recurring payments are documented for sellers who initiate later charges themselves; this requires tokenized card handling and appropriate account access.

facts.label: Recurring payment links
facts.value: The current payment-links page describes permanent recurring links for monthly subscriptions and ongoing services.

facts.label: Managed recurring schedule
facts.value: Managed recurring can use daily, weekly, monthly, or custom frequency; custom intervals can be 1–180 days.

facts.label: Iterations and retries
facts.value: The V2 recurring model supports a finite iteration count or unlimited (0); failed-payment retry count can be set up to five, with attempts made daily until exhausted or paid.

facts.label: Other subscription billing tools
facts.value: No public docs found for seats, usage billing, proration, trials, coupons, plan changes, or dunning tools beyond recurring retries.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Sellers can redirect customers to a MyFatoorah-hosted payment page showing the account's enabled methods.

facts.label: Embedded checkout
facts.value: Embedded checkout can display the payment experience on the seller site; MyFatoorah handles PCI requirements for this integration.

facts.label: Links, invoices, and product pages
facts.value: Payment links accept a specified amount; product links display a set of products and quantities; invoices can be sent by email, SMS, or returned as a URL.

facts.label: Custom domain and hosted-page limits
facts.value: No public documentation found for a custom checkout domain or public per-plan checkout limits.

facts.label: Developer API and SDKs
facts.value: MyFatoorah publishes REST API documentation, API tokens, and web/mobile SDKs.

facts.label: Official commerce plugins
facts.value: The docs list plugins for CS-Cart, Drupal Commerce, Ecwid, ExpandCart, GoDaddy, Joomla, Laravel, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop, Shopify, Symfony, WHMCS, WooCommerce, Zoho, and others.

facts.label: Shopify setup
facts.value: Shopify integration requires an activated MyFatoorah account/API and a Shopify plan that permits the payment integration.

facts.label: WooCommerce setup
facts.value: An official MyFatoorah WooCommerce plugin is available; it requires a configured WooCommerce site and SSL certificate.

facts.label: Webhooks and payment status
facts.value: Webhooks can notify sellers about payment, refund, recurring, balance-transfer, supplier, and dispute events; MyFatoorah recommends validating signatures and checking payment details.

facts.label: Test environment
facts.value: Sellers can test using a demo account, test cards, or public test token; the documented demo route starts with Kuwait and needs support activation for selected features.

facts.label: Seller tax responsibility
facts.value: The merchant remains responsible for its licensed activity, invoices, customer sale, and country legal compliance. MyFatoorah is a processor, not the seller or tax merchant of record.

facts.label: Tax calculation and collection coverage
facts.value: No jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction tax calculation, collection, filing, or remittance coverage matrix was found.

facts.label: Invoicing and merchant compliance
facts.value: The merchant remains responsible for issuing invoices and records required to verify individual transactions.

facts.label: Payment receipts and invoice links
facts.value: The system can create payment invoices and send their links by email or SMS; payment links also provide downloadable receipts/invoices and notifications.

facts.label: Business tax invoice features
facts.value: Current marketing claims automatic certified invoices compliant with tax systems, but the public docs do not define country coverage, tax-ID fields, or compliance certification.

facts.label: Tax-exempt checkout
facts.value: No tax-exempt purchase or tax-ID validation workflow was found.

facts.label: Seller payout method
facts.value: Bank settlement is the documented payout method; funds go to the bank details recorded with the merchant account.

facts.label: Other payout methods
facts.value: No public docs checked list PayPal, Payoneer, or seller-wallet withdrawals as standard payout choices.

facts.label: Account and settlement currencies
facts.value: API account base currency corresponds to the selected local market; supported regional currency codes are KWD, SAR, BHD, AED, QAR, OMR, JOD, and EGP.

facts.label: Multiple or foreign-currency payouts
facts.value: No public matrix says whether a seller can receive settlement in a currency different from the local account base currency.

facts.label: Regional settlement timing
facts.value: The regional terms say settlement usually occurs within 24 business hours or the next business day, unless the merchant requests another interval; suspicious funds may be held longer.

facts.label: Saudi settlement schedule options
facts.value: The current FAQ says Saudi merchants can choose daily, weekly, or monthly settlements from the dashboard.

facts.label: Initial settlement delay
facts.value: No separate universal first-payout delay or first-settlement reserve period was published.

facts.label: Daily settlement weekday details
facts.value: Arabic MyFatoorah blog text describes a Saudi daily deposit schedule of Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday, while the FAQ gives only “daily, weekly, monthly.”

facts.label: Digital product delivery
facts.value: No native file delivery, licence-key delivery, membership access, or SaaS provisioning feature was found in the product pages or developer docs reviewed.

facts.label: Product and shipping fulfillment
facts.value: Product links collect item, quantity, and delivery details; shipping tools connect courier services and tracking.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: A separate approval-required Multi-Vendor feature lets an account onboard suppliers, assign invoice shares, and manage supplier bank deposits.

facts.label: Multi-vendor pricing
facts.value: No public additional Multi-Vendor subscription or setup price was found; the merchant agreement and quote determine current fees.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: MyFatoorah's reviewed gateway terms restrict Bitcoin companies and exchange platforms and do not present a crypto checkout offer.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto collection or custody product is offered in the reviewed official product pages.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto settlement path is documented.

facts.label: Crypto completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto checkout or crypto refund flow is documented.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: MyFatoorah is a hosted payment service, and no crypto software product is offered.

facts.label: Transaction reporting and exports
facts.value: The gateway page says the dashboard can filter payments and download reports; the API also provides reporting endpoints.

facts.label: Customer and transaction export formats
facts.value: No complete public list of downloadable customer, transaction, tax, or subscription export formats was found.

facts.label: Moving to another provider
facts.value: No public payment-token migration or customer-data portability route to another provider was found.

facts.label: Merchant cancellation
facts.value: The country terms let a merchant terminate with 30 days' notice; the agreement renews yearly unless terminated by either party with the notice period.

facts.label: Inactive accounts
facts.value: Accounts with no transactions for more than six months are considered dormant and may be automatically suspended; updating merchant information is required to reactivate.

facts.label: Final balance and retained records
facts.value: The terms say unused reserve is settled at closure; they do not give a general timetable for releasing all remaining funds. Records are retained for ten years after service discontinuation.

facts.label: Current product and name
facts.value: MyFatoorah is the current name for online payment acceptance, payment links, invoicing, product links, and marketplace payment tools.

facts.label: Regional operator
facts.value: In Saudi Arabia, the current privacy notice identifies Fatoorah For Electronic Marketing, a closed joint stock company, as “MyFatoorah”.

facts.label: Ultimate owner or parent
facts.value: No ultimate owner or parent company is named in the current About, privacy, terms, or contact pages checked.

facts.label: Name history
facts.value: The official Arabic About page says the company began in Kuwait in 2016. A July 2024 post describes a refreshed visual identity, not a product-name change.

facts.label: Acquisition and shutdown check
facts.value: No official acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notice was found on the English or Arabic blog archives, About page, current products page, or official news search.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: MyFatoorah lists country contact emails and phone numbers, plus support through the merchant portal; its product page advertises technical support by phone, live chat, and tickets.

facts.label: Support hours and response promises
facts.value: The Arabic complaints page gives Saudi complaint-desk hours Sunday–Thursday, 9:00–18:00, and an acknowledgement target of one business day. The gateway page separately advertises 24/7 technical support.

facts.label: Current operating status
facts.value: MyFatoorah appears active: its current site lists live payment products in eight countries and developer docs include current v3 APIs and updates.

facts.label: Material recent changes
facts.value: The official blog archive includes product and security articles through September 2025; the company announced a new visual identity in July 2024. No acquisition or sunset item appeared in the checked blog/About material.

facts.label: Legal entity and licence
facts.value: The Saudi notice names Fatoorah For Electronic Marketing, closed joint stock company, CR 1010709742; MyFatoorah lists Saudi Central Bank licence 21/LLC/1444.

facts.label: Security scope
facts.value: Current privacy notice says MyFatoorah uses PCI DSS compliance for card data, encryption in transit, access controls, monitoring, and data masking.

facts.label: Regional contracting entities and licences
facts.value: The public pages checked do not identify the legal contracting company and regulator licence number for each of Kuwait, UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman, Egypt, and Jordan.

facts.label: Currency conversion cost
facts.value: A universal public percentage or fixed FX charge for merchant checkout settlement is not published; any tariffed fee is account/currency specific.
