facts.value: Belgium Bancontact online: One EUR 1.99% + 0.20; Plus EUR 1.49% + 0.15; Pro 0.50% + EUR 0.12 per payment. VAT inclusion not stated.

facts.label: Local-method cost
facts.value: iDEAL is listed as a supported online method for the Netherlands, but the current public country pricing table does not list a method-specific iDEAL processing or refund fee. VAT treatment is therefore not published.

facts.label: Subscription and billing surcharge
facts.value: Recurring card transactions use the online/acquiring service; a separate recurring billing surcharge is not listed in the public checkout tariff. VAT treatment for any account-specific recurring fee is not stated.

facts.label: Subscription and billing surcharge
facts.value: Account plan monthly fee, where used, is separate from per-transaction processing. Recurring billing features require merchant implementation and support activation.

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons
facts.value: myPOS does not advertise a tax calculation, filing or registration service for online sellers in the product and pricing pages checked. Any required VAT collection and filings remain the merchant's responsibility.

facts.label: Tax-service and other checkout add-ons
facts.value: Whether online processing, plan and account-service fees include or add VAT is not stated in the public fee tables reviewed. Hardware store terms say device prices are shown excluding VAT and the final product total includes VAT; that hardware rule does not settle service-fee VAT.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: Full and partial refunds are supported to the original payment method. The public developer guide says refund processing may have a small fee; the exact fee is shown in the merchant's account tariff and varies by market.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: A universal online refund fee and rule for retaining the original processing fee are not published in the current country pricing tables. myPOS says a fee may apply and that an account tariff may show it, but no current public amount is listed. VAT treatment for a refund fee is not stated.

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility
facts.value: Merchant is liable for reversed payments, lost chargebacks, card-scheme amounts and applicable fees. myPOS may debit the balance and place reserves/holds.

facts.label: Dispute cost and responsibility
facts.value: A single standard merchant-acquiring chargeback fee and a fee refund when the merchant wins are not published. The GBP 15 chargeback-initiation line in the UK account tariff is listed under myPOS business-card fees, so it is not treated here as a merchant acquiring dispute fee.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: Approved card receipts settle into the myPOS e-money account within seconds/instantly at no separate instant-settlement charge. The account balance is the payout destination for acquiring funds.

facts.label: Payout cost
facts.value: External bank-transfer fees are account/country and plan specific. Examples on published fee pages include UK SEPA transfer GBP 4 and EUR SEPA transfer EUR 1 on the standard account tariff; newer plans include monthly free transfer quotas. VAT inclusion is not stated.

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: No minimum card-processing settlement amount is published; the service advertises instant credit into the myPOS account.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: myPOS can set or change payment limits for regulation, risk or security reasons and notify the merchant through the account or service website.

facts.label: Payment and account limits
facts.value: A universal public minimum/maximum online transaction amount or fixed monthly collection cap is not published. The checkout must have each charge currency enabled.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: The service pages currently list EEA markets plus the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Gibraltar. Legal eligibility requires the business or sole trader to be established or resident in a country listed for the service.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: A sole trader or legal entity can apply for business use. The terms require legal capacity and an established business or professional activity; personal, household use is excluded.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Applicant's registered business address, or personal address when applying as a sole trader, must be in an eligible service country.

facts.label: Local presence and bank requirements
facts.value: Card proceeds settle to the merchant's myPOS e-money account. myPOS provides the account and IBAN, so a separate bank account is not listed as a prerequisite for receiving card proceeds.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Online signup requires identity and business checks. The current service agreement describes account details, identity documents and a face-to-face video identification step, with possible requests for more evidence.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Online checkout must pass store/API review and testing before production activation. myPOS requires secure HTTPS notification URLs and a completed sandbox test flow.

facts.label: Signup route and minimum business size
facts.value: Merchants start online and submit an account application for approval. A minimum annual revenue or online-payment volume for opening an account is not published.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Physical goods and professional services are covered in general merchant pages. No public allowlist for SaaS, software downloads, memberships, courses or other digital products was found.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: myPOS requires the merchant to use the service for its own lawful business activity; it does not advertise a merchant-of-record or digital-product fulfillment service.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: The acceptance policy restricts illegal activity, counterfeit or infringing goods, child exploitation, illegal gambling, tobacco and pharmaceutical sales in e-commerce, and processing payments for unrelated third parties.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: A complete current matrix for adult content, crypto, AI services, crowdfunding and marketplaces is not published in the public product pages reviewed.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: Payment links are promoted for cross-border sales, but myPOS does not publish a complete buyer-country allow/deny matrix. Card-scheme, sanctions and merchant-risk controls still apply.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Current merchant agreement states a default 10% reserve for Virtual/e-commerce transactions unless otherwise agreed. It may be changed based on merchant risk; held funds can remain reserved up to one year or longer when needed to protect legal interests.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: myPOS also describes reserves/holds as risk-dependent; excessive refunds, chargebacks, suspected breach or legal compliance risks can trigger withholding or suspension.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: myPOS describes online signup and verification but does not publish a guaranteed number of days for identity review, account approval, site certification or enabling recurring payments.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Payment service provider and acquirer with an e-money merchant account. The merchant remains the seller of the goods or services; myPOS processes payment and settles proceeds to the merchant's myPOS account.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Processing currency is selected for the store and must be supported and agreed with myPOS. Current terms name EUR, USD and GBP as examples and allow other supported currencies; no complete public checkout currency list was found.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Account and settlement currencies can differ from the processing currency if the account supports both. myPOS applies its exchange rate and any tariffed conversion fee when it converts.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Online card acceptance includes Visa, Mastercard and their debit/prepaid brands; the developer method list also includes American Express, JCB, Bancontact and iDEAL, with iDEAL identified for the Netherlands.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: myPOS online pages advertise Apple Pay and Google Pay alongside card checkout.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Bancontact is an online method in Belgium, and iDEAL is a Netherlands-specific method in the developer method list.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Cash, bank transfer, mobile-wallet and other local methods are not presented as a single universal online method set; enabled methods vary by country and checkout.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time card payments are supported through hosted checkout, Payment Request and PayLink/PayButton.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Recurring card charging is supported through saved-card tokens and In-App Purchase calls, but it is not enabled by default; the merchant must ask myPOS support to activate it.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: The public documentation describes card-token recurring transactions; a recurring schedule for local methods or wallets is not published.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Stored-card tokenization and subsequent merchant-initiated charges are available. Built-in subscription plans, invoices, dunning, retries, proration, trials and coupon management are not documented as a billing product.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Checkout options include hosted online checkout, a checkout API/SDK, payment links, Payment Requests, payment buttons and Payment Tag.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Hosted checkout redirects the buyer to the myPOS payment page and returns transaction status to the merchant site; PayButtons can be embedded in a site.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Custom-domain checkout and a public limit on the number or lifetime of payment links are not published.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Current developer docs provide Checkout API, PHP/Java/JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, hosted checkout, transaction status, webhook validation and sandbox testing.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Official e-commerce plugins include WooCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Zen Cart, osCommerce, CloudCart, X-Cart and other named platforms.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Payment notifications are sent to a merchant HTTPS URL; the API provides status queries and webhook validation.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Sandbox cards, sandbox credentials and test scenarios are documented; API version support is managed through developer docs.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Merchant remains responsible for setting the buyer price, determining applicable sales taxes/VAT, issuing tax documentation and filing/remitting tax. myPOS does not act as a merchant of record or publish a tax filing service.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Tax handling by country, tax calculation rules and tax-exempt checkout logic are not documented as an included myPOS online feature.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Checkout can return transaction status and transaction details; seller product and tax invoices remain the merchant's responsibility. A buyer-facing myPOS VAT-invoice service is not published.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Acquiring proceeds first settle to the myPOS e-money account. From that balance the merchant can use a myPOS card or request a supported bank transfer; external transfer options depend on account country and currency.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: A complete list of external bank-transfer corridors and seller-bank-country rules for every market is not published in one public page.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Merchant may hold multiple myPOS balances; account marketing says 12 currencies, while legal terms permit EUR, USD, GBP or another supported currency agreed for processing and settlement.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Full account-currency availability by seller country is not listed in one current public matrix.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Card-processing proceeds are credited to the myPOS account within seconds or instantly after approval/settlement; this is the advertised account credit, not a guaranteed arrival time at another bank.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: External bank-transfer arrival estimates by country, weekends and bank holidays are not guaranteed in the online payment material reviewed.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: myPOS processes payments and provides payment status and reporting; it does not advertise file delivery, software-license fulfillment, course access or membership provisioning as a service.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Automatic split settlement of one card payment to multiple unrelated sellers is not offered in the online payment docs; merchants can use separate accounts and transfers, subject to account/API approval.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable to myPOS's documented card, wallet and bank-method acquiring product; no merchant crypto asset/network checkout offer is advertised.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Not applicable: myPOS does not document crypto checkout or crypto custody for merchants.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto-to-fiat or crypto payout route is published for this product.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: myPOS does not document crypto payment confirmations, blockchain settlement or crypto refunds.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: myPOS is a hosted acquiring service and developer API, not self-hosted crypto gateway software.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Dashboard provides online transaction details, payment method/origin, fees, reserve information and refund history. A complete export format and token portability process are not published.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Merchant may terminate a service agreement without a termination charge by notifying myPOS, closing the account and redeeming the available e-money balance.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: myPOS may hold funds up to 180 days after closure where reversals, chargebacks, claims or compliance risks remain; longer where law requires. Account fee pages state e-money redemption on closure is free.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: myPOS is the current brand for the merchant account, online checkout, payment links and payment requests. It became part of Advent International in 2024; no later sale or myPOS rebrand was found in the official newsroom/history pages checked.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Public pages list phone, email and chat support; several market pages advertise 24/7 support. The newer Pro plan advertises priority support.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Supported support languages by country and any paid technical-support response SLA are not published in one full public matrix.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: myPOS is active and taking applications: official product, registration, pricing, developer, help and newsroom pages are live. The newsroom lists 2026 launches and partnerships.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: myPOS announced acquisition by Advent International in 2024 and later announced acquisitions including Toporder and LAVEGO. No official shutdown, service sunset or later ownership-change notice was found in the newsroom/history pages checked.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: myPOS service terms identify the contracting/payment entities by market. UK services identify myPOS Payments Ltd as FCA-authorized electronic-money institution; EEA terms reference myPOS Europe/iCard entities.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: myPOS Checkout pages state PCI-DSS compliance; the public pages reviewed do not give a current certificate scope or independent assessor details for each entity.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Current myPOS terms require identity checks and name the regulated E-money Institution, but a payment-acquiring licence number for every local contract entity is not provided in a single public directory page.

facts.value: Payment in installments is available as an option subject to activity/configuration, but its merchant fee and customer financing conditions are not published.

facts.value: No public ePay sales-tax calculation, filing, tax-registration, or separate fraud-tool price was found.

facts.label: Refund ability

facts.label: Refund fee and original commission
facts.value: Whether NAPS charges a refund fee or returns the original processing commission is not stated in the ePay pricing, payment-link, dashboard, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Dispute fee and loss allocation
facts.value: No public chargeback fee, liability allocation, debit timing, or fee-return-on-win rule was found in the dashboard, public ePay pricing, or linked merchant terms.

facts.label: Chargeback responsibility
facts.value: The merchant can respond to disputes inside Dashboard; public information does not say who bears a final reversed payment or related scheme costs.

facts.label: Payout fee

facts.label: Minimum payout
facts.value: A minimum settlement balance or payout threshold is not published in the ePay, payment-link, or help pages checked.

facts.label: Volume pricing
facts.value: The older official ePay page invites merchants processing more than 250,000 DH per month to contact sales about declining pricing. The current page offers custom pricing for high volume and marketplaces.

facts.label: Per-transaction limits
facts.value: Public minimum/maximum charge amounts, daily transaction caps, and account-tier volume limits were not found in the ePay, help, or integration pages checked.

facts.label: Seller signup country
facts.value: The public ePay offer is for Moroccan merchants and businesses; onboarding requests Moroccan business records and a bank RIB.

facts.label: Foreign seller eligibility
facts.value: Whether a business registered outside Morocco can sign up is not published on the ePay page, help centre, or customer application page checked.

facts.label: Companies
facts.value: Moroccan legal entities may apply; the general checklist includes recent RC, ICE, tax/professional identifier when applicable, representative CIN, company RIB, and company statutes or equivalent.

facts.label: Sole traders and individual merchants
facts.value: A Moroccan individual merchant may apply with recent RC or model 7, CIN, RIB, and professional tax certificate if applicable.

facts.label: Auto-entrepreneurs
facts.value: Moroccan auto-entrepreneurs are listed as eligible applicants with an auto-entrepreneur card, RNAE registration certificate, CIN, and RIB.

facts.label: Associations and organizations
facts.value: Associations or organizations may apply with statutes, proof of legal existence, representative CIN, authorization/board document, and RIB.

facts.label: Franchises and multi-site sellers
facts.value: The ePay page lists franchises, networks, and multi-site organizations, asking for entity, location, bank, and representative information.

facts.label: Local presence and bank account
facts.value: NAPS requires a RIB for settlement. The public profile checklist uses Moroccan business documents; the page does not expressly state whether a foreign bank RIB is accepted.

facts.label: Owner residency and bank-country rules
facts.value: Separate owner-residency, beneficial-owner nationality, and foreign-bank exceptions are not published in the onboarding page, help centre, or terms links checked.

facts.label: Identity and business checks
facts.value: NAPS says it checks the applicant’s identity, legal status, business activity, settlement account, and information required for payment-services compliance.

facts.label: Supporting documents
facts.value: Listed documents vary by legal form and include RC/ICE/tax information, RIB, identity documents, statutes or association proof, and auto-entrepreneur records.

facts.label: Website and store checks
facts.value: NAPS says it reviews the business file, activity, functional needs, and technical environment before activation; a detailed public website-content checklist was not found.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Public signup is a request/application followed by NAPS file review and merchant activation; it is not instant self-service processing.

facts.label: Minimum company size or revenue
facts.value: No general minimum revenue, employee count, or monthly volume for basic signup was found in the ePay, payment-link, help, or application pages checked.

facts.label: Business types served
facts.value: NAPS promotes ePay for e-commerce merchants, businesses, services, platforms, and companies.

facts.label: Entrepreneurs and independents
facts.value: NAPS markets payment links and online acceptance to entrepreneurs and independents, including sellers without a website.

facts.label: SMEs and startups
facts.value: NAPS presents ePay, payment links, Dashboard, and API integration as options for SMEs and startups.

facts.label: Digital versus physical goods
facts.value: No public approval matrix was found for software, SaaS, downloads, courses, memberships, or physical-product categories.

facts.label: Prohibited and restricted activities
facts.value: A full prohibited-business list or risk-category matrix was not published on the ePay page, help centre, or accessible merchant-facing terms reviewed.

facts.label: Marketplaces and high-risk models
facts.value: Marketplaces and platforms can request a customized offer; public pages do not say which marketplace or submerchant models are accepted.

facts.label: Buyer-country coverage
facts.value: NAPS advertises domestic and international card acceptance, so foreign cardholders can pay where their card/network and issuer allow the transaction.

facts.label: Buyer-country and card restrictions
facts.value: Country-level card restrictions, sanctions screening rules, and issuer-country exceptions are not published on the pages checked.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: A general rolling reserve, payout hold schedule, or public triggers for withheld merchant funds are not stated in the ePay, Dashboard, or merchant terms pages checked.

facts.label: Approval and launch estimate
facts.value: NAPS’s older brochure says a merchant may be operational in 48 working hours, conditional on eligibility and acceptance. Current pages say application, approval, integration, and testing are required but give no universal approval deadline.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: NAPS ePay is a payment gateway and NAPS describes NAPS SA as a payment institution providing merchant payment acceptance.

facts.label: Seller of record
facts.value: The merchant sells its own goods or services; NAPS provides payment acceptance and settlement. No merchant-of-record service is described.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: The public ePay and payment-link pages do not list buyer charge currencies. MAD/DH is used for published fees, but that alone does not establish the checkout charge currency.

facts.label: Online card methods
facts.value: NAPS ePay lists Visa, Mastercard, and Maestro for website/app checkout.

facts.label: International and premium cards
facts.value: The ePay price card distinguishes domestic cards from international and premium cards; its current standard international/premium commission is listed separately below.

facts.label: Other checkout methods
facts.value: The online ePay FAQ names cards only. Mobile wallets and local bank-transfer methods were not listed for ePay in the pages checked.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: ePay and payment links support ordinary one-off card payments.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Recurring payments are available as an advanced ePay option; the older ePay pack page associates Card-on-File and recurring payment with Premium.

facts.label: Recurring method limits
facts.value: Card-on-File/tokenization is described for saved cards. The supported recurring card brands, retry schedule, and country/currency limits are not specified publicly.

facts.label: Subscription billing
facts.value: NAPS accepts recurring payment use cases, but the reviewed pages describe payment collection tools rather than a full subscription billing system.

facts.label: Trials, seats, usage, proration, discounts
facts.value: No public ePay feature matrix for trials, seat/usage billing, coupons, plan changes, proration, or metered billing was found.

facts.label: Failed recurring payments
facts.value: The public pages mention reducing unpaid payments but do not provide retry timing, dunning messages, or automatic recovery rules.

facts.label: Hosted/redirect checkout
facts.value: ePay provides a secure payment page; the legacy e-Go page calls it a standard payment page.

facts.label: Integrated and API checkout
facts.value: ePay offers integration through WooCommerce, PrestaShop, API, SDK/PHP, and a page hosted by NAPS; merchant-hosted card entry is limited to certified PCI DSS environments.

facts.label: Payment links
facts.value: ePay Link creates a secure URL from the NAPS Dashboard. Sellers can send links by WhatsApp, email, SMS, social networks, or QR code without a store website.

facts.label: Custom domain and checkout branding
facts.value: Payment-page logo/color customization is listed for ePay; custom domain support and plan-specific branding limits were not published.

facts.label: Public developer documentation
facts.value: NAPS advertises an API and SDK/PHP integration; a public technical API reference was not located from the product and developer pages checked.

facts.label: Official e-commerce integrations
facts.value: NAPS lists plugins/modules for WooCommerce and PrestaShop and an API/SDK route for custom platforms.

facts.label: Sandbox and testing
facts.value: The official guide says NAPS provides a test environment before production activation.

facts.label: Webhooks and event delivery
facts.value: Public information about webhook events, retry rules, and event-signature validation was not found in the ePay FAQ or developer help pages checked.

facts.label: Sales-tax collection and filing
facts.value: NAPS is presented as the payment provider, not seller of record. Public pages do not say NAPS calculates, collects, registers, files, or remits the merchant’s sales taxes.

facts.label: VAT on NAPS fees
facts.value: Setup and payment-link fixed fees explicitly marked HT are excluding VAT. Current ePay annual and percentage/1-DH processing lines do not each state HT or TTC.

facts.label: Transaction confirmation and reporting
facts.value: ePay sends a transaction confirmation to merchant and buyer after validation; Dashboard shows payment status and transaction details.

facts.label: Customer tax invoices
facts.value: A merchant invoice generator, buyer tax-invoice format, VAT-number collection, or tax-exempt workflow is not described in the ePay or payment-link pages checked.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: ePay settles by bank transfer to the merchant’s submitted bank account/RIB.

facts.label: Payout currency
facts.value: The ePay page confirms a bank-account settlement but does not name the settlement currency or foreign-currency account support.

facts.label: Settlement timing
facts.value: NAPS says it processes on J+1 and transfers to the merchant bank account on J+2, subject to applicable conditions and business days.

facts.label: Digital delivery and customer access
facts.value: NAPS sells payment acceptance and does not advertise digital-file delivery, software licensing, or membership-access control as part of ePay.

facts.label: Platform and marketplace support
facts.value: NAPS lists marketplaces/platforms as candidates for a customized merchant offer.

facts.label: Split payments and submerchant onboarding
facts.value: Public documentation for split settlement, submerchant accounts, or marketplace fee routing was not found in the ePay or marketplace pages checked.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: NAPS ePay is a card-payment product; no crypto payment offer was found on NAPS product pages.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable: no NAPS merchant crypto checkout offer was found.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout
facts.value: Not applicable: the researched service settles card payments to a merchant bank account and does not publish crypto settlement.

facts.label: Crypto completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: no crypto invoice or blockchain refund flow is part of the researched product.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: NAPS ePay is a hosted card gateway, not crypto payment software or a self-hosted crypto server.

facts.label: Reports and transaction export
facts.value: Dashboard supports reports, financial history download, transaction filters, and reconciliation; the page says transaction history can be downloaded without a stated time limit.

facts.label: Data portability and migration
facts.value: No customer/card-token export or migration route to another processor is described in the Dashboard, API, or ePay pages checked.

facts.label: Merchant contract and account closure
facts.value: Public merchant cancellation, notice period, termination fee, data retention, and remaining-funds release clauses could not be checked: the official merchant terms link from NAPS’s client flow timed out.

facts.label: Public closure fee
facts.value: A closure or account termination fee is not stated in the available ePay or payment-link price pages.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: NAPS ePay is the online card-acceptance gateway named in the directory’s NAPS Morocco row. NAPS ePay Link is a separate no-website payment-link offer.

facts.label: Operator and owner
facts.value: NAPS says it is a subsidiary of M2M Group.

facts.label: Legal company identity
facts.value: NAPS SA is a Moroccan company registered in Casablanca, RC 130313.

facts.label: Product and brand history
facts.value: The current brand is NAPS. NAPS says its history began in 2012, it launched acquiring in 2017, and it expanded to e-commerce in 2018; no older product name or rebrand notice was found.

facts.label: Status and acquisition notice
facts.value: NAPS is active. On 2025-12-25 the Competition Council authorized NAPS to acquire certain CMI assets consisting of physical-TPE merchant contracts.

facts.label: Support channels and hours
facts.value: NAPS lists a customer-relations centre and contact email; company pages advertise customer support 7 days a week.

facts.label: Support response commitment
facts.value: No public response-time guarantee or paid support tier was found on the ePay, help, or contact pages checked.

facts.label: Current operation
facts.value: NAPS ePay and ePay Link are currently presented with application routes, live pricing, integrations, and settlement details.

facts.label: Shutdown and sunset notices
facts.value: No official NAPS shutdown, closure, or online-offer sunset notice was found in the company news, press, and blog archives checked.

facts.label: Regulatory market change
facts.value: Morocco’s Competition Council made the CMI’s commitments binding in 2024, including a transition to a multi-acquirer market and transfer of merchant contracts; NAPS was the complainant.

facts.label: Regulatory status
facts.value: Bank Al-Maghrib’s 2018 committee notice names NAPS among existing approved entities authorized to extend activity to payment accounts and payment services; its 2024 supervision report lists NAPS SA among payment institutions.

facts.label: Security and card data
facts.value: NAPS describes ePay as protected by 3D Secure and PCI DSS controls; its company guide claims PCI DSS 4.0.1 certification.

facts.label: Privacy and data location

facts.value: Fiat on-ramp/off-ramp requires activation with a supported third-party provider, whose own checks and fees apply.

facts.value: NOWPayments says integration is free and lists transaction-based service fees; no standard setup, monthly or annual subscription charge is shown.

facts.value: Eligible merchants may receive a negotiated custom rate as low as 0.3%; enterprise terms are individually agreed.

facts.label: International card processing
facts.value: No international-card surcharge is published for the core crypto gateway; fiat-partner card pricing is partner-specific.

facts.label: Automatic cross-currency conversion
facts.value: Current pricing lists 1.5% for multi-currency payments/autoconverted payments, plus network fees where an on-chain move occurs.

facts.label: Fixed-rate surcharge

facts.label: Custody conversion
facts.value: Current price page lists 1% for off-chain conversions; a separate help answer lists 0.5% for manual custody conversion.

facts.value: Fiat partner methods such as card/bank transfers have provider- and location-specific fees; no universal local-method table is published by NOWPayments.

facts.label: Refund of merchant sale
facts.value: Because core crypto payments settle to the merchant's wallet, the merchant initiates a customer refund from its own wallet; crypto transfers cannot be reversed.

facts.label: Refund costs
facts.value: Network fees apply to refunds; NOWPayments fees/remuneration are non-refundable under the current terms.

facts.label: Failed or wrong-asset payment refunds
facts.value: Stuck/failed payments may be returned case by case after support contact and validation; wrong network, wrong coin, missing memo/tag or under-minimum deposits are common cases.

facts.label: Disputes and chargebacks
facts.value: Crypto transactions are irreversible and do not support card-style chargebacks; merchant handles customer disputes and manual refunds.

facts.label: Risk holds
facts.value: NOWPayments or a third-party provider can suspend, delay or refuse transactions for suspected fraud, legal/compliance reasons or technical problems.

apps.name: OpenNode
apps.line: Bitcoin and Lightning checkout with wallet, conversion and payout tools.

free.text: No setup, minimum, monthly or annual fee

cells.type: Bitcoin payment processor and settlement service
cells.payout: Lightning in seconds; on-chain often under 10 minutes

fee.math: One typical Bitcoin payment rate is published and used in every country. The full list of seller countries isn't published.
One typical Bitcoin payment rate is published and used in every country. The full list of seller countries isn't published.

apps.news: The official press room and company-news archive had no acquisition, licence change, or shutdown announcement; the newest listed company item was 2022-09-13.

facts.label: Required gateway or bank account
facts.value: No separate card gateway is needed for Bitcoin checkout. A linked USD bank account is needed only for USD wallet transfers/conversion.

facts.label: Verification dependency
facts.value: Production merchant onboarding requires registered-business KYB and identity checks before USD bank features can be enabled.

facts.label: Setup and recurring fixed fees
facts.value: OpenNode says it charges no setup, minimum, monthly, or annual fee.

facts.label: Typical processing price
facts.value: Typical processing fees for payments and payouts are 1%.

facts.label: Custom pricing
facts.value: OpenNode asks businesses with volume, high-value, high-risk, or strategic needs to contact it for pricing; the public site shows no standard rate card by plan.

facts.label: Pricing page switches
facts.value: The pricing page has amount and currency selectors in its conversion calculator, but no seller-country, plan, or billing-period switch exposing a different public fee.

facts.label: Nonprofit price exception
facts.value: For eligible US 501(c)(3) nonprofits, the first $50,000 in donations has no processing fee; the page states 1% after that.

facts.label: International card price
facts.value: Not applicable: no international card-acquiring method is described for the current Bitcoin checkout.

facts.label: Conversion charge
facts.value: OpenNode says Bitcoin-to-fiat conversion is free; no conversion fee is charged by OpenNode.

facts.label: Automatic fiat conversion
facts.value: Automatic conversion at payment is limited to approved US-based businesses with a USD bank account.

facts.label: Local payment method cost
facts.value: Not applicable to local bank/card payment methods: customers pay using Bitcoin on-chain or Lightning.

facts.label: Billing surcharge
facts.value: No separate invoice or recurring billing surcharge is published; invoices are a Bitcoin payment workflow, not a subscription billing plan.

facts.label: Tax service
facts.value: No automated tax calculation, collection, filing, or remittance add-on is published.

facts.label: Manual tax input
facts.value: Payment requests let a merchant add a tax percentage to the requested amount.

facts.label: General customer refunds
facts.value: General merchant refunds are not an automatic reversal; OpenNode says merchants can contact support for help initiating a Bitcoin refund.

facts.label: Under/overpayment refund
facts.value: For an on-chain underpayment or overpayment refund, OpenNode subtracts 200 satoshis (0.00000200 BTC) for network fees; refunds are typically completed within 24 hours.

facts.label: Refund destination and unknown fee
facts.value: Under/overpayment refunds require a Bitcoin on-chain address and are not sent to a Lightning invoice. General refund fee and return of the original processing fee are not published.

facts.label: Chargebacks
facts.value: Bitcoin payments have no card-network chargeback mechanism; once confirmed on-chain they cannot be reversed through OpenNode.

facts.label: Buyer disputes and loss responsibility
facts.value: OpenNode terms say the merchant and customer are solely responsible for resolving transaction disputes; OpenNode will not mediate.

facts.label: Scheduled BTC payout
facts.value: Scheduled on-chain Bitcoin withdrawals are free, run each Sunday at 11:30 UTC, and require at least 0.001 BTC.

facts.label: On-demand Bitcoin payout
facts.value: On-demand on-chain BTC withdrawals cost 1%; instant Lightning withdrawals are free.

facts.label: USD bank payout fee
facts.value: USD bank-transfer fees and minimums vary by transfer method and bank partner; no single public fee amount is given.

facts.label: Payout calculation example
facts.value: Our calculation: on a 0.01 BTC on-demand on-chain withdrawal, the 1% withdrawal charge is 0.0001 BTC: 0.01 BTC × 0.01 = 0.0001 BTC.

facts.label: Scheduled Bitcoin minimum
facts.value: Minimum balance for scheduled Bitcoin transfer is 0.001 BTC.

facts.label: On-demand on-chain Bitcoin minimum
facts.value: Minimum amount for an instant on-chain withdrawal is 0.002 BTC.

facts.label: USD bank minimum
facts.value: Scheduled USD bank withdrawals require $500; one-time USD bank transfers have no minimum.

facts.label: Lightning payout minimum
facts.value: A separate minimum for Lightning withdrawals is not published in the payout guide.

facts.label: On-chain request amount range
facts.value: Minimum on-chain payment request is 542 satoshis; maximum is listed as no limit.

facts.label: Lightning request amount range
facts.value: Minimum Lightning payment request is 1 satoshi; maximum is 5 BTC.

facts.label: API charge lifetime
facts.value: API charge TTL is configurable from 10 minutes to 4,320 minutes (72 hours), with a default of 1,440 minutes (24 hours).

facts.label: Account volume limits
facts.value: No standard merchant account transaction-volume cap is published in the public pricing or help pages checked.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: OpenNode says it serves 120+ countries, but that figure does not identify eligible merchant-incorporation countries. The complete seller signup list is not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: USD settlement seller geography
facts.value: USD conversion, settlement, and bank transfers are for US-based businesses; automatic USD conversion is limited and requires OpenNode approval based on expected volume.

facts.label: US state restrictions
facts.value: A help article says USD conversion and transfers are unavailable to businesses and individuals in Alaska, Arkansas, Connecticut, New York, North Carolina, and Texas.

facts.label: Company and individual legal forms
facts.value: The current verification guide says accounts are available to registered businesses only.

facts.label: Sole traders
facts.value: The guide does not say whether a registered sole trader or sole proprietorship meets its business-registration requirement.

facts.label: Business registration evidence
facts.value: KYB asks for one document proving the company's legal existence, such as an incorporation certificate or registry extract.

facts.label: USD bank account
facts.value: US businesses need a USD bank account to use USD conversion and withdrawals. The USD wallet's bank account is held in the business's name.

facts.label: KYB ownership documents
facts.value: OpenNode asks for a document establishing all control persons when there is more than one owner or the applicant does not own over 25%.

facts.label: Business address verification
facts.value: One document showing the business name and address is required; utility and bank statements must be within three months, while the guide also lists recent tax returns and government certificates.

facts.label: KYC for owners or controllers
facts.value: OpenNode requests identity data for beneficial owners with over 25% ownership, or the account control person if no owner exceeds that threshold.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: A public signup route and separate development environment are documented, but production account approval is discretionary under the terms.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No minimum revenue or monthly processing volume is published for standard merchant signup. USD automatic conversion has a separate volume qualification by support.

facts.label: Products and services
facts.value: The payment product is presented for ecommerce, products, services, invoices, donations, and in-person sales, subject to review and the acceptable-use terms.

facts.label: Digital delivery and subscriptions
facts.value: The docs do not publish a specific approval rule for SaaS, downloads, courses, or memberships; subscriptions over one year are listed as high-risk/restricted.

facts.label: Nonprofit donation offer
facts.value: OpenNode advertises waived processing fees for US 501(c)(3) nonprofits on their first $50,000 of donations; later processing is 1%.

facts.label: Financial services and third-party funds
facts.value: Terms prohibit money transmission, money services, bill pay, crowdfunding, insurance, and holding or aggregating funds owed to third parties.

facts.label: Other high-risk or prohibited businesses
facts.value: Terms list illegal gambling, counterfeit or infringing goods, deceptive/no-value services, drug paraphernalia, MLM, false health claims, and other partner-restricted or elevated-risk businesses.

facts.label: Restricted subscription term
facts.value: Subscriptions longer than one year are specifically listed among high-risk businesses.

facts.label: Buyer locations
facts.value: OpenNode promotes Bitcoin acceptance from around the world, but terms do not guarantee availability in every jurisdiction. A complete buyer-country allowlist was not found.

facts.label: Sanctions and prohibited counterparties
facts.value: Terms prohibit transactions with persons or entities subject to US OFAC sanctions; sanctioned-jurisdiction currencies are not supported for payment requests.

facts.label: Holds and freezes
facts.value: Terms permit account suspension or withdrawal restrictions for suspected breaches, identity review, or legal process.

facts.label: Standard reserve policy
facts.value: No standard rolling-reserve percentage or holding period is published.

facts.label: Approval-time estimate
facts.value: A standard KYB or account approval time is not published.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Bitcoin payment processor and wallet/settlement service; not a merchant of record.

facts.label: Seller to the buyer
facts.value: The merchant sells its own goods or services and is responsible for customer identity, receiving full payment, and resolving transaction disputes.

facts.label: Payment request display currencies
facts.value: Merchants can create Bitcoin payment requests from most fiat currencies; the currency calculator supports 190+ source currencies.

facts.label: Unsupported currency codes
facts.value: The current help list excludes ANG, ARS, BAM, BGN, CUC, ETB, HRK, SDG, SLL, SSP, VEF, VES, XAF, XOF, XPF, and ZWL, as well as currencies of sanctioned jurisdictions.

facts.label: Customer payment methods
facts.value: Checkout accepts Bitcoin on-chain or through Lightning; the payer uses a Bitcoin wallet, QR code, wallet link, or copied payment address/invoice.

facts.label: Cards and local payment methods
facts.value: Current merchant product and payment docs describe Bitcoin checkout; card acquiring and non-Bitcoin local payment methods are not offered as checkout methods in the pages checked.

facts.label: One-time payment
facts.value: Yes. Dashboard payment requests create one-off on-chain or Lightning checkouts.

facts.label: Automatic recurring collection
facts.value: No automatic subscription billing or scheduled card collection is described in the merchant help or developer docs checked.

facts.label: Subscription method limits
facts.value: No recurring payment method or subscription retry schedule is published.

facts.label: Invoicing
facts.value: Dashboard invoices support itemized products or services, a due date, PDF download, email, and a permanent payment link; invoices can be voided.

facts.label: Overdue invoice recovery
facts.value: Invoice states include open, overdue, paid, and void. The docs do not describe automatic payment retries.

facts.label: Failed or partial payment recovery
facts.value: For an on-chain underpayment, the payer can top up the missing amount or request a refund; the merchant can set an underpaid acceptance threshold.

facts.label: Other subscription features
facts.value: Trials, metered billing, coupons, seats, prorations, plan changes, and automatic retries are not published as billing features.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Yes. API-created charges return a hosted checkout URL; the merchant can redirect buyers to OpenNode checkout or build its own interface from the Bitcoin payment URI.

facts.label: Payment buttons and links
facts.value: Merchants can create customizable “Pay with Bitcoin” buttons and shareable payment template links; donation templates allow the buyer to choose an amount.

facts.label: In-person checkout
facts.value: The mobile POS uses a payment request on the merchant's phone; the buyer pays using a QR code or wallet link.

facts.label: Checkout customization and custom domain
facts.value: Business name/logo and request information can be customized. Custom domains, hosted checkout branding controls, and per-plan limits were not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: API
facts.value: REST API supports creating charges, querying payments, exchanges, balances, refunds for underpayments, and Bitcoin withdrawals.

facts.label: Webhooks
facts.value: Callback webhooks report charge and withdrawal status changes, including paid, expired, underpaid, refunded, failed, and confirmed.

facts.label: Sandbox
facts.value: Separate development and production environments are documented. Development uses Bitcoin testnet and testnet-connected Lightning infrastructure.

facts.label: Official libraries and ecommerce plugins
facts.value: Official API libraries are listed for Node.js and PHP; help pages cover Shopify, WooCommerce, and Magento integrations.

facts.label: Event test tool
facts.value: Developer docs include a webhook simulator that sends sample charge events without a real payment.

facts.label: Seller tax responsibility
facts.value: Merchant is responsible for taxes arising from its use of OpenNode; terms disclaim tax advice.

facts.label: Tax coverage by country
facts.value: No supported tax jurisdiction list or tax registration/filing service is published.

facts.label: Buyer invoices and records
facts.value: Dashboard invoices can be itemized and downloaded as PDF or sent by email/link; transaction history can be exported.

facts.label: Tax IDs and exemption handling
facts.value: Business tax-ID capture, tax-exempt buyer handling, and jurisdiction-specific fiscal invoice compliance are not published.

facts.label: Bitcoin payout methods
facts.value: Merchant can withdraw Bitcoin to an external on-chain wallet or send it over Lightning.

facts.label: Fiat payout method
facts.value: Eligible US businesses can withdraw USD to a linked destination bank account.

facts.label: Stablecoin payout method
facts.value: No stablecoin wallet or stablecoin payout option is described in current product or payout documentation.

facts.label: Bitcoin settlement currency
facts.value: Merchant can retain accepted funds as BTC in the OpenNode Bitcoin wallet and withdraw to an external Bitcoin wallet.

facts.label: Fiat settlement currency
facts.value: The October 2026 currency guide names USD for settlement and bank transfers for US-based businesses.

facts.label: Older local-currency marketing
facts.value: The settlement marketing page still says “8 supported local currencies,” while the October 2026 support guide lists USD for settlement and bank transfer.

facts.label: Bitcoin payment settlement
facts.value: Lightning payments are marked paid when received; on-chain payments move to paid after confirmation, and on-chain confirmation time depends on Bitcoin network conditions.

facts.label: USD bank payout timing
facts.value: Scheduled USD transfers process daily at 8:00 AM ET and should reach the bank the same business day; transfers initiated after cutoff generally arrive next business day (T+1).

facts.label: Bitcoin withdrawal timing
facts.value: Scheduled Bitcoin withdrawal is weekly Sunday 11:30 UTC; on-demand Lightning is usually within seconds, while on-chain typically settles within one block and often under 10 minutes.

facts.label: Product fulfillment
facts.value: OpenNode records payment status and notifies merchant systems; the merchant's store or application remains responsible for delivering products, downloads, or access.

facts.label: Donation receipts
facts.value: OpenNode provides a completed-transaction record; the nonprofit is responsible for providing any donor tax receipt.

facts.label: Marketplace and split payouts
facts.value: Terms prohibit collecting or aggregating money owed to third parties. Split settlement documented by OpenNode divides one merchant's payment between BTC and USD, not multiple sellers.

facts.label: Marketplace account support
facts.value: A managed multi-seller marketplace payment product is not published.

facts.label: Accepted crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Current merchant checkout accepts Bitcoin (BTC) on the Bitcoin blockchain and through the Bitcoin Lightning Network.

facts.label: Other coins and stablecoins
facts.value: No other coin, token, or stablecoin is listed in current merchant payment documentation.

facts.label: Custody of BTC
facts.value: OpenNode is custodial while BTC is held in the account's platform wallet; merchants can withdraw to an external Bitcoin wallet.

facts.label: Custody of USD
facts.value: For eligible automatic conversion, USD is credited to a wallet powered by bank partners and held in a bank account in the merchant's name.

facts.label: Fiat and crypto settlement choices
facts.value: Merchants can settle in BTC, or eligible US-based businesses can convert and withdraw USD; marketing claims of other local settlement currencies conflict with current support guidance.

facts.label: Stablecoin settlement
facts.value: No stablecoin settlement option is published.

facts.label: Conversion cost
facts.value: OpenNode says it charges no conversion fee for converting between BTC and supported fiat.

facts.label: Payment completion
facts.value: Lightning payments are reported paid when received; on-chain invoices pass through processing until one or more confirmations and may expire if unpaid.

facts.label: Underpayment and overpayment
facts.value: On-chain underpayments can be topped up or refunded; overpayments can be refunded to an on-chain BTC address. OpenNode deducts 200 sats and says completion is typically within 24 hours.

facts.label: General refund and price risk
facts.value: A merchant refund is a new BTC transfer, not a charge reversal; the merchant bears BTC price movement and network conditions.

facts.label: Refund fee coverage
facts.value: The 200-sat deduction is stated for under/overpayment refunds; a general merchant refund fee is not published.

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: OpenNode is a hosted payment service; merchants do not self-host the processor or maintain a Bitcoin node to use its checkout.

facts.label: Merchant infrastructure cost
facts.value: No OpenNode server-hosting cost is required; standard setup/monthly/yearly fees are not charged, though merchant website, ecommerce, and third-party integration costs may apply.

facts.label: Transaction exports
facts.value: Payment, transfer, conversion, and account-summary records can be exported as CSV or XLS and downloaded from an emailed link.

facts.label: Provider migration
facts.value: A migration service to another processor is not published; merchant can export records and use API data.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Help says account closure requires contacting support. The terms allow either party to terminate at any time by notice.

facts.label: Funds and data after closure
facts.value: Terms say remaining crypto may be converted to fiat and sent to a bank account supplied by the customer, less fees, within a reasonable time; OpenNode may delete the account or content.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: OpenNode is a Bitcoin and Lightning payment processor for merchants, with checkout, invoicing, conversion, and payout tools.

facts.label: Contracting company
facts.value: Public terms name OpenNode, Inc., a Delaware corporation.

facts.label: Parent, acquisition, or rebrand
facts.value: No parent company, acquisition, or rebrand is identified in the current terms or the official press room and company-news pages checked.

facts.label: Product history
facts.value: OpenNode announced a Stripe app in 2022 for US Stripe merchants to convert Stripe proceeds to Bitcoin. The current Stripe product page still says “Coming soon,” so current availability is not established.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: OpenNode publishes email and help-center chatbot support; discrepancy articles describe support access as 24/7.

facts.label: Support languages and response times
facts.value: Public support hours by language and guaranteed response times are not published.

facts.label: Live service status
facts.value: The official status page showed all systems operational on 2026-11-07, including payments, Bitcoin nodes, API, and BTC withdrawals; no incident was listed that day.

facts.label: Market and product focus
facts.value: 2020 company material described remittance, wallet, and local-currency corridors; 2022 updates announced fintech/Stripe partnerships. Current pages emphasize merchant Bitcoin checkout, invoices, in-person POS, and US USD settlement.

facts.label: Prime Trust historical exposure
facts.value: A 2025 bankruptcy-court complaint alleges OpenNode used Prime Trust for payment rails, liquidity, settlement, and custodial services in 2023.

facts.label: Legal entity and regulatory statement
facts.value: Terms identify OpenNode, Inc. as a Delaware corporation. OpenNode's product page says it is a registered money services business and follows AML, anti-terrorist-financing, and OFAC requirements.

facts.label: FinCEN registry verification
facts.value: The FinCEN MSB search page loaded, but its search interface did not expose a result for OpenNode in this check.

facts.label: Security certifications
facts.value: No named PCI, SOC, or other independent security certification and scope was found on the product, terms, or help pages checked.

facts.value: Ozow's merchant terms cover payments for merchant goods and services, subject to legality, risk review and any method-specific restrictions.

facts.value: Payrexx Pay Plus lists Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Diners Club, Discover, Apple/Google Pay, iDEAL, SEPA Direct Debit, EPS, Bancontact, Alipay, WeChat Pay, Klarna and Przelewy24.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: The public payment-method index also lists Visa Click to Pay, Mastercard Click to Pay, PayPal, JCB, UnionPay, V Pay, and other external methods; availability depends on PSP and account.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Payrexx supports checkout pages and payment links; card wallets use the underlying card fee rather than a separate Payrexx wallet fee.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time online payments are supported by Payrexx Pay and Payrexx Pay Plus.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Payrexx Pay supports recurring payments only for tokenization-capable methods: TWINT, PostFinance Pay, Mastercard, Visa, Samsung Pay, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Payrexx Pay Plus does not support Payrexx-managed recurring payments; use a different provider if it supports subscriptions.

facts.label: Recurring payments and method limits
facts.value: Payrexx supports API tokenization for recurring/variable charges, but there is no single universal recurring method or seller-country matrix across external PSPs.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Subscription periods can be daily, weekly, monthly or annual; subscription records show status, billing period, duration and cancellation notice.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Failed Payrexx-managed subscription charges retry once daily for seven days, then the subscription is marked failed.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Pages supports products/variants, inventory and discount codes; subscription tool supports recurring products and customer self-service.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Seat-based pricing, metered billing and usage aggregation are not described as native subscription features in the checked subscription and developer docs.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Hosted Payrexx payment pages, mini-shop Pages, Paylink, invoice payment page, Terminal page, QR Pay and Donation pages are available.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Pages can be embedded by iframe and styled with logo, fonts, colors and look-and-feel profiles.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Payment links can be shared by email and personalized; Paylink docs say SMS and WhatsApp sending are not included.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Payrexx provides a REST API, API keys, official plugins and webhooks; the current merchant API is version 1.13.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Webhooks report transaction, subscription and payout events; failed deliveries can be retried up to 10 times.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Test mode is available for Payrexx Pay/Pay Plus and transaction exports can filter live versus test payments.

facts.label: Integration and testing
facts.value: Free plan access to plugins/API is unclear: marketing pricing lists API and plugins with Free, while the plan documentation says plugins and custom API integrations are excluded.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Payrexx is a gateway; the merchant sells to the buyer and handles its own tax obligations, registrations, collection and filing.

facts.label: Tax responsibilities and coverage
facts.value: Payrexx lets the merchant configure tax rates and tax treatment on invoices, but this does not make Payrexx the tax filer or remitter.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Payrexx can send a PDF payment receipt with order confirmation and lets merchants create/send buyer invoices with VAT treatments and payment links.

facts.label: Receipts and business invoices
facts.value: Payrexx does not publish a universal tax-compliant invoice format for every seller country; the seller configures the invoice and tax details.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Payrexx Pay pays directly to the merchant's configured bank account; Pay Plus payouts are processed by the partner bank (currently shown in payout reports as Stripe UK).

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Payrexx uses bank payout accounts; supported account-currency/country combinations include CHF, EUR, USD, GBP and DKK.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Payout currencies: CHF, EUR, USD, GBP and DKK, with bank-country combinations listed by Payrexx.

facts.label: Payout and balance currencies
facts.value: Payrexx says CHF/EUR payouts have no exchange fee when the payout is made to a matching currency account; other currencies can require conversion.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Default payout interval is weekly, processed Monday; new online merchants have a 4-day delay, adjustable from 3 to 8 days by risk and eligibility.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Daily, weekly and monthly payouts are supported; daily payouts can be requested after at least 3 months and remain risk/industry dependent.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Bank transfer may take about 3 business days after Payrexx initiates payout; weekends/holidays can extend the calendar wait.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: Payrexx Pages creates a mini-shop with products, variants, stock, discount codes and subscription options; Paylink, Invoice and Donation provide hosted payment tools.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: No automatic digital file delivery, software-license issuance or membership access integration is published in the reviewed e-commerce tools overview.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Payrexx offers a separate platform/marketplace/white-label product from CHF 199 per month; platform API can onboard/manage merchants and submit KYC information.

facts.label: Multi-seller and split payments
facts.value: Platform offer can process and pay out merchant transactions; platform partners receive a buy-rate and may set downstream fees.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Payrexx lists a Crypto payment method and a separate Centi method; the online fee table lists Crypto at 1.45% with CHF 0.00 fixed fee.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: The reviewed public payment-method pages do not identify a complete coin/token and blockchain-network matrix for Payrexx Crypto or Centi.

facts.label: Who controls crypto funds
facts.value: Custody/control of any crypto assets is not described in the reviewed Payrexx payment-method, terms or refund pages.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout path
facts.value: Crypto-to-fiat conversion, supported payout assets/networks and conversion charges are not detailed on the reviewed official public pages.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: The Payrexx Pay feature matrix says Crypto has no dashboard refund support; blockchain confirmation, expired payment and under/overpayment rules were not found.

facts.label: Hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Payrexx is a hosted, browser-based payment service; the merchant integrates through hosted tools, API or plugins and does not deploy the payment gateway software.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Merchants can export transaction and customer records as CSV/Excel, payout reports as CSV/XLSX/PDF, and annual statements as PDF.

facts.label: Exports and moving providers
facts.value: Customer data can be imported from CSV/XLSX; card-token and subscription migration to another PSP is not established by the reviewed export docs.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: A merchant can end a plan in Plan & Billing; paid plans run on 1-, 2- or 3-year renewals, and downgrading waits until the active term ends.

facts.label: Closing an account
facts.value: Account deletion is irreversible and removes transactions; it is only available when no Payrexx invoices remain outstanding.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Payrexx is the online payments gateway and e-commerce platform operated by PAYREXX AG, a Swiss company registered in Thun.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Payrexx Europe AG is a 100% subsidiary of PAYREXX AG and handles EEA market entry and promotion.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: The current shareholder percentages/control of PAYREXX AG are not published. Payrexx disclosed a CHF 2.5 million Series A investment involving INS Holding AG and an Icelandic investor consortium in December 2023; it did not announce a change of control or acquisition.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Ticket support is included across online plans; published support guidance says written tickets usually get a reply within one business day and within 72 hours maximum.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Standard/Premium pricing lists phone support Monday–Friday, 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00; Premium also includes prioritized support.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Support documentation is available in the Payrexx knowledge base; no public service-level response guarantee for account review or payouts was found.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Payrexx currently advertises live merchant plans and publishes current product/news content. Its company press page and blog were checked for acquisition or shutdown notices; none was found.

facts.label: Operating status and recent changes
facts.value: Product renames: Payrexx Swiss Collecting became Payrexx Pay; Payrexx Direct became Payrexx Pay Plus.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: PAYREXX AG is a member of VQF, a Swiss self-regulatory organization for financial intermediaries; Payrexx states it is not a bank.

facts.label: Legal entity, licence and security scope
facts.value: Payrexx Europe AG is the Liechtenstein EEA subsidiary; Payrexx Pay Plus payout reports identify partner-bank processing (Stripe UK).
