facts.value: Plisio publishes no general local registration, owner-residency, or bank-country rule for merchants.

facts.label: Seller bank account
facts.value: A bank account is not listed as a prerequisite in the published crypto invoice and address-withdrawal flow.

facts.label: Identity checks
facts.value: FAQ and security pages say Plisio does not require proof of identity; the linked AML/KYC PDF says suspicious transactions may be held for identity verification through Sumsub.

facts.label: Merchant KYB documents
facts.value: No standard merchant KYB checklist, business-document list, or routine review procedure was published in the merchant docs and terms checked.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: The site offers public signup and describes free account creation; merchant API use requires a Plisio account and API secret.

facts.label: Minimum business size or volume
facts.value: No minimum revenue, monthly volume, or business-size requirement is published for the standard gateway.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: The gateway is marketed for website and store payments, invoices, donations, and multiple integrations; it does not publish a complete approved-product matrix.

facts.label: Product approval list
facts.value: The pages checked do not give a complete allowed-products or merchant-vertical list.

facts.label: Restrictions
facts.value: Users must comply with applicable law and sanctions restrictions; Plisio may deny, suspend, or terminate access for inactivity, suspected compromise, or term violations.

facts.label: Adult, gambling, and high-risk categories
facts.value: The current official terms and merchant docs checked do not settle eligibility for these categories.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: The docs publish sanctions and legal restrictions but no complete current buyer-country payment blocklist.

facts.label: Sanctioned buyers
facts.value: Terms prohibit transactions with or on behalf of sanctioned or restricted persons and certain sanctioned territories.

facts.label: Reserve and funds-hold policy
facts.value: No standard reserve percentage or duration is published; terms allow account suspension, regulatory-request freezes, and sanctions-related holds.

facts.label: Risk review hold
facts.value: AML/KYC policy says a suspicious transaction may be placed on hold while identity is checked; if verification is refused in the described exchange flow, funds are returned minus network fees.

facts.label: Approval time
facts.value: No public merchant-approval estimate was found. The AML document describes a three-day response window for a risk-triggered identity check, not initial merchant approval.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Crypto payment gateway and crypto wallet service; not a card acquirer or merchant of record.

facts.label: Seller of record
facts.value: The merchant creates the order and remains responsible for its sale; no merchant-of-record service is described in the product docs or terms.

facts.label: Invoice denomination
facts.value: API invoices may be denominated in one of 167 listed fiat currencies using source_currency and source_amount, then request payment in supported crypto.

facts.label: Checkout charge currency
facts.value: Customers pay the invoice in one of the crypto assets enabled for that Plisio store; ordinary card and bank charge currencies are not part of this gateway.

facts.label: Payment methods
facts.value: Crypto transfers only: supported coins and tokens on their listed chains. No card, bank-transfer, or mobile-money checkout is documented.

facts.label: Buyer checkout routes
facts.value: Hosted invoice page, merchant-integrated API, and dashboard-created invoice link or QR code are documented.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time order invoices are supported through API and invoice links.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Automatic recurring subscription collection is not documented in the API, pricing, or integrations pages checked.

facts.label: Payment-method limits for renewals
facts.value: No recurring crypto schedule, retry rule, subscription mandate, or renewal method matrix is published.

facts.label: Subscription billing features
facts.value: Seats, usage billing, trials, discounts, plan changes, prorations, and dunning are not documented as Plisio gateway features.

facts.label: Failed payment recovery
facts.value: API callbacks report invoice status changes, but no subscription retry or dunning workflow is published.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Standard API can return or redirect to a hosted Plisio invoice page.

facts.label: Embedded / white-label checkout
facts.value: White Label allows custom invoice design and checkout without redirecting to Plisio; published fee is 1.5% with asset-specific exceptions below.

facts.label: Payment links and QR
facts.value: Dashboard invoices can be shared by link or QR code without connecting an API.

facts.label: API and developer docs
facts.value: Public REST API docs cover invoice creation, transaction status, account balance, fee plans, fee estimates, and withdrawals.

facts.label: Webhooks / callbacks
facts.value: Invoice API supports callback URLs for status updates and separate success and failure callbacks.

facts.label: Plugins and SDKs
facts.value: Official integration page lists plugins for platforms including BigCommerce, Blesta, Botble, CS-Cart, Easy Digital Downloads, Ecwid, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop, Shopware, VirtueMart, WHMCS, WooCommerce, X-Cart, XenForo, and Zender.

facts.label: Test mode
facts.value: A public test-mode or sandbox environment was not identified in the API docs, pricing, or integration pages checked.

facts.label: Tax responsibility
facts.value: Plisio is presented as payment infrastructure rather than merchant of record; merchants remain responsible for their own product sales and taxes.

facts.label: Tax jurisdictions covered
facts.value: No list of supported tax jurisdictions, tax calculation, or tax remittance coverage is published.

facts.label: Payment receipt and transaction records
facts.value: API includes invoice identifiers, amounts, status updates, and callback details; dashboard provides transaction history.

facts.label: Business tax invoice and tax-ID fields
facts.value: No tax-ID collection, tax exemption, or compliant tax invoice feature was found in the invoice API or merchant docs checked.

facts.label: Crypto payout methods
facts.value: Merchant can cash out or send mass payouts to one or more blockchain addresses using supported crypto assets.

facts.label: Bank, PayPal, or card payout
facts.value: No bank, PayPal, or card payout method appears in the public merchant cash-out API.

facts.label: Balance currencies
facts.value: Plisio documents a multi-currency crypto account; accepted assets and networks are listed in the supported-cryptocurrency appendix.

facts.label: Fiat balance / payout currencies
facts.value: No seller fiat balance or bank-payout currency list was found; API fiat values are invoice denomination and exchange-rate reference fields.

facts.label: Settlement path
facts.value: Standard product docs show balances in Plisio accounts followed by seller withdrawals; a 2026 official marketing article instead claims direct-to-merchant-wallet settlement.

facts.label: Payout timing
facts.value: Plisio advertises “instant transfers,” while actual transfers depend on blockchain confirmation, network congestion, and the selected normal or priority fee plan.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: Not applicable as a built-in delivery tool: Plisio processes the payment, while download, licence, membership, and customer-access fulfilment are not offered in the gateway docs checked.

facts.label: Marketplace and split payments
facts.value: Mass payout can send to multiple wallet addresses, but a split-payment or marketplace seller-onboarding product tied to a buyer charge was not documented.

facts.label: Supported native coins
facts.value: Current appendix lists BTC, ETH, ETH on Base, LTC, DASH, ZEC, DOGE, BCH, XMR, TRX, BNB/BSC, ETC, TON, and SOL.

facts.label: Supported stablecoins and tokens
facts.value: Appendix lists USDT on Ethereum, Tron, BSC, TON, and Solana; USDC on Ethereum, Base, BSC, and Solana; plus TUSD, SHIB, APE, BTT, BUSD, and LoveBit on their listed networks.

facts.label: Asset availability limits
facts.value: The appendix says the Dashboard is authoritative for enabled assets and warns that unsupported chain or contract transfers may be lost.

facts.label: Accepted checkout networks
facts.value: Published network families include Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base, Litecoin, Dash, Zcash, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Monero, Tron/TRC-20, BSC/BEP-20, Ethereum Classic, TON, and Solana/SPL.

facts.label: Standard account custody
facts.value: FAQ says Plisio stores funds on remote servers disconnected from the internet; pricing advertises 90% of funds in cold wallets; account and withdrawal APIs expose Plisio balances.

facts.label: Direct-wallet / non-custodial claim
facts.value: An official 2026 Plisio article says customer payments go directly to the merchant wallet and are never held by Plisio.

facts.label: Crypto settlement
facts.value: The documented account flow supports retaining balances in supported crypto and withdrawing to an external crypto address.

facts.label: Stablecoin settlement
facts.value: Supported stablecoin balances can be used only on their listed chains; API supports withdrawal in the selected supported asset.

facts.label: Fiat settlement and payout
facts.value: Fiat-valued invoices are supported, but public merchant docs do not describe conversion to bank fiat or a fiat payout currency.

facts.label: Invoice expiry
facts.value: API lets the seller set invoice expiry in minutes using expire_min.

facts.label: Payment status and callbacks
facts.value: Invoice callback statuses let a merchant distinguish new, pending, completed, and failed payment states.

facts.label: Underpayment and overpayment
facts.value: Underpayment can be manually completed after the wait period if it is at least 95% of the invoice; lower payments remain underpaid. Overpayments can show a completed status with the paid percentage.

facts.label: Refund handling
facts.value: Crypto transfers are irreversible; seller-initiated return is a new crypto withdrawal and can incur service and network fees.

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: Plisio is a hosted service; seller uses its account and API rather than installing Plisio server software.

facts.label: Server requirements and maintenance
facts.value: No Plisio server hardware, self-hosted deployment, or server-maintenance requirements are published for merchants.

facts.label: Cost of running software
facts.value: No self-hosting or software licence fee is published; gateway fees and blockchain network fees still apply.

facts.label: Transaction data access
facts.value: Merchant can query transaction and balance data through the API; dashboard pricing page advertises transaction history and filters.

facts.label: Export and migration
facts.value: A public export format for customer/payment records or a documented migration route to another processor was not found.

facts.label: Account closure
facts.value: Terms say a user may close an account and stop using the service; remaining crypto in a suspended or closed account may be withdrawn unless prohibited by law or court order.

facts.label: Inactive account handling
facts.value: Terms define inactivity as over 180 days and allow Plisio to move funds to cold storage; support can assist when the user returns.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: Plisio is a hosted cryptocurrency payment gateway with invoices, an API, wallet balances, and mass payouts.

facts.label: Service status
facts.value: Pricing, FAQ, integrations, and developer documentation were available during this check.

facts.label: Legal name in current site footer

facts.value: An official Plisio article identifies “UK PLISIO LTD #12374919”; Companies House lists PLISIO LTD (12374919) as dissolved on 2021-06-29. Its connection to the current Plisio, Inc. is not established.

facts.label: Acquisition, rebrand, or parent

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Pricing page advertises 24/7 technical support and API connection help; terms give support@plisio.net for withdrawal help on a suspended account.

facts.label: Support service levels
facts.value: Public support response targets, language coverage, and plan-specific support limits were not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Current operation
facts.value: The official product, fee page, docs, FAQ, and integrations page were live on 2026-11-07.

facts.label: Shutdown, acquisition, or service sunset
facts.value: No shutdown, acquisition, or service-sunset notice was found in the official blog or product pages searched.

facts.label: Product changes
facts.value: Blog and product pages show continuing content and product documentation; no dated merchant-service sunset or migration notice was located.

facts.label: Current contracting entity and country
facts.value: Current footer identifies “Plisio, Inc.” but the linked terms do not name the contracting entity or give its incorporation country.

facts.label: Licence / regulator record
facts.value: No current licence claim was found on Plisio's product, legal, pricing, or security pages. The FCA Register and FinCEN MSB search tools were opened, but their interactive query fields could not be queried through the web reader; exact-name web searches yielded no clear result.

facts.label: Enforcement notices
facts.value: Exact-name web searches of regulator domains found no Plisio-specific enforcement notice; no direct regulator record was identified for the current operator.

apps.news: The current regional price pages were checked for current card rates; no separate official Shopify newsroom/changelog notice of a general Shopify Payments fee increase or decrease was found in the pages searched.

facts.label: Other required accounts
facts.value: A Shopify store and paid Shopify subscription are required for live Shopify Payments; no separate processor account is normally set up by the merchant.

facts.label: Third-party provider dependency
facts.value: If Shopify Payments is unavailable or replaced, the seller needs an eligible third-party gateway and pays that gateway separately; Shopify may also charge its own third-party transaction fee.

facts.label: Shopify plan required
facts.value: US region page showed Basic, Grow and Advanced at USD 29/79/299 per month billed yearly, or USD 39/105/399 per month billed monthly; Plus starts at USD 2,300/mo on a 3-year term or USD 2,500/mo on a 1-year term.

facts.label: Subscription trial/promotion
facts.value: US pricing page advertised a 3-day free trial followed by USD 1/month for 3 months; standard subscription price applies after promotion.

facts.label: Shopify Payments fixed monthly/setup costs
facts.value: No separate Shopify Payments monthly, setup, or hidden fee is listed beyond the Shopify plan subscription and transaction fees.

facts.label: International card pricing, US example
facts.value: US page lists an additional 1% for online international cards across Basic/Grow/Advanced/Plus; exact issuer/currency treatment is account-dependent.

facts.label: Other regional international-card rates
facts.value: Australia, Canada, UK, NZ and Singapore pages show market-specific “online international” rates; the stated amount can be a complete rate, not an add-on.

facts.label: Cross-border fee base
facts.value: Cross-border card processing rates depend on issuing country/region and card type; Shopify shows domestic and “rest of world” rates in Admin.

facts.label: Currency conversion fee
facts.value: When charge/presentment currency differs from payout currency, Shopify's fee is 1.5% for US seller accounts and 2% for France and all other Shopify Payments regions.

facts.label: PayPal Wallet conversion
facts.value: For US and France Shopify Payments accounts using PayPal Wallet, the listed conversion fee is 3%; it is not available for other Shopify Payments regions per this table.

facts.label: Refund/chargeback conversion treatment
facts.value: Conversion fee is charged at capture, not again when refunding or receiving a chargeback; the original conversion and card fees are not returned on a refund.

facts.label: Multi-currency payout fee
facts.value: Shopify says multi-currency payout fees depend on plan and account location; a single public rate table covering all supported countries was not found in the pages checked.

facts.label: Local-method fees
facts.value: Local payment method fees vary by seller region, method, plan and displayed price schedule; no universal local-method fee applies.

facts.label: USDC checkout fee
facts.value: US pricing lists USDC at 2.9% + USD 0.30 Basic, 2.7% + USD 0.30 Grow, 2.5% + USD 0.30 Advanced, and 2.25% + USD 0.30 Plus.

facts.label: Bank method and wallet price examples
facts.value: The localized pricing pages separately price wallets and local methods (for example UK Klarna 4.99% + GBP 0.30 on Basic/Grow/Advanced, and 3.79% + GBP 0.30 on Plus).

facts.label: Other local-method prices
facts.value: No single public list of every local-method rate for every seller-country/buyer-country combination was found.

facts.label: Subscription/billing surcharge
facts.value: Shopify Payments has no separate universal recurring-billing fee published; processing follows the rate for the selected payment method and plan, and subscription apps can have separate fees.

facts.label: Fraud analysis
facts.value: Built-in fraud analysis is included with Shopify plan features and requires Shopify Payments; more advanced fraud/risk products may be separately priced.

facts.label: Tax add-ons
facts.value: Shopify Tax features and advanced tax platform are separate from payment processing; tax calculation/collection features have market and plan conditions.

facts.label: Other checkout add-on price
facts.value: No universal separate Shopify Payments setup or fraud add-on charge was published in the reviewed fee page; optional third-party apps may charge independently.

facts.label: Refund fee and retained processing fee
facts.value: No new transaction fee is charged for issuing a Shopify Payments refund, but the original card processing fee is not returned to the seller.

facts.label: Refund timing and limits
facts.value: Refund may remain pending up to 2 business days, then can take up to 10 business days to reach the buyer; usual maximum refund window is 120 days, subject to method/bank.

facts.label: Currency-conversion refund result
facts.value: Refund uses the current exchange rate if conversion is necessary; Shopify does not return the original conversion fee or card fee.

facts.label: Dispute responsibility
facts.value: The issuing bank decides card chargeback outcomes; the disputed amount and fee are taken from seller funds. Shopify supplies response tools but disclaims liability for the outcome.

facts.label: Chargeback fee: USD/CAD/AUD/NZD/GBP markets
facts.value: Published chargeback fees: US USD 15; Canada CAD 15 or USD 15; Australia AUD 25; New Zealand NZD 20; UK GBP 10.

facts.label: Chargeback fee: euro markets
facts.value: Most listed euro-area countries charge EUR 15; Ireland charges EUR 15 plus 23% VAT.

facts.label: Chargeback fee: other listed markets
facts.value: Hong Kong HKD 85; Japan JPY 1,300; Mexico MXN 200; Singapore SGD 16.35; UAE AED 60 + 5% VAT; Switzerland CHF 15 or EUR 15; Norway NOK 200 or EUR 15; Sweden SEK 150 or EUR 15; Poland PLN 75 or EUR 15; Czechia CZK 400 or EUR 15; Denmark DKK 115 or EUR 15; Hungary HUF 7,000 or EUR 15; Gibraltar GBP 15; Liechtenstein CHF 15 or EUR 15.

facts.label: Dispute fee returned on win
facts.value: The chargeback fee is returned if the chargeback is resolved in the seller's favor; network dispute-resolution programs can resolve some cases automatically.

facts.label: Inquiry and response
facts.value: A chargeback removes the disputed amount and fee; an inquiry does not initially remove either. Merchant submits evidence by the displayed deadline in Admin.

facts.label: Payout fees
facts.value: Shopify states Shopify Payments charges card-processing fees but not an additional Shopify transaction fee when it is the sole provider; a separate payout fee schedule was not found for ordinary domestic bank payouts.

facts.label: Minimum payout examples
facts.value: No minimum payout for US, Canada and Australia; EUR markets commonly have EUR 1, UK GBP 1, Switzerland CHF 5 or EUR 1, and UAE AED 20.

facts.label: Other payout minimums
facts.value: Minimum payout thresholds for other currencies are shown by country in the payout-timing table; no one global minimum applies.

facts.label: Card/payment limits
facts.value: No single public per-payment minimum/maximum applies across card brands and all Shopify Payments countries; limits can depend on method, currency, processor and account.

facts.label: Local-method limits
facts.value: Local methods may impose their own currency, amount, buyer-location, eligibility or onboarding rules.

facts.label: Seller signup countries
facts.value: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, China (mainland), Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Hong Kong SAR, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States.

facts.label: Country not listed
facts.value: Businesses based outside the Help Center's supported-country list need a third-party payment provider for card acceptance.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Terms allow a person operating as a sole proprietor or a corporation/other legal entity, subject to the designated-country rules.

facts.label: Age requirement
facts.value: The account representative must generally be at least 18; a parent or guardian must represent an under-18 applicant.

facts.label: Local entity/residency
facts.value: Seller must identify the country where the business operates and be its legal resident or have a duly established and, where required, registered/licensed business there.

facts.label: Local bank requirement
facts.value: Payout account type and bank location depend on seller country and payout currency; each country guide sets the accepted bank corridor.

facts.label: Business verification
facts.value: Shopify/processor can request identity, address, registration or tax IDs, beneficial-owner details, business invoices, reseller authorization, business licence and financial statements.

facts.label: Store information
facts.value: Applicant must provide a business/site URL, trading name and billing descriptor; country setup pages may require identity and business documents.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Open setup from Shopify Admin for an eligible store; Shopify and processors review submitted details before confirming eligibility.

facts.label: Minimum business size or processing volume
facts.value: No general minimum revenue, transaction volume, or business tenure is published for standard Shopify Payments signup.

facts.label: Supported product types
facts.value: Lawful goods and services may be sold if the business type is supported by the country terms and is not prohibited.

facts.label: Digital products and subscriptions
facts.value: Shopify Payments can process eligible digital-goods and subscription orders when the store uses a compatible subscription app and supported payment method.

facts.label: Important business restrictions
facts.value: Prohibited categories include regulated/illegal goods, financial services and money transfer, virtual currency/crypto services, adult content, weapons, tobacco, and prescription drugs/medical devices. Country terms can add restrictions.

facts.label: Risk/compliance review
facts.value: High refund/dispute activity, delayed fulfillment, sudden volume increases, compliance concerns, or missing requested records can trigger review, restrictions, reserve, or payout hold.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions
facts.value: No single public global list of countries where every Shopify Payments buyer can pay was found; card networks and each local method have their own country and currency coverage.

facts.label: Local-method buyer eligibility
facts.value: A local method appears only for eligible customer locations and currencies; market configuration, seller entity and payment method can further limit availability.

facts.label: Reserve/hold policy
facts.value: Shopify or processors may hold payouts during verification, compliance, fraud, complaint, dispute, fulfillment or account-risk reviews; a reserve can be fixed or percentage-based.

facts.label: Reserve release
facts.value: Reserve end date and risk review determine whether funds are released, extended, reduced or increased; processing to payout can take several business days after release.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: No general approval-time estimate was found for Shopify Payments.

facts.label: Provider type and legal seller
facts.value: Integrated gateway/payment service, not merchant of record. The seller sells to the customer and remains responsible for the transaction and sale.

facts.label: Processing partners
facts.value: One or more payment processors and financial service providers perform processing/settlement; the applicable processor depends on seller country and can change.

facts.label: Charge currencies
facts.value: Shopify Payments supports local-currency checkout for eligible methods and Markets; Shopify advertises selling in 130+ currencies. Actual processing currencies vary by country and method.

facts.label: Non-Shopify gateway currency handling
facts.value: With a different gateway, local prices can display, but checkout converts to the store's default currency unless the gateway is Adyen with compatible setup.

facts.label: Card brands
facts.value: Card checkout supports major networks including Visa and Mastercard; country pages add market-specific brands such as Amex, Discover, Diners Club, JCB, UnionPay, Maestro, or local debit.

facts.label: Accelerated checkout
facts.value: Shop Pay, Apple Pay and Google Pay are available in eligible markets/devices; local method and market rules apply.

facts.label: Local payment methods
facts.value: Methods include Bancontact, iDEAL \

facts.label: Expanded local methods
facts.value: The 2026-05-30 rollout lists MobilePay, TWINT, BLIK and Przelewy24 in additional seller countries.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Standard one-time card and supported wallet/local-method checkout is supported.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Shopify Payments works with Shopify Subscriptions and compatible checkout-integrated subscription apps.

facts.label: Recurring method limits
facts.value: Recurring charges require a supported card/wallet and gateway setup; local, manual and many non-card methods may be unavailable for automatic renewal. USDC cannot be used for subscription products.

facts.label: Billing features
facts.value: Shopify Payments does not itself provide subscription plan management, usage billing, proration, dunning rules, or customer subscription portal; those require Shopify Subscriptions or another app.

facts.label: Failed-payment recovery
facts.value: A subscription app/gateway setup handles recurring payment failure; Shopify's new payment recovery with a third-party gateway applies to eligible one-time card transactions, not recurring subscription charges.

facts.label: Checkout options
facts.value: Hosted Shopify Checkout is included with the Shopify store; accelerated checkout and Shop Pay can be enabled where supported.

facts.label: Payment links and embedded sales
facts.value: Shopify's Quick Sale can send a payment link; Buy Buttons can embed products and send buyers to Shopify Checkout.

facts.label: Integration/API
facts.value: Shopify Admin API and payment app integrations can manage payment settings and orders; processor integrations are installed/configured through Shopify.

facts.label: Webhooks/events
facts.value: Shopify webhooks can notify an app about order and transaction changes; delivery and retries follow Shopify webhook rules.

facts.label: Test mode
facts.value: Shopify Payments test mode simulates payments; test gateway orders require a paid Shopify plan and are not paid out.

facts.label: Sales-tax responsibility
facts.value: Shopify Payments is not merchant of record; seller remains responsible for sales-tax registration, collection, filing and remittance, even when Shopify tax tools calculate amounts.

facts.label: Tax feature coverage
facts.value: Shopify Tax can calculate tax and provide tax features in supported regions; Advanced Tax is an add-on and tax filing/remittance coverage depends on product and location.

facts.label: Tax on processing fees
facts.value: Shopify says taxes are added to processing fees for Switzerland, EU, Australia and Singapore; UK/EU reverse-charge details depend on seller registration and location.

facts.label: Receipts
facts.value: Shopify can send order confirmation and payment-related emails; stores can customize notifications and checkout communications.

facts.label: Business invoices/tax IDs
facts.value: Shopify supports order invoices/packing slips through platform features/apps, but a universal tax invoice generated by Shopify Payments is not promised for all seller jurisdictions.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: Standard payouts go to a verified seller bank account; eligible sellers may use Shopify Balance or receive supported multi-currency bank payouts.

facts.label: Payout-method constraints
facts.value: US, Europe, UK, Australia, Canada, Hong Kong, Singapore and UAE have distinct bank-location and currency requirements; account guides specify exact bank acceptance.

facts.label: Domestic payout currencies
facts.value: Payouts are usually in the seller market's domestic currency (for example USD, CAD, GBP, AUD, EUR, SGD, HKD, JPY, NZD, MXN or AED), subject to country terms.

facts.label: Multi-currency payouts
facts.value: Eligible stores can add non-domestic payout currencies; availability depends on plan, seller location, currency and a matching bank account.

facts.label: Settlement vs bank arrival
facts.value: Capture-to-available settlement varies by country and risk; after payout is sent, the bank can take another 1–3 business days. Daily/weekly/monthly payout schedule is selectable in most regions.

facts.label: Standard payout timing examples
facts.value: Minimum settlement is 2 business days Australia; 3 days for US, Canada, UK, Ireland and most listed European markets; 5 days UAE.

facts.label: Higher-risk payout timing
facts.value: Higher-risk accounts may receive custom schedules of 5–20 business days; new accounts can initially take longer than regional minimum.

facts.label: Product delivery/access
facts.value: Shopify Payments processes checkout but does not itself deliver digital files, software licences or membership access; seller uses Shopify fulfillment tools or an app/integration.

facts.label: Digital delivery add-ons
facts.value: Shopify's free Digital Products app can deliver files or access links after payment; third-party apps have separate terms and fees.

facts.label: Multi-seller/split payment
facts.value: No public Shopify Payments split-payout/submerchant feature or general marketplace settlement terms were found.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Shopify Payments accepts USDC on Base, Ethereum L1, Optimism, Polygon and Arbitrum in eligible regions.

facts.label: Crypto seller/buyer eligibility
facts.value: Eligible US, Mexico, listed European markets and Hong Kong stores can offer USDC, subject to representative residential-address and business-category checks; some US states are excluded.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Sellers can choose local-currency payout or claim USDC to a connected wallet; while unclaimed, USDC is reflected in the Shopify Payments balance. Public docs do not fully identify custody/control arrangements for the interim balance.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout options
facts.value: Default USDC checkout settlement can be in local fiat through normal Shopify Payments payouts without an FX/multicurrency fee; eligible merchants can manually claim USDC to a compatible wallet.

facts.label: Crypto settlement timing
facts.value: Fiat proceeds follow the store's normal Shopify Payments schedule; USDC in the crypto balance must be manually claimed by the merchant.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion/refunds
facts.value: USDC orders cannot be disputed by the customer through card chargeback; no partial capture, no subscription purchase, and cashback can cap the refundable amount.

facts.label: Crypto network fees
facts.value: Shopify says USDC checkout customers do not pay gas fees; it does not charge a separate Shopify conversion fee for local-currency payout under the announced offer.

facts.label: Crypto hosting
facts.value: Not applicable: Shopify Payments is a hosted commerce/payment service; sellers do not run a Shopify Payments node or wallet server.

facts.label: Transaction exports
facts.value: Shopify allows order and transaction history export as CSV, including captured payment transaction fields such as gateway, type, amount, currency and status.

facts.label: Payment-data portability
facts.value: No public promise was found that saved card credentials/tokens can be moved to another processor for every Shopify Payments account.

facts.label: Closing payment access
facts.value: Shopify Payments can be suspended or terminated under its terms; termination does not cancel Shopify store terms automatically.

facts.label: Remaining funds after closure
facts.value: Funds can remain held for refunds, chargebacks, fees, investigations or other obligations and are paid subject to processor terms.

facts.label: Shopify plan cancellation
facts.value: Shopify plan must be paused/deactivated separately; standard plan billing and cancellation terms are separate from Shopify Payments closure.

facts.label: Current name, product, owner and old names
facts.value: Shopify Payments; Shopify's integrated payments service for Shopify stores. No separate old product name identified.

facts.label: Current status and recent availability changes
facts.value: Active. Changelog says launched in 15 additional European seller countries on 2025-03-21.

facts.label: Feature retirement
facts.value: Meta Pay was removed as a Shopify Payments accelerated-checkout option on 2025-02-10; historical transactions remain reportable.

facts.label: Newsroom/product update
facts.value: Shopify announced USDC on Shopify Payments on 2025-06-12, initially in early access; Fall '26 merchant edition announced seven additional local methods on 2026-10-28.

facts.label: Support access
facts.value: Basic/Grow list 24/7 live chat; Advanced lists enhanced live chat; Plus lists priority support and priority 24/7 phone support in the plan comparison.

facts.label: Support channels
facts.value: Shopify Help Center offers support access through the store account; Shopify Payments payout holds are handled through Admin alerts/email and support.

facts.label: Operating status
facts.value: Shopify Payments is active in the supported seller countries listed by Shopify; no current shutdown notice found.

facts.label: Recent method changes
facts.value: Seven local methods announced in Shopify's Fall '26 merchant edition on 2026-10-28; country availability depends on the method and eligible store.

facts.label: Contracting entity
facts.value: Payments terms name Shopify Inc. for Canada; Shopify Payments (USA) Inc. for the US; Shopify International Limited for Europe/UK and listed markets; Shopify Commerce Singapore Pte. Ltd. for Australia, China mainland, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand and Singapore.

facts.label: Underlying processor/regulatory role
facts.value: Processor and financial-institution entities vary by designated country; Shopify's processor list identifies the applicable providers and their terms.

facts.label: Security scope
facts.value: Shopify states Level 1 PCI DSS compliance for Shopify; Shopify stores are PCI compliant by default.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Prohibited examples include adult content/services, including qualifying AI-generated adult content; gambling/prize competitions; unauthorized copyrighted goods; deceptive get-rich-quick sales; illegal drugs; crypto mining/staking and secondary NFT sales.

facts.label: Important restrictions
facts.value: Third-party content platforms, crowdfunding/fundraising and other restricted industries need additional review; approval can be modified or revoked.

facts.label: Buyer-country restrictions

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy
facts.value: Stripe can create a reserve, notify its terms, change it when risk or a financial provider requires, fund it from balances/bank debits and apply it against liabilities.

facts.label: Reserve and hold policy

facts.value: Tap says it currently accepts no new merchants from Egypt, Jordan, or Lebanon. Egypt received a payment-facilitator/service-provider license announcement in 2025, so licensing does not establish that new sellers can currently onboard there.

facts.label: Seller legal forms
facts.value: Tap describes individual accounts for unlicensed businesses and corporate accounts for licensed businesses. The individual account is described as a home-based account with a personal bank account and no business license.

facts.label: Qatar home businesses
facts.value: Qatar home-business sellers need a commercial permit; the permit route described by Tap requires the business owner to be Qatari and the bank account name to match the registration.

facts.label: Bank account requirement
facts.value: An active bank account is required for payouts: individual accounts use the individual’s name and corporate accounts the business name. Business IBAN evidence must show account name, number, bank address, and IBAN; its English name must match the legal business name.

facts.label: Bank country and supported payout reach
facts.value: Payouts are limited to businesses in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE, Oman, and Qatar; Tap says it cannot pay businesses outside those markets.

facts.label: Business identity documents
facts.value: Tap asks for a business license or commercial registration, authorized signatory and owners/shareholders, with possible MOA, VAT certificate, or address proof. It requests ID for signatories and owners at a 20%–25%+ threshold (foreign owners: passport). A live website or social page must show products/services, prices, About, terms, refunds, privacy, and checkout.

facts.label: Extra review and regulated businesses
facts.value: Corporate ownership chains, marketplaces, or regulated activities may trigger more KYC; regulated businesses must provide their activity license and, for financial products, CFT/AML policies.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: goSell has an online registration route; goCollect can be downloaded and opened as an account. Activation requires document submission and a contract signed in Arabic or English.

facts.label: Minimum business size or sales
facts.value: No public revenue, transaction-volume, or employee minimum was found. The agreement permits termination for inactivity or activity below a minimum set between Tap and merchant.

facts.label: Digital products and software
facts.value: The public material reviewed does not explicitly approve SaaS, software licenses, ebooks, downloads, or courses, and does not give a complete allow/deny list for service or physical-product categories.

facts.label: Marketplace sellers
facts.value: Marketplace operators may use Tap's marketplace product; retailer onboarding and payout access require Tap's KYC/business verification where applicable.

facts.label: High-risk business categories
facts.value: Tap specifically names game coins, hacks, and sharpshooters, iTunes cards, Bitcoin sales by individuals, and unlicensed mobile-wallet apps as unsupported examples.

facts.label: Legal and activity restrictions
facts.value: Sellers must hold licenses required for their activity and country; Tap may reject unlawful or Tap-inappropriate activity. Marketplaces may receive enhanced KYC, and regulated sellers need the regulator license and, for financial products, CFT/AML policies. No full prohibited-use schedule for adult content, gambling, crowdfunding, or every digital-product category was found.

facts.label: Buyer countries
facts.value: Tap says merchants in supported countries can accept payments from around the world, subject to enabled methods and network rules. A complete buyer-country exclusion or sanctions list was not found.

facts.label: Holds and payout withholding
facts.value: Payouts may be held while an account is unapproved, documents are expired, bank details are wrong, or a transaction is disputed or under review.

facts.label: Reserve and post-termination hold
facts.value: Agreements allow reserves/collateral and withholding; UAE terms say an agreed balance may be retained up to 2 years after termination for later chargebacks/credits.

facts.label: Approval-time estimate
facts.value: Tap says it usually activates accounts within 3 business days after required documents and setup are complete.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Payment gateway and payment service provider for online acceptance; it also offers billing links, merchant payouts, and marketplace payment tools.

facts.label: Legal seller and delivery responsibility
facts.value: The merchant sells its own goods or services and remains responsible for fulfilment, customer terms, and disputes about delivery.

facts.label: Named charge currencies
facts.value: The currencies help page names AED, BHD, EUR, GBP, KWD, OMR, QAR, SAR, and USD; multi-currency must be requested for goSell/goCollect.

facts.label: Payment-method currency limits
facts.value: Some local methods are currency-specific: mada uses SAR, KNET KWD, OmanNet OMR, and Tabby has its own SAR/AED/KD minimums.

facts.label: International card schemes
facts.value: Visa, Mastercard, and American Express are listed as supported card methods, with acceptance dependent on market and account enablement.

facts.label: Saudi local method
facts.value: mada is available to Saudi sellers and supports SAR only.

facts.label: Kuwait local method
facts.value: KNET is available only to merchants based in Kuwait and accepts KWD only.

facts.label: Bahrain local method
facts.value: Benefit is identified as Bahrain's local debit scheme; Tap says regional merchants can request it without a Bahrain license or bank account.

facts.label: Oman local method
facts.value: OmanNet debit cards can be accepted through Tap SDKs or its hosted page and require OMR.

facts.label: Qatar local method
facts.value: NAPS appears in Tap's goCollect supported-method description for the region; the reviewed sources do not provide a complete NAPS seller/currency matrix.

facts.label: UAE local method
facts.value: Jaywan online acceptance was announced for UAE Tap merchants and is automatically enabled for eligible merchants under existing domestic card pricing.

facts.label: Installments
facts.value: Tabby is listed for KSA and UAE. Tap's Tabby help says it is for corporate merchants using goSell websites/apps, not goCollect links.

facts.label: Digital wallets
facts.value: Tap lists Apple Pay and STC Pay in its regional method overview; Apple Pay market support depends on seller country, currency, and channel.

facts.label: Google Pay, PayPal, and Careem Pay
facts.value: Tap's accepted-method page lists Google Pay and PayPal in UAE/Kuwait, and Careem Pay in UAE. Google Pay developer docs list UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain, with USD as an addition.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: One-time card and local-method charges are supported through goSell, hosted checkout, SDKs, and the Charges API.

facts.label: Recurring card payments
facts.value: Card subscriptions support daily, weekly, monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, semiannual, or annual billing. Activation is requested from Tap; API webhooks can report recurring charge events.

facts.label: Recurring method limits
facts.value: Tap's docs require its saved-card feature and use customer, card, and payment-agreement IDs. STC Pay does not support recurring payments.

facts.label: Recurring payment fees
facts.value: No separate subscription surcharge is stated in the reviewed recurring-payment help or API pages.

facts.label: Plan changes
facts.value: Changing an existing subscription amount requires canceling it and creating a new subscription; Tap says the saved card need not be re-entered.

facts.label: Trials, seats, metering, discounts, proration, and dunning
facts.value: No public feature matrix for trials, seats, usage billing, discounts, proration, or retry/dunning rules was found in the subscription and invoice docs checked.

facts.label: Hosted checkout
facts.value: Tap provides hosted web checkout and embedded web/mobile checkout SDKs; the developer overview lists Flutter, iOS, Android, and React Native. Eligible methods depend on merchant enablement.

facts.label: Payment links and invoices
facts.value: goCollect sends bills/payment links by email, SMS, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and other social channels; dashboard and invoice APIs are available.

facts.label: Custom domain and hosted checkout branding limits
facts.value: No public plan-specific custom-domain or hosted-checkout branding limit was found in the docs and pricing pages checked.

facts.label: API and developer docs
facts.value: Public APIs cover charges, authorizations, customers, invoices, refunds, and payment methods.

facts.label: SDKs and store plugins
facts.value: Tap lists web/mobile SDKs and official plugins including WooCommerce, Magento, and OpenCart; Shopify has native and redirect integrations.

facts.label: Sandbox keys and webhooks
facts.value: Tap provides separate test and live keys for sandbox transactions. Server-to-server webhooks report asynchronous charge, invoice, and subscription events to a seller-supplied endpoint.

facts.label: Checkout and integrations
facts.value: Hosted checkout reduces integration work; direct card-data handling requires the seller to meet PCI DSS requirements and provide a valid PCI certificate/AOC.

facts.label: Sales tax collection and remittance
facts.value: Tap acts as a gateway; the seller's agreement leaves product/service obligations and applicable taxes with the merchant. No merchant-of-record tax remittance promise was found.

facts.label: Seller registration and filings
facts.value: Seller must maintain the licenses/authorizations needed for its activity and pay applicable taxes in its registered market.

facts.label: Tax coverage by jurisdiction
facts.value: No public jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction tax filing or remittance coverage list was found.

facts.label: Payment confirmations and receipts
facts.value: Dashboard tracks transactions and reports receipt numbers; charge/invoice objects also include receipt fields, although the current Charges API says the receipt parameter is no longer supported.

facts.label: Seller invoices and bills
facts.value: goCollect and the Invoices API let sellers create, send, track, remind, and cancel customer bills/invoices.

facts.label: Buyer business tax IDs and exemption handling
facts.value: No public workflow for buyer VAT IDs, tax-exempt purchases, or tax-invoice compliance by country was found.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Tap pays to bank accounts in the six operating GCC markets. Kuwait also offers manual USD settlement on request.

facts.label: Payout currencies
facts.value: Local payout currencies are SAR, KWD, BHD, AED, OMR, and QAR; Kuwait also has manual USD settlement, and UAE terms describe AED and USD wallet settlement.

facts.label: Foreign-currency payout conversion
facts.value: If transaction currency differs from designated payout currency, Tap applies an FX rate; UAE terms give a 2% to 5% currency-pair premium.

facts.label: Saudi settlement timing
facts.value: Mada transactions settle in 3 working days; Visa/Mastercard in 5 working days.

facts.label: Kuwait settlement timing
facts.value: KNET settles within 2 business days; Visa, Mastercard, and Amex settle within 5 business days.

facts.label: Bahrain settlement timing
facts.value: Benefit settles in 3 working days; Visa/Mastercard/Amex settle in 5 working days.

facts.label: UAE settlement timing
facts.value: Funds settle after 5 business days, then are paid weekly on Tuesday; corporate bank transactions are available Friday.

facts.label: Oman settlement timing
facts.value: Transactions settle within 5 business days; payouts are sent twice weekly, Monday and Wednesday.

facts.label: Qatar settlement timing
facts.value: Qatar transactions settle in 5 business days; merchant can ask for a less-frequent schedule.

facts.label: Pending balance availability
facts.value: Tap says transactions generally move from pending to available balance within 3 to 5 business days, depending on payment method.

facts.label: Product delivery and access
facts.value: Tap processes payments and sends invoices/payment links; seller remains responsible for delivering goods/services. No digital-file hosting, software-license delivery, or membership-access feature was found.

facts.label: Marketplace support
facts.value: Tap offers marketplace onboarding, retailer KYC, split allocation, commission retention, and retailer payouts through APIs/product tools.

facts.label: Marketplace approval and fees
facts.value: Marketplace operators may face enhanced due diligence; public marketplace pricing or split-payment surcharge is not stated.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable. Tap is researched here as a fiat payment gateway; its published business-types page lists individual Bitcoin sales as unsupported.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable. No crypto product or custody offer was found.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout
facts.value: Not applicable. No crypto conversion or crypto payout offer was found.

facts.label: Crypto payment completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable. No crypto payment or crypto refund product was found.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable. Tap is a hosted payment service, but it does not publish a crypto checkout software product.

facts.label: Exports
facts.value: Tap dashboard supports transaction statements and exports in Excel or PDF.

facts.label: Customer/payment-data portability
facts.value: No public migration process for saved cards, payment tokens, subscription agreements, or importing customer data to another provider was found.

facts.label: Merchant termination
facts.value: Agreement lasts one year and auto-renews; either party may terminate with 30 days' written notice. Merchant may withdraw before contract conclusion within at least 10 working days and receive advance fees back if not tied to delivered service.

facts.label: Immediate termination and remaining funds
facts.value: Tap may terminate immediately for listed breach, nonpayment, insolvency, fraud/unlawful activity, inactivity, regulatory order, or missing information. Fees/disputes remain due and payouts may be withheld for risk.

facts.label: Account closure steps and personal-data retention
facts.value: No separate public account-closure workflow or universal deadline to release remaining funds was found. Tap's privacy notice says personal data is kept as long as required for service and legal/regulatory/accounting needs.
