facts.value: For Wix Payments multi-currency purchases: US 1%; EU 2%; UK 2%; Canada 2%; Switzerland 2%.

facts.label: Exchange rate and payout currency
facts.value: Wix uses XE rates at payment time and converts Wix Payments funds to the site's main currency; the seller's payout is in that currency.

facts.label: US PayPal/Venmo
facts.value: US PayPal wallet and Venmo: 3.49% + USD 0.49 per payment.

facts.label: US Pay Later and BNPL
facts.value: US PayPal Pay Later: 4.99% + USD 0.49; Afterpay, Affirm, and Klarna: 6% + USD 0.30 each.

facts.label: EU iDEAL
facts.value: iDEAL: 2.5% + EUR 0.30.

facts.label: EU Bancontact
facts.value: Bancontact: 1.4% + EUR 0.30.

facts.label: EU Klarna group A
facts.value: Austria, Belgium, Finland, Germany, and Netherlands: 2.99% + EUR 0.35.

facts.label: EU Klarna group B
facts.value: Italy, Portugal, and Spain: 4.99% + EUR 0.35.

facts.label: UK Clearpay and Klarna
facts.value: Clearpay: 6% + GBP 0.30; Klarna: 4.99% + GBP 0.35.

facts.label: Switzerland local methods
facts.value: TWINT: 1.9% + CHF 0.30; iDEAL: 2.5% + CHF 0.40; Klarna: 2.99% + CHF 0.35.

facts.label: Brazil Pix and boleto
facts.value: Pix: 0.95% per completed payment; boleto: BRL 2.99 per paid boleto.

facts.label: Canada Interac POS
facts.value: Canada Interac: CAD 0.15 per transaction on Wix Payments POS; no percentage is shown in the schedule.

facts.label: Recurring-payment surcharge
facts.value: No separate Wix Payments recurring-payment surcharge was listed; the public fee schedule lists method/country rates, not a billing surcharge.

facts.label: Tax calculation and filing add-on
facts.value: A Wix Payments tax-service fee was not found. Wix's terms say the seller determines, collects, reports, and remits sales taxes.

facts.label: Other checkout add-ons
facts.value: No general fraud-screening or payment-related add-on fee schedule was found in the Wix Payments fee and terms pages checked.

facts.label: Refund fee and retained fee
facts.value: No additional refund fee is listed for standard Wix Payments cards; the original processing fee is not returned.

facts.label: Refund timing and minimum
facts.value: Refunds can take 3–5 business days to reach a buyer; the typical minimum is 1 unit of local currency, with PayPal US at USD 0.50.

facts.label: Dispute responsibility
facts.value: The seller bears the chargeback amount and customer-sale responsibility; Wix/processor provide the dispute workflow and may contest certain disputes.

facts.label: Chargeback fee
facts.value: USD 15 (US), CAD 15 (Canada), EUR 15 (EU), GBP 15 (UK), and CHF 15 (Switzerland); Wix Payments Brazil currently has no chargeback fee.

facts.label: Fee and funds returned on a win
facts.value: If the seller wins a dispute, the disputed amount and chargeback fee are returned to the Wix Payments balance.

facts.label: Payout fees
facts.value: A general Wix Payments payout-transfer fee schedule was not found in the payout, Brazil transfer, fee, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Minimum available balance
facts.value: General payout help says a payout is made only when available balance reaches at least “$1”; the page does not explain the localized threshold for every payout currency.

facts.label: Brazil payout minimum
facts.value: No distinct Brazil payout minimum was stated in the Brazilian account, transfer, and fee pages checked.

facts.label: Minimum transaction
facts.value: Minimum charge amounts: USD 1 (US), BRL 1 (Brazil), CAD 1 (Canada), EUR 1 (Europe), GBP 1 (UK), CHF 1 (Switzerland).

facts.label: Maximum transaction/account limits
facts.value: A universal public maximum charge or rolling collection limit was not found; terms allow Wix/processors to set limits based on risk and volume.

facts.label: Seller countries and account currencies
facts.value: Austria (EUR), Belgium (EUR), Brazil (BRL), Canada (CAD), Finland (EUR), Germany (EUR), Ireland (EUR), Italy (EUR), Lithuania (EUR), Netherlands (EUR), Portugal (EUR), Spain (EUR), Switzerland (CHF), United Kingdom (GBP), United States (USD).

facts.label: Country and territory exclusions
facts.value: Some associated overseas territories, autonomous regions, dependencies, and military addresses are excluded; examples include Åland Islands and the Isle of Man.

facts.label: Sole sellers and individuals
facts.value: Individual, sole proprietorship, or sole-trader account types are accepted where offered for the seller's country.

facts.label: Companies and organizations
facts.value: Company, partnership, and some organization or nonprofit types are supported when that type is available locally and required registration details are supplied.

facts.label: Business and bank country match
facts.value: Individual account setup must be in the same country as the bank. A business's registration country, bank country, and account setup country must generally match.

facts.label: Bank-account ownership
facts.value: The payout bank account must be active and owned by the account holder or business; the name must match the Wix Payments account.

facts.label: Identity and business review
facts.value: Wix reviews the seller identity, account details, bank information, and website content before full activation and payouts.

facts.label: Common verification documents
facts.value: Possible requests include government photo ID, bank statement, address evidence, registration or tax IDs, business information, ownership and control details, and product/service description.

facts.label: Website readiness
facts.value: The site should be published and show the business name, contact details, product/service description, and other required consumer disclosures.

facts.label: Signup route
facts.value: Connect Wix Payments from the site's Accept Payments dashboard; the account is subject to review and Wix says it is not yet available to all users.

facts.label: Minimum business size
facts.value: No public revenue, order-volume, or company-size minimum was found in the signup, fees, terms, or country pages checked.

facts.label: Supported sales
facts.value: Wix Payments processes payments for a seller's own products or services; Wix's platform supports store items, services, bookings, plans, and digital products subject to payment-policy review.

facts.label: Third-party collection
facts.value: The account is for the seller's own business, not for collecting or holding funds for another seller.

facts.label: Prohibited activity
facts.value: Prohibited items include specified adult products/services, illegal activity, and categories disallowed by Wix, networks, or the regional processor.

facts.label: Prohibited-page consequence
facts.value: Wix may hide or remove products, suspend or close the account, withhold funds, or refund customers when a seller violates restrictions.

facts.label: Buyer-country scope
facts.value: Wix does not publish one universal buyer-country allowlist for all sellers and methods; foreign buyer acceptance depends on card/method, country, currency, and sanctions rules.

facts.label: Brazil card restriction
facts.value: Wix Payments Brazil currently accepts only credit cards issued in Brazil; Pix and boleto have their own domestic flows.

facts.label: Reserve policy
facts.value: Wix may set rolling or one-time reserves, withhold settlement, or require the seller to add funds to cover expected refunds, disputes, complaints, or risk.

facts.label: Standard reserve amount
facts.value: No universal reserve percentage or duration is published for all Wix Payments accounts.

facts.label: Verification estimate
facts.value: Wix says verification may take up to 7 business days after requested details/documents are provided.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Integrated payment gateway and payment-management layer; it connects Wix sites to processors and method providers.

facts.label: Merchant of record
facts.value: The seller is the merchant of record and is responsible for its transactions, customers, products, and liabilities.

facts.label: Seller role and fulfillment
facts.value: The seller remains responsible for customer service, transaction legitimacy, product delivery, product quality, and required licences.

facts.label: Main charge currency
facts.value: Account/site main currency follows the Wix Payments market: USD, CAD, GBP, CHF, EUR, or BRL as listed for seller country.

facts.label: Multi-currency checkout
facts.value: Eligible Wix Payments sites can show and charge in additional buyer currencies; supported currency depends on payment method and market.

facts.label: Card networks
facts.value: Major supported card brands include Visa, Mastercard, Discover, American Express, Diners, China UnionPay, JCB, and Maestro, subject to country and processor availability.

facts.label: Digital wallets
facts.value: Apple Pay and Google Pay are available in eligible countries and currencies, with fees generally following the relevant card rate except where the schedule specifies otherwise.

facts.label: US wallet/PayPal options
facts.value: Selected US users can connect PayPal inside Wix Payments, including PayPal wallet, Venmo, Pay Later, and recurring payments.

facts.label: EU local methods
facts.value: Wix Payments lists iDEAL and Bancontact; Klarna is available in selected countries.

facts.label: UK local methods
facts.value: Clearpay and Klarna are listed for the UK; cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay are also available.

facts.label: Switzerland local methods
facts.value: Wix's fee page lists TWINT, iDEAL, Klarna, cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay for Switzerland.

facts.label: Brazil methods
facts.value: Wix Payments Brazil supports Brazilian-issued credit cards, Pix, and boleto.

facts.label: Giropay retirement
facts.value: Giropay is no longer supported by Wix Payments; Wix says sellers can connect Mollie separately if they still need Giropay.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: Wix Payments supports one-time card, wallet, and eligible local-method payments for Wix orders and pay links.

facts.label: Recurring payments
facts.value: Wix Payments supports recurring charges through eligible Wix apps and plans, but recurring Wix Payments card collection is the standard supported route.

facts.label: Recurring method limits
facts.value: Wix Payments recurring payments are limited to credit/debit cards; Brazil recurring charges are credit card only and cannot use installment payments.

facts.label: PayPal recurring
facts.value: PayPal with Wix Payments supports recurring payments for select US users.

facts.label: Billing feature owner
facts.value: Wix apps manage subscriptions, plans, booking/service renewals, or recurring invoices; Wix Payments supplies the supported charge method.

facts.label: Failed-payment recovery
facts.value: Wix provides payment-status handling and reminder/renewal flows through associated Wix business apps; a universal Wix Payments dunning policy and fee were not found.

facts.label: Plan, trial, or usage billing
facts.value: These subscription rules are managed by Wix apps and plan settings, not defined as a universal Wix Payments feature.

facts.label: Wix checkout
facts.value: Checkout is integrated into Wix Stores, Bookings, Events, and other supported Wix business apps.

facts.label: Pay links
facts.value: Wix Pay Links creates shareable payment URLs for a custom amount or catalog item, with email, QR, embed, and social sharing options.

facts.label: Pay-link controls
facts.value: Sellers can set an expiration date, limit payment count, mark an order shippable, and deactivate or duplicate links.

facts.label: Developer APIs and event notifications
facts.value: Wix publishes Payments APIs and payment event notifications for transactions, refunds, and related account activity.

facts.label: Transactions API change
facts.value: Wix's developer changelog says Transactions API methods and transaction-created/updated events were deprecated on 2026-09-30; newer Payments APIs are documented.

facts.label: Test and integration route
facts.value: Wix accepts payments through its integrated dashboard and supports official third-party provider connections; the public pages checked did not establish a general Wix Payments sandbox available to all merchants.

facts.label: Sales tax responsibility
facts.value: The merchant alone determines applicable taxes and is responsible for assessing, collecting, reporting, and remitting them.

facts.label: Tax-service coverage
facts.value: Wix Payments does not publish a universal tax calculation, registration, filing, or remittance service as part of payment processing.

facts.label: Buyer receipt
facts.value: Wix can issue receipts for paid orders and pay links; receipts can be downloaded, printed, emailed, or set to automatic delivery.

facts.label: Invoices and tax IDs
facts.value: Wix Invoices can request payment and record a sale, but whether a tax invoice or tax-ID field is appropriate depends on the seller's country and tax obligations.

facts.label: Payout method
facts.value: Standard Wix Payments payouts go to an approved bank account owned by the seller/business.

facts.label: Payout currency
facts.value: Normal Wix Payments payout is in the site's main currency; country-linked account currencies are USD, CAD, GBP, CHF, EUR, or BRL.

facts.label: Brazil currency requirement
facts.value: Wix Payments Brazil requires the Wix account/site currency to be BRL.

facts.label: General payout schedule
facts.value: Verified sellers can choose daily, weekly, or monthly payouts. Weekly defaults to Monday; monthly defaults to the first, with editable schedule days.

facts.label: General processing and first-payout timing
facts.value: Payments typically settle and clear a 2–5 business-day pending period; first funds are available for payout on average about 7 days after the first payment.

facts.label: Bank arrival
facts.value: After a payout is sent, bank arrival usually takes 3–5 business days.

facts.label: Brazil cards, Pix, boleto
facts.value: Brazil card funds are generally available 30 days after purchase unless accelerated; Pix is available in Wix balance in real time; paid boleto funds become available within 3 business days after confirmation.

facts.label: Brazil bank transfer day
facts.value: Available Brazil balance is transferred automatically on the next business Monday; a bank holiday shifts it to the following Monday.

facts.label: Digital products and access delivery
facts.value: Wix Stores can sell digital products and related Wix apps can manage video, memberships, and plans; Wix Payments handles eligible charges, while the Wix product/app supplies delivery or access.

facts.label: Download or licence delivery included in payment service
facts.value: Wix Payments alone does not publish a separate file-hosting or software-license fulfilment service.

facts.label: Marketplace and split payments
facts.value: Wix Payments is for the seller's own business and terms prohibit using it for the benefit of a third party; a standard self-serve marketplace split-payout feature was not found.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable to Wix Payments itself; crypto payment gateways may be connected separately through Wix where available.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable to Wix Payments itself; custody depends on the separately connected crypto provider.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout
facts.value: Not applicable to Wix Payments itself; crypto conversion and payout are set by any separate third-party provider.

facts.label: Crypto completion and refund
facts.value: Not applicable to Wix Payments itself; a third-party crypto provider sets confirmation and refund rules.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable to Wix Payments itself; merchants do not self-host Wix Payments processing software.

facts.label: Transaction exports
facts.value: Wix provides downloadable CSV payment and settlement reports, with transaction, payout, fee, and status details.

facts.label: Customer/payment-data portability
facts.value: A general route to export stored payment credentials or move subscription tokens to another processor was not found in reports, terms, or migration pages checked.

facts.label: Closing the payment account
facts.value: A seller can stop Wix Payments by closing its User Payment Account or disconnecting the service; Wix may also suspend or terminate access with notice.

facts.label: Funds and records after closure
facts.value: Wix may hold remaining funds until dispute risk or other liabilities are cleared and may delete transaction information; the account-closure help says remaining credit may be refunded to cardholders.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: Wix Payments is Wix's integrated payments service for transactions on Wix websites and through Wix commerce features.

facts.label: Owner and old name
facts.value: Wix Payments is a Wix.com Ltd. service; its terms also apply to Wix affiliates and regional processors. No former product name was found.

facts.label: Operating status
facts.value: Product, help, signup, current fee, and status pages are live; the Wix status page showed Wix Payments operational when checked.

facts.label: Recent changes and feature retirement
facts.value: Wix announced Stripe-powered local payment methods for 11 European markets on 2025-12-16. Giropay is no longer supported through Wix Payments.

facts.label: Support channels and availability
facts.value: Wix Customer Care provides chat, callback, or email options depending on issue, language, and region; Wix describes dedicated 24-hour support for Wix Payments.

facts.label: Payment status support
facts.value: Account owners can review payment, refund, chargeback, and payout status in the Wix dashboard; disconnected accounts retain dashboard access.

facts.label: Recent payments API retirement
facts.value: On 2026-09-30 Wix deprecated several Payments Transactions API methods and related transaction-created/updated events.

facts.label: Product news and country expansion
facts.value: Wix announced Stripe local payment methods across 11 Europe/UK markets on 2025-12-16 and said further EMEA/APAC expansion was planned.

facts.label: Pricing and change notices
facts.value: Current fee schedule exposes region selections; terms last revised 2026-05-06 and allow fee/feature changes, with notice for additional service fees where applicable.

facts.label: Public fee-change notice search
facts.value: Wix's newsroom, product updates, developer changelog, and current fee schedule were checked; no dated general Wix Payments processing-fee change notice was found.

facts.label: Full service closure/acquisition notice
facts.value: Wix newsroom, product, status, and help pages checked showed no Wix Payments shutdown or acquisition notice; product is active.

facts.label: Contracting and processor entities
facts.value: Wix Payments terms identify Wix.com Ltd. and affiliates; current terms pages list Adyen and Stripe as regional processors, PayPal US as a method/processor, and Pagarme for Brazil.

facts.label: Security and compliance statement
facts.value: Wix states it is PCI DSS Level 1 as a service provider and merchant, with yearly external assessment; its security page also lists ISO certifications.

apps.name: WooPayments
apps.line: Card, wallet, local, and payment-link checkout for WooCommerce.

free.text: No setup or monthly processing fee; requires WooCommerce

cells.countries: US, UK, Germany, and many other countries
cells.payout: US 2 days; new accounts wait 7 days plus pending time

fee.math: The rate for online payments made with cards from the US.
The rate for online payments made with cards from the UK.
The rate for online payments made with cards from Germany and other listed euro-area countries.
India isn't one of the 38 published seller countries.

apps.news: News check 2026-11-09: no sale, shutdown, rebrand, or incident found.

facts.label: Required commerce platform
facts.value: A working WooCommerce store is required; WooPayments is not a stand-alone checkout processor outside WooCommerce.

facts.label: WooPayments plugin cost
facts.value: The WooPayments plugin is free to install and has no setup charge or monthly online-processing subscription.

facts.label: Required account connection
facts.value: A WordPress.com account must be connected; signup creates a Stripe Express account for payment and verification details.

facts.label: Fixed payment-service costs
facts.value: Public pricing says there is no setup fee or monthly fee for online payment processing; fees are deducted per payment.

facts.label: WooCommerce infrastructure cost
facts.value: The WooCommerce core software is free and open source; optional paid extensions are separate products.

facts.label: US and Puerto Rico international cards
facts.value: Add 1.50% when a card is issued outside the account country; cards issued in Puerto Rico trigger the US international fee.

facts.label: Canada international cards
facts.value: Canada adds 1.00% for an international card.

facts.label: Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, and Singapore international cards
facts.value: Australia and New Zealand add 1.50%; Hong Kong and Singapore add 1.50%.

facts.label: Europe and UK international cards
facts.value: European-market card fee is +2.00% for cards issued outside Europe; UK rate is +2.00% for international cards.

facts.label: Japan, Switzerland, and UAE international cards
facts.value: Japan, Switzerland, and UAE list a +2.00% international payment fee.

facts.label: Currency conversion add-on
facts.value: The published card conversion add-on is +1.00% for US accounts and +2.00% for other listed markets.

facts.label: When conversion can be avoided
facts.value: Adding an eligible payout bank account in the payment currency can avoid conversion of that payment into the default currency.

facts.label: Fee calculation basis
facts.value: If payment currency matches a saved payout currency, fees are charged in that currency; otherwise the payment is converted to the default currency before fees are deducted.

facts.label: US BNPL fees
facts.value: US Affirm and Afterpay are 6.00% + USD 0.30; Klarna is 5.99% + USD 0.30.

facts.label: Canadian BNPL fees
facts.value: Canada Affirm and Afterpay are each 6.00% + CAD 0.30.

facts.label: Australia and New Zealand BNPL
facts.value: Afterpay is 6.00% + AUD 0.30 in Australia and 6.00% + NZD 0.30 in New Zealand.

facts.label: United Kingdom BNPL
facts.value: Clearpay is 6.00% + GBP 0.30; Klarna is 4.99% + GBP 0.35.

facts.label: Klarna in euro markets
facts.value: Klarna is offered in selected European countries; its rate differs by country, including EUR 2.99% + EUR 0.35 in Germany and EUR 4.99% + EUR 0.40 in France and Spain.

facts.label: Euro local payment rates
facts.value: For EUR accounts, the posted common rates include Bancontact 1.40% + EUR 0.25, EPS 1.80% + EUR 0.25, iDEAL / Wero EUR 0.29, and SEPA EUR 0.35.

facts.label: Subscription and B2B BNPL limits
facts.value: BNPL cannot be used for B2B transactions or subscription products; buyer country and checkout currency are generally constrained to the seller account's country and national currency.

facts.label: Stripe Billing surcharge
facts.value: US orders using the Stripe Billing engine incur an additional 1.00% on the whole order, including initial or renewal payments.

facts.label: Other recurring surcharge
facts.value: No general recurring-payment surcharge is listed for the standard on-site card renewal flow in the public fee schedule checked.

facts.label: Other transaction add-ons
facts.value: Amazon Pay has payment-source-dependent fees; most express methods use card rates, while Link has a stated international-fee exception.

facts.label: Payment surcharge rules
facts.value: A general WooPayments fee pass-through to buyers is not included as a fixed add-on; local law and card-network rules govern surcharging.

facts.label: Refund processing
facts.value: Full and partial refunds can be issued in WooCommerce Orders or from transaction details; supported card refunds are submitted immediately.

facts.label: Refund fee and buyer timing
facts.value: WooPayments does not return the original transaction fee when a merchant refunds; buyers commonly wait 5–10 business days for the credit.

facts.label: Dispute and chargeback process
facts.value: Dispute amount and fee are debited when a dispute arrives; the card issuer decides the outcome; merchants may accept or submit evidence.

facts.label: Dispute fee by market
facts.value: Posted card dispute fees include USD 15, CAD 20, AUD/NZD 25, EUR/GBP 15, HKD 85, JPY 1,500, SGD 15, CHF 15, AED 60, CZK 550, HUF 7,000, DKK/NOK 200, PLN 65, RON 100, and SEK 200.

facts.label: Dispute fee refund on win
facts.value: If the merchant challenges a dispute and wins, the disputed amount and dispute fee are credited back.

facts.label: Standard payout fee
facts.value: A separate standard bank payout fee was not listed in the payout and country-fee pages checked.

facts.label: Instant payout fee
facts.value: Eligible US sellers can request instant payout for a 1.50% fee; this option is not generally available outside the US.

facts.label: Minimum payout balance
facts.value: Minimums: AED 2, CHF 5, CZK 30, DKK 20, EUR 1, GBP 1, HUF 360, JPY 1, NOK 20, PLN 5, RON 5, SEK 20, SGD 1; currencies not listed have no minimum.

facts.label: Payout maximum
facts.value: Bank payouts have no published maximum; a US debit-card payout is capped at USD 9,999 per transfer.

facts.label: Charge minimums
facts.value: Minimum charge amount depends on payout currency, from AED 2.00, USD 0.50, EUR 0.50, and GBP 0.30 to other listed local thresholds.

facts.label: Charge maximum
facts.value: Published general maximum is 999,999.99 in the transaction currency, except IDR has a higher stated limit; some local methods have separate maximums.

facts.label: Supported seller countries
facts.value: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, and United States.

facts.label: Territory exclusions
facts.value: French territories outside the EEA, Dutch constituent countries such as Aruba and Curaçao, UK Crown Dependencies and overseas territories, and US territories other than Puerto Rico are excluded.

facts.label: Individuals and sole traders
facts.value: Individuals and businesses can sign up in listed countries, subject to local account-type rules; UAE accounts cannot use the individual type.

facts.label: Company and business accounts
facts.value: Company accounts are supported where Stripe account types and local rules allow; onboarding requests business category and registration information.

facts.label: Business-country selection
facts.value: For a business, select the country where the business is registered, not the owner's residence; the chosen country cannot be changed later through signup.

facts.label: Local bank and bank ownership
facts.value: A bank account is required for payouts in all supported markets; Stripe verifies that the payout account is linked to the account holder or business.

facts.label: KYC and business review
facts.value: Stripe verifies personal and business details before live processing; it may request additional information later.

facts.label: Requested verification information
facts.value: Signup can request legal name, date of birth, home/business address, bank details, business type, phone, tax number, and owner details.

facts.label: Site readiness
facts.value: The store must be accessible over HTTPS and describe the business and products; incomplete sites can delay review of some local methods.

facts.label: Signup and account creation
facts.value: Install and activate WooPayments, connect a WordPress.com account, choose live or test payments, and complete Stripe verification.

facts.label: Published minimum size or turnover
facts.value: No universal revenue, order-volume, or business-size minimum was published in the pricing, signup, country, or policy pages checked.

facts.label: Supported seller products
facts.value: WooPayments processes eligible payments for products and services sold through the merchant's WooCommerce store.

facts.label: Third-party collections and marketplaces
facts.value: WooPayments is set up for the connected merchant's store; no general split-payment or marketplace payout product is documented in the self-serve gateway offer.

facts.label: Restricted and prohibited business types
facts.value: WooPayments restricts or prohibits some businesses and products under Stripe, network, and local-method rules.

facts.label: Effect of policy breach or risk review
facts.value: WooPayments or Stripe may restrict payments or payouts, request more information, apply a reserve, or close an account.

facts.label: Buyer-country coverage
facts.value: Merchants may accept payments from customers worldwide, subject to payment-method, currency, card, sanctions, and legal restrictions.

facts.label: International card availability
facts.value: Visa and Mastercard are listed for customers in any country; some other card brands and local methods have market-specific exclusions.

facts.label: Reserve and payout holds
facts.value: Stripe can apply fixed or rolling reserves or transfer part of an account balance based on risk; held funds are intended to cover future refunds/disputes and may later be released.

facts.label: Approval time estimate
facts.value: A general guaranteed approval timeline was not published in the signup and KYC pages checked.

facts.label: Provider type
facts.value: Online payment gateway integrated into WooCommerce, with payment controls in the WordPress admin dashboard.

facts.label: Merchant of record and seller role
facts.value: The store merchant sells to the buyer; WooPayments processes payment and does not take over the seller's product-sale obligations.

facts.label: Processing partner relationship
facts.value: Stripe verifies the seller and creates a connected Stripe Express account; the seller uses WooPayments inside WordPress rather than the standard Stripe dashboard.

facts.label: Supported payment currencies
facts.value: WooPayments lists more than 100 presentment currencies; exact currency availability depends on card brand and method.

facts.label: Multi-currency customer checkout
facts.value: WooPayments Multi-Currency can show prices in a selected or automatically localized buyer currency; payout currency may differ.

facts.label: Card networks
facts.value: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover/Diners, China UnionPay, JCB, Cartes Bancaires, and Australian eftpos are supported with stated market restrictions.

facts.label: Express checkout wallets
facts.value: Built-in express methods include Amazon Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link by Stripe, and WooPay.

facts.label: Buy now, pay later
facts.value: Affirm, Afterpay/Cash App Afterpay/Clearpay, and Klarna are available in eligible markets.

facts.label: Local payment methods
facts.value: Available options include Alipay, Bancontact, EPS, GrabPay, iDEAL / Wero, Multibanco, SEPA Direct Debit, WeChat Pay, and legacy P24.

facts.label: Separate WooCommerce gateways
facts.value: WooPayments is optional; WooCommerce can also use separate gateways such as the Woo Stripe extension, PayPal, Square, Braintree, and others.

facts.label: One-time payments
facts.value: WooPayments supports one-time store checkout payments using cards and eligible express or local methods.

facts.label: Subscription compatibility
facts.value: Automatic renewals work with the paid WooCommerce Subscriptions extension for cards and supported express checkout methods.

facts.label: Retired native subscriptions
facts.value: The built-in WooPayments subscriptions feature was removed before version 10.2.0; merchants now need WooCommerce Subscriptions for recurring billing.

facts.label: Stripe Billing renewal option
facts.value: US merchants using WooCommerce Subscriptions can enable Stripe Billing as an off-site billing engine; the fee schedule adds 1% on affected orders.

facts.label: Failed recurring payment handling
facts.value: Subscription retry behavior is controlled by the WooCommerce Subscriptions setup and selected billing engine; a universal included WooPayments dunning schedule is not stated.

facts.label: Plans, trials, and usage billing
facts.value: Subscription plans and trial/renewal rules are provided through WooCommerce Subscriptions or other store extensions, not a standalone WooPayments billing plan.

facts.label: Checkout and payment links
facts.value: WooPayments is embedded in WooCommerce checkout; WooCommerce can send links to pay pending orders, and its mobile app can share order-payment links and QR codes.

facts.label: Developer integration
facts.value: WooPayments is a WordPress extension with documented payment settings, supported WooCommerce checkout flows, and REST endpoints.

facts.label: Sandbox and test mode
facts.value: Test accounts or test mode simulate payments, refunds, and disputes without charging real buyers; Singapore and UAE are excluded from the no-detail test-account route.

facts.label: Current security maintenance
facts.value: WordPress.org published plugin releases through 11.2.0; WooCommerce's Nov. 3, 2026 advisory instructs updating to 11.2.1 or a fixed branch build.

facts.label: Sales tax on customer orders
facts.value: WooPayments does not calculate or collect buyer sales tax as part of payment processing; the merchant configures tax through WooCommerce or a separate tax tool and is responsible for filing/remitting.

facts.label: Tax on processing fees
facts.value: VAT, GST, or consumption tax may be added to WooPayments fees according to the account country; registered sellers may qualify for reverse-charge or zero-rate treatment where stated.

facts.label: Fee tax invoices
facts.value: Eligible country merchants can access monthly fee invoices, including VAT/GST/CT and transaction-currency totals; prior-month invoices are generated on the 10th.

facts.label: Customer invoice and receipt
facts.value: WooCommerce creates order records and emails; the tax invoice/receipt format and mandatory fields are configured by the store or extensions, not a universal WooPayments invoice service.

facts.label: Payout methods
facts.value: Payouts go to a bank account in all supported seller countries; US accounts may also use a debit card.

facts.label: Payout schedule choices
facts.value: Daily is the default for most accounts; eligible accounts can choose weekly or monthly.

facts.label: Payout currencies
facts.value: Payout currency follows the merchant's account/bank setup; eligible merchants can add additional currency bank accounts.

facts.label: Currency conversion at payout
facts.value: Funds are converted to the available payout currency if there is no matching payout bank account currency, subject to the conversion fee.

facts.label: Pending period by seller country
facts.value: Standard pending time: Australia and US 2 business days; Japan and New Zealand 4 business days; UAE 5 business days; Hong Kong and Singapore 7 calendar days; all other countries 3 business days.

facts.label: First payout wait
facts.value: Every new account has a one-time 7-day wait starting after its first successful payment, then the standard pending period and payout schedule apply.

facts.label: Payout cutoff and non-business days
facts.value: Most accounts use a 00:00 UTC daily cutoff; Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand, and Singapore use local midnight; weekends and local holidays start pending time on the next business day.

facts.label: Schedule and bank arrival
facts.value: Funds can be paid daily, weekly, or monthly after pending time; actual bank availability may take extra days and is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Digital product delivery
facts.value: WooPayments charges for eligible WooCommerce orders; file delivery, access grants, and licence management are WooCommerce or extension functions.

facts.label: Marketplace split payments
facts.value: A self-serve marketplace split-payout feature was not found in the WooPayments gateway docs, product listing, or policies.

facts.label: Crypto assets and networks
facts.value: Not applicable: WooPayments is a fiat payment gateway and does not list cryptocurrency assets or blockchain networks as supported payment methods.

facts.label: Crypto custody
facts.value: Not applicable: WooPayments does not offer a merchant crypto wallet or custody service.

facts.label: Crypto conversion and payout
facts.value: Not applicable: WooPayments settles supported payment methods to bank accounts or eligible US debit cards, not crypto wallets.

facts.label: Crypto completion and refunds
facts.value: Not applicable: WooPayments does not publish crypto confirmations or on-chain refund handling.

facts.label: Crypto hosting and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: WooPayments is a hosted processing service integrated through a WooCommerce extension, not merchant-operated crypto software.

facts.label: Transaction export
facts.value: Merchants can filter and export WooPayments transactions to CSV from Payments > Transactions; reports include payout, fee, and balance activity.

facts.label: Migration and token portability
facts.value: Store/site migration is supported with documented account-transfer steps, but a universal card-token export to a different payment processor was not found.

facts.label: Account closure and access after stopping
facts.value: Disabling WooPayments does not delete the account; the plugin should be kept at least six months after the final transaction to retain access to refunds, disputes, and transaction records.

facts.label: Remaining funds and records
facts.value: WooPayments states account records may need to be retained for tax and compliance; account-specific reserve or final payout timing is not a universal published number.

facts.label: Current name and product
facts.value: WooPayments is Woo's integrated payments service for WooCommerce stores.

facts.label: Owner and operating project
facts.value: WooPayments is offered by Woo, the WooCommerce business within Automattic; processing is built in partnership with Stripe.

facts.label: Operating status
facts.value: Product, documentation, signup guide, public pricing, and WordPress plugin listing were live; the plugin listing reported 800,000+ active installations.

facts.label: Current version and release history
facts.value: WordPress.org listed version 11.2.0, released 2026-10-08; its changelog records Onelink support in Great Britain and other fixes.

facts.label: Recent method changes
facts.value: P24 is no longer available for new activations from 2026-08-17; iDEAL was renamed iDEAL / Wero on 2026-03-31.

facts.label: Country expansion notice
facts.value: Seven countries were added for in-person card-present acceptance in May 2026; no online seller-country expansion was identified in that announcement.

facts.label: Support availability
facts.value: WooCommerce support assists with setup and payment operations; the Stripe partnership page says WooCommerce support is the first contact and may refer processing cases to Stripe.

facts.label: Recent feature and fee changes
facts.value: Current fee page remains pay-as-you-go; checked 2026 product update archive for online country and fee changes, and did not find a new online seller market in the in-person expansion notice.

facts.label: Retired and renamed methods
facts.value: P24 new activation ended 2026-08-17; iDEAL became iDEAL / Wero in March 2026; standalone native subscriptions were removed before plugin version 10.2.0.

facts.label: Changelog support update
facts.value: Plugin 11.2.0 added Onelink in Great Britain; WooPayments and the Stripe extension have separate release histories.

facts.label: Contract and processor
facts.value: Signup accepts Stripe's Connected Account Agreement; WooPayments is a Woo product built with Stripe's processing services.

facts.label: PCI and data security
facts.value: WooPayments states it is a PCI DSS Level 1 service provider; hosted card fields keep card number and CVC out of the store database.

facts.label: Product-specific licence
facts.value: A single WooPayments financial-services licence covering every supported country was not published in the product pages, terms/policies, or Stripe agreement reviewed.

facts.value: Terms say funds may be held with a nominated bank or intermediary in Ziina's name and reflected in the user's Ziina Wallet.

facts.value: Fees page lists cash-outs as free in its current column and 1 AED in a future column effective November 1, 2026; a September 24 help article says cash-outs are free.

facts.value: Professional accounts have lower monthly limits; verified Business accounts can receive up to AED 2,000,000/month and are offered up to AED 90,000 per transaction.

facts.value: International cards add 1.5 percentage points per transaction to the 2.6% + AED 1 Business rate.

facts.label: International surcharge definition
facts.value: The 1.5% extra also applies to a transaction in a non-AED currency; public fee help says international card or non-AED currency, not that both 1.5% charges stack.

facts.label: Non-AED conversion markup
facts.value: When seller requests a non-AED payment amount, Ziina's help says the exchange rate used to settle in AED includes a 1.2% FX markup over market rate.

facts.label: FX and processing fees
facts.value: Non-AED payment requests also trigger the published 1.5% processing surcharge; public pages do not clarify whether the 1.2% conversion markup and 1.5% surcharge are stacked on one transaction or how the markup is itemized.

facts.label: FX rate basis
facts.value: Ziina says the exchange rate is based on rates obtained from third-party providers; the exact time and named reference rate for merchant multi-currency payments are not consistently specified.

facts.label: Ziina Balance payments
facts.value: Business receiving payments via Ziina Balance are charged the same published 2.6% + AED 1 per transaction.

facts.label: Pay by Bank cost
facts.value: A separate transaction fee for the 2026 Pay by Bank offer is not published in About, the business fee article or checkout pages reviewed.

facts.label: Invoice surcharge

facts.label: VAT collection feature
facts.value: Invoices and payment links can include a merchant-entered VAT amount; the merchant remains responsible for deciding and remitting its taxes.

facts.label: Tax/fraud add-on costs
facts.value: No separate seller price for automatic tax calculations, tax filings or a fraud-protection add-on was found in the fee, product or terms pages reviewed.

facts.label: Dispute fee amount
